title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
嘉靖己酉秋八月時當鄉試
河南有司舉如
制巡按監察御史張〔英〕寔惟監臨
廼預檄所司徵禮儒官之賢
者以柄試事及期畢至爰循
舊典以〔銓〕暨教諭林〔烋〕爲考
===
試官教諭羅〔見麟〕鄭〔喬〕周〔儒〕
黃〔岵〕葛〔永泰〕劉〔岸〕毛〔凰〕爲同
考試官布政司左布政使王
〔汝孝〕左叅政馮〔岳〕司提調按
察司按察使陳〔燿〕僉事王〔言〕
司監試其餘百執事咸慎選
以充諏日入院齋瀹洗心執
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

嘉靖己酉秋八月，時當鄉試，河南有司舉如制。巡按監察御史張〔英〕寔惟監臨，廼預檄所司，徵禮儒官之賢者，以柄試事。及期畢至，爰循舊典，以〔銓〕暨教諭林〔烋〕爲考試官，教諭羅〔見麟〕、鄭〔喬〕、周〔儒〕、黃〔岵〕、葛〔永泰〕、劉〔岸〕、毛〔凰〕爲同考試官。布政司左布政使王〔汝孝〕、左叅政馮〔岳〕司提調，按察司按察使陳〔燿〕、僉事王〔言〕司監試。其餘百執事咸慎選以充，諏日入院，齋瀹洗心，執
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the jiyou year of the Jiajing reign [1549], the time came for the Provincial Examination, and the responsible officials in Henan conducted it according to the prescribed regulations. The Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Zhang Ying 張英, served as Supervising Official. He therefore sent advance instructions to the responsible offices to summon, with due courtesy, worthy Confucian educational officials to direct the examination. All arrived at the appointed time. Following established precedent, Quan 銓 [the author] and Instructor Lin Xiu 林烋 were appointed Examiners; Instructors Luo Jianlin 羅見麟, Zheng Qiao 鄭喬, Zhou Ru 周儒, Huang Hu 黃岵, Ge Yongtai 葛永泰, Liu An 劉岸, and Mao Huang 毛凰 were appointed Associate Examiners. Wang Ruxiao 王汝孝, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Feng Yue 馮岳, Left Vice Administration Commissioner, of the Provincial Administration Commission, served as Proctors. Chen Yao 陳燿, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Wang Yan 王言, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, oversaw examination monitoring. All the remaining functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. On a chosen auspicious day, they entered the examination compound, purified themselves through fasting and ablution, cleansed their minds, and applied themselves…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
競將事進提學副使翁〔大立〕
所簡士二千有奇三試之拔
其儁者八十人第其名氏幷
文之可式者以
獻錄成〔銓〕當序諸首用告多士
竊惟河南古豫州之域星分
大火當天地之中迺羲昊之
===
遺址而成周之舊墟也嵩嶽
降神圖書呈瑞人文之盛載
昔可稽矣始〔銓〕應聘而來也
蓋嘗望太行瞻嵩嶽盤礴千
里曰茲生申甫之地也其靈
乎涉滎汜覩河洛川澤瀠滙
曰茲神物之鍾也其異乎比
punctuated:
競將事，進提學副使翁〔大立〕所簡士二千有奇，三試之，拔其儁者八十人，第其名氏，幷文之可式者以獻。錄成，〔銓〕當序諸首，用告多士。
竊惟河南，古豫州之域，星分大火，當天地之中，迺羲昊之遺址，而成周之舊墟也。嵩嶽降神，圖書呈瑞，人文之盛，載昔可稽矣。始〔銓〕應聘而來也，蓋嘗望太行，瞻嵩嶽，盤礴千里，曰：「茲生申甫之地也，其靈乎！」涉滎汜，覩河洛，川澤瀠滙，曰：「茲神物之鍾也，其異乎！」比
translation_en:
…diligently carrying out their duties, they admitted the more than two thousand scholars selected by Weng Dali, Vice Commissioner for Education. They examined them in three sessions and selected eighty outstanding candidates, ranking their names and submitting these together with writings worthy of serving as models. When the record was completed, it fell to me, Quan, to place a preface at its beginning, addressing the assembled scholars.
I humbly reflect that Henan occupies the territory of ancient Yuzhou. Its celestial correspondence is the Great Fire asterism, and it lies at the center of Heaven and Earth. Here are the vestiges of the ancient sovereigns Xi and Hao and the former seat of Chengzhou. Mount Song sent down divine spirits; the River Chart and the Luo Writing manifested auspicious signs. The flourishing of human culture here can be verified in the records of antiquity. When I, Quan, first came in response to the invitation, I gazed toward the Taihang Mountains and Mount Song, sprawling over a thousand li, and said: “This is the land that gave birth to Shen and Fu. How numinous it is!” Crossing the Xing and Si waters and viewing the Yellow and Luo Rivers, with their winding and converging streams and marshes, I said: “Here is where divine objects gather. How extraordinary it is!” By the time…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
入都邑采民風大小相恤耕
行崇讓曰茲中和之氣表見
于人物者也其美乎因意必
有哲人者出爲我
國家名世之瑞然欲知之無從
也旣得肆觀其文則見其學
識本原辭尚體要闡性命之
===
蘊酌今古之宜究禮樂刑政
之中悉人情物理之變言雖
人人殊要皆本聖門之奧義
歟
至治之精華罔非大受遠到之
器而誠可副哲人之想者也
豈以其山河之靈異而宣洩
punctuated: 入都邑，采民風，大小相恤，耕行崇讓，曰：「茲中和之氣表見于人物者也，其美乎！」因意必有哲人者出，爲我國家名世之瑞，然欲知之無從也。旣得肆觀其文，則見其學識本原，辭尚體要，闡性命之蘊，酌今古之宜，究禮樂刑政之中，悉人情物理之變。言雖人人殊，要皆本聖門之奧義歟，至治之精華，罔非大受遠到之器，而誠可副哲人之想者也。豈以其山河之靈異而宣洩
translation_en:
…Entering the cities and towns and observing the customs of the people, I found that high and low cared for one another and that, in farming and conduct, they prized deference [?]. I said: “Here the spirit of equilibrium and harmony manifests itself in the people. How admirable!” I therefore thought that wise men must surely emerge here, auspicious gifts to our state who would win renown in their age. Yet I had no means of knowing who they were.

Once I was able to examine their writings at length, I saw that their learning and understanding were rooted in fundamental principles and that their language valued substance and essentials. They elucidated the profundities of human nature and destiny, weighed what was appropriate in ancient and present times, investigated the proper balance in rites, music, punishments, and government, and understood the variations in human feelings and the principles of things. Though each expressed himself differently, all were grounded in the profound teachings of the sages and the finest principles of consummate government [?]. Every one was a man capable of bearing great responsibilities and attaining far-reaching accomplishments, truly fulfilling my conception of wise men. Could it be that the numinous wonders of these mountains and rivers find their expression…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
于人文者如是乎昔嘗讀詩
見人才之盛者莫如周故曰
有疏附曰有先後曰有奔奏
曰有禦侮竊以爲天之純佑
而周實若是及讀棫樸之章
則又曰周王壽考遐不作人
然後知文德化成其功不可
===
誣也恭惟我
皇上御極中興躬脩文德
敬一有箴五箴有註以續虞廷
精一之傳以闡聖門心學之
奥凡黌序俊髦罔不佩服
聖學游泳
神化矧中州密邇
punctuated:
于人文者如是乎？昔嘗讀《詩》，見人才之盛者莫如周，故曰有疏附，曰有先後，曰有奔奏，曰有禦侮。竊以爲天之純佑，而周實若是。及讀《棫樸》之章，則又曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人？」然後知文德化成，其功不可誣也。
恭惟我皇上御極中興，躬脩文德，《敬一》有箴，《五箴》有註，以續虞廷精一之傳，以闡聖門心學之奥。凡黌序俊髦，罔不佩服聖學，游泳神化，矧中州密邇
translation_en:
…thus manifested in human culture? I once read the Book of Odes and saw that no age surpassed the Zhou in its abundance of talented men. Thus it speaks of those who draw others close and give support, those who lead and follow, those who hasten on their duties, and those who ward off aggression. I privately thought that Heaven’s unstinting aid had indeed made the Zhou such as this. But when I read the ode “The Oak and the Shrubs” (Yupu), it also said: “Long-lived is the king of Zhou; does he not nurture men?” Only then did I understand that the achievement of civil virtue in transforming and perfecting people cannot be denied.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor, occupying the imperial throne and bringing about a restoration, personally cultivates civil virtue. He has provided an admonition on “Reverent Unity” (Jingyi) and annotations to the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen), thereby continuing the tradition of refinement and single-mindedness from the court of Shun and elucidating the profundities of the sages’ learning of the mind. Among the outstanding scholars in the schools, none fails to embrace and practice the imperial teachings and immerse himself in their wondrous transforming influence. How much more so in Zhongzhou, lying so close to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
畿甸沾被尤先者乎固宜思皇
多士生我
明盛如昔之所謂申與甫者出于
其間蜚英燿采遠追成周之
盛美而非特獨得於山河之
助已也雖然尤有說焉蓋敎
化者造士之本也禮義者士
===
人之坊也然士人之效用又
莫重于始進若昔大猷正敎
崇化士咸以禮義自固故其
進以正而臻迓衡用乂之休
迨後漢唐之世士緣立敎之
疎而所以自待者亦薄夫立
敎疎則士習日頽自待薄則
punctuated:
畿甸，沾被尤先者乎？固宜思皇多士，生我明盛，如昔之所謂申與甫者，出于其間，蜚英燿采，遠追成周之盛美，而非特獨得於山河之助已也。
雖然，尤有說焉。蓋敎化者，造士之本也；禮義者，士人之坊也。然士人之效用，又莫重于始進。若昔大猷，正敎崇化，士咸以禮義自固，故其進以正，而臻迓衡用乂之休。迨後漢唐之世，士緣立敎之疎，而所以自待者亦薄。夫立敎疎，則士習日頽；自待薄，則
translation_en:
…the capital region, and thus among the very first to receive these benefits? Surely, then, admirable scholars in great numbers should arise in our flourishing Ming, with men like those ancient figures Shen and Fu emerging among them. Their distinction should spread and their brilliance shine, matching across the ages the splendid achievements of the Zhou, rather than owing their success solely to the aid of mountains and rivers.
Yet there is a further point to make. Instruction and moral transformation are the foundation for cultivating scholars; ritual propriety and righteousness are their safeguards. As for scholars’ service, nothing is more consequential than their initial entry into office. In antiquity, under the great Way, teaching was set right and moral transformation exalted. Scholars all fortified themselves with ritual propriety and righteousness. Thus they entered office through upright means and attained the blessings of securing peace and bringing about good government. By the later ages of Han and Tang, however, lax provision for instruction also led scholars to expect little of themselves. When instruction is lax, scholars’ conduct deteriorates daily; when they expect little of themselves, then…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
士坊愈潰不知其于敎化義
禮何如也故曰周士貴秦士
賤豈以士有貴賤也耶顧其
始進何如耳今爾多士學古
入官誦詩達政固將爲進之
始也使其如此而言如此而
行殫其所學爲明謨爲保惠
===
以翼我
皇上中興之運則亦申甫之儔也
不然則剽竊枝葉毀失根本
得人爵以棄天爵甚至競取
名位榮身肥家而無裨于政
理則上負
朝廷掄材圖治之意下負主司
punctuated: 士坊愈潰，不知其于敎化義禮何如也。故曰：「周士貴，秦士賤。」豈以士有貴賤也耶？顧其始進何如耳。今爾多士，學古入官，誦詩達政，固將爲進之始也。使其如此而言，如此而行，殫其所學，爲明謨，爲保惠，以翼我皇上中興之運，則亦申甫之儔也。不然，則剽竊枝葉，毀失根本，得人爵以棄天爵，甚至競取名位，榮身肥家，而無裨于政理，則上負朝廷掄材圖治之意，下負主司
translation_en: …the moral restraints upon scholars crumble ever further; one wonders what regard they have for moral instruction, righteousness, and ritual propriety. Thus it is said: “The scholars of Zhou were esteemed; the scholars of Qin were despised.” Does this mean that scholars are inherently noble or base? It depends only on how they first enter official service. Now you, the assembled scholars, study antiquity to enter office and recite the Odes to understand government: these are surely to be the foundation of your entry into service. If you speak and act accordingly, devote all your learning to enlightened counsel and to protecting and benefiting the people, and thereby assist the resurgence of Our Emperor’s reign, then you too will be peers of Shen and Fu, the worthy ministers of Zhou. Otherwise, you merely plagiarize superficial details and destroy or lose the foundations, obtaining human rank while abandoning Heaven-conferred nobility. You may even vie for reputation and position, bringing glory to yourselves and wealth to your families while contributing nothing to good government. You would then fail, above, the court’s intention of selecting talent to achieve good government, and, below, the presiding examiners’…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以人事
君之忠將不淪于可賤之耻也耶
爾多士其愼諸是舉也廵撫
右副都御史彭〔黯〕保釐中土
篤興士類總理河道右僉都
御史方〔鈍〕撫治鄖陽右僉都
御史任〔瀛〕胥敕彝憲丕植人
文士習均有賴焉者也至于
===
有事鹺政則監察御史劉〔應〕
〔熊〕朱〔有孚〕有事馬政則監察
御史陶〔欽臯〕有事平獄則刑
部郎中金〔翮〕有事理賦則户
部主事洪〔公諧〕盧〔鳳儀〕有事
典禮則行人邵〔惟中〕張〔雲路〕
punctuated:
以人事君之忠，將不淪于可賤之耻也耶？爾多士其愼諸！

是舉也，廵撫右副都御史彭〔黯〕保釐中土，篤興士類；總理河道右僉都御史方〔鈍〕、撫治鄖陽右僉都御史任〔瀛〕，胥敕彝憲，丕植人文，士習均有賴焉者也。至于有事鹺政，則監察御史劉〔應〕〔熊〕、朱〔有孚〕；有事馬政，則監察御史陶〔欽臯〕；有事平獄，則刑部郎中金〔翮〕；有事理賦，則户部主事洪〔公諧〕、盧〔鳳儀〕；有事典禮，則行人邵〔惟中〕、張〔雲路〕、
translation_en:
…the loyalty shown in serving the ruler by providing him with worthy men—would you not then sink into contemptible disgrace? You scholars, take heed!

For this examination, Peng An 彭黯, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, maintained order in the central lands and earnestly fostered the scholarly community. Fang Dun 方鈍, Director-General of River Conservancy and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and Ren Ying 任瀛, Grand Coordinator of Yunyang and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, both upheld established statutes and greatly cultivated literary learning. The scholarly ethos benefited from them all.

As for those engaged in salt administration, there were Investigating Censors Liu Yingxiong 劉應熊 and Zhu Youfu 朱有孚; in horse administration, Investigating Censor Tao Qingao 陶欽臯; in the equitable adjudication of criminal cases, Jin He 金翮, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; in tax administration, Hong Gongxie 洪公諧 and Lu Fengyi 盧鳳儀, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue; and in ceremonial duties, Messengers Shao Weizhong 邵惟中 and Zhang Yunlu 張雲路…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
張〔柱〕皆祇役戾止雅意崇尚
者也若夫襄勞于外贊理惟
寅則右布政使王〔楊〕右參政
楊〔宜〕左參議翟〔鎬〕許〔天倫〕副
使陳〔儲秀〕蔣〔懷德〕唐〔耀〕僉事
沈〔民悅〕牟〔朝宗〕劉〔光文〕李〔兆〕
〔龍〕都指揮僉事李〔僑〕高〔鴻儒〕
===
以奉
表行則右參政何〔繼之〕副使王
〔橋〕以部稅行則右參議李〔文〕
〔進〕咸始事預勞於例得書
直隸太平府蕪湖縣儒學教
諭敖〔銓〕謹序
punctuated:
張〔柱〕，皆祇役戾止，雅意崇尚者也。若夫襄勞于外，贊理惟寅，則右布政使王〔楊〕、右參政楊〔宜〕、左參議翟〔鎬〕、許〔天倫〕、副使陳〔儲秀〕、蔣〔懷德〕、唐〔耀〕、僉事沈〔民悅〕、牟〔朝宗〕、劉〔光文〕、李〔兆〕〔龍〕、都指揮僉事李〔僑〕、高〔鴻儒〕。以奉表行，則右參政何〔繼之〕、副使王〔橋〕；以部稅行，則右參議李〔文〕〔進〕。咸始事預勞，於例得書。
直隸太平府蕪湖縣儒學教諭敖〔銓〕謹序。
translation_en:
… and Zhang Zhu: all arrived in reverent discharge of their duties and earnestly esteemed and promoted learning. As for those who shared the work outside and respectfully assisted its administration, they were Wang Yang, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yang Yi, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhai Gao and Xu Tianlun, Left Administration Assistant Commissioners; Chen Chuxiu, Jiang Huaide, and Tang Yao, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Shen Minyue, Mou Chaozong, Liu Guangwen, and Li Zhaolong, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Li Qiao and Gao Hongru, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. He Jizhi, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and Wang Qiao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, departed to present a memorial to the throne; Li Wenjin, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, departed to supervise the conveyance of tax revenues. All had shared in the work at its outset and, under established practice, merit being recorded here.
Preface respectfully composed by Ao Quan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuhu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試
監臨官
巡按河南監察御史張英〔彥實福建莆田縣人　辛丑進士〕
提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使王遴〔紹甫山東東平州人　丙戌進士〕
河南等處承宣布政使司左參政馮岳〔望之浙江慈谿縣人　丙戌進士〕
監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使陳燿〔德孚直隸靜海縣籍浙　江山陰縣人丙戌進士〕
河南等處提刑按察司僉事王言〔代言山東登州衛籍　招遠縣人辛丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸太平府蕪湖縣儒學教諭敖銓〔平之江西高安縣人　丙午貢士〕
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭林烋〔貞義福建閩縣人癸　卯貢士〕
同考試官
直隸淮安府沭陽縣儒學教諭羅見麟〔于時廣東番禺縣人　癸卯貢士〕
江西南安府崇義縣儒學教諭鄭喬〔于遷廣西桂林右衛籍湖　廣臨湘縣人庚子貢士〕
湖廣荊州府夷陵州遠安縣儒學教諭周儒〔醇卿雲南右衛籍直隸　桃源縣人丙午貢士〕
陝西漢中府南鄭縣儒學教諭黃坫〔元岑四川富順縣人　癸卯貢士〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子適衛冉有僕子曰庶矣哉冉有曰旣庶
矣又何加焉曰富之曰旣富矣又何加
焉曰敎之
致廣大而盡精微極高明而道中庸
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取於
人以爲善
易
===
六二直方大不習无不利
中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
可久則賢人之德可大則賢人之業易簡
而天下之理得矣天下之理得而成位
乎其中矣
有大而能謙必豫故受之以豫
書
克明俊德以親九族九族旣睦平章百姓
百姓昭明協和萬邦黎民於變時雍
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子適衛，冉有僕。子曰：「庶矣哉！」冉有曰：「旣庶矣，又何加焉？」曰：「富之。」曰：「旣富矣，又何加焉？」曰：「敎之。」

致廣大而盡精微，極高明而道中庸。

大舜有大焉：善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以爲善。

易

六二：直方大，不習无不利。

中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣；天下之理得，而成位乎其中矣。

有大而能謙必豫，故受之以豫。

書

克明俊德，以親九族。九族旣睦，平章百姓。百姓昭明，協和萬邦。黎民於變時雍。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master went to Wei, with Ran You driving his carriage. The Master said, “How numerous the people are!” Ran You asked, “Once they are numerous, what more should be done for them?” He replied, “Enrich them.” “Once they are prosperous, what more should be done for them?” He replied, “Teach them.”

Extend to the broad and great while fully exploring the subtle and minute; reach the lofty and luminous while following the way of the Mean.

The great Shun had something still greater: he joined others in doing good, set aside his own views to follow others, and gladly drew upon others to practice goodness.

Book of Changes

Six in the second place: straight, square, and great; without practice, nothing is unfavorable.

In Inner Sincerity (Zhongfu), benefit lies in steadfast correctness; thus it accords with Heaven.

What can endure is the virtue of the worthy person; what can become great is the undertaking of the worthy person. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s place in their midst.

One who possesses greatness yet can remain humble will surely find joy; therefore Humility is followed by Joy (Yu).

Book of Documents

He was able to manifest his eminent virtue and thereby bring the nine degrees of kinship into affection. Once these kinsmen were harmonious, he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans. Once the hundred clans were clearly ordered, he brought the myriad states into concord. The common people were thereby transformed and became harmonious.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
德惟一動罔不吉
我聞在昔成湯既受命時則有若伊尹格
于皇天在太甲時則有若保衡
立政任人準夫牧作三事
詩
如切如磋如琢如磨瑟兮僩兮赫兮咺兮
約軧錯衡八鸞瑲瑲服其命服朱芾斯皇
有瑲葱珩
顒顒卬卬如圭如璋令聞令望
===
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之儀式刑
文王之典日靖四方伊嘏文王既右享
之我其夙夜畏天之威于時保之
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕
冬齊高子來盟〔閔公二年〕楚屈完來盟于
師〔僖公四年〕
楚子伐鄭〔宣公十年〕
公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒□
punctuated:
德惟一，動罔不吉。
我聞在昔成湯既受命，時則有若伊尹，格于皇天；在太甲，時則有若保衡。
立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事。

詩
如切如磋，如琢如磨；瑟兮僩兮，赫兮咺兮。
約軧錯衡，八鸞瑲瑲。服其命服，朱芾斯皇，有瑲葱珩。
顒顒卬卬，如圭如璋，令聞令望。
我將我享，維羊維牛，維天其右之。儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。伊嘏文王，既右享之。我其夙夜，畏天之威，于時保之。

春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕
冬，齊高子來盟。〔閔公二年〕楚屈完來盟于師。〔僖公四年〕
楚子伐鄭。〔宣公十年〕
公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒□
translation_en:
When virtue is single-minded, no action is inauspicious.
I have heard that in former times, when Cheng Tang had received the Mandate, there was Yi Yin, whose influence reached august Heaven; in the time of Tai Jia, there was the Guardian and Preceptor, Bao Heng.
In establishing government, appoint trusted officers, judicial officers, and governors to constitute the three principal offices.

Book of Odes
As though cut and filed, as though carved and polished; solemn and dignified, illustrious and imposing.
With leather-bound wheel hubs [?] and an ornamented crossbar, the eight carriage bells jingle. He wears the robes bestowed upon him; his vermilion knee-covering is splendid, and his green jade pendants chime.
Dignified and lofty, like a gui tablet and a zhang tablet of jade; excellent in reputation and esteem.
I present my offerings: sheep and oxen. May Heaven accept them. I follow and emulate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace to the four quarters. Great King Wen has graciously accepted these offerings. Day and night I shall stand in awe of Heaven’s majesty, and thus preserve what has been bestowed.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
In winter, Gaozi of Qi came to conclude a covenant. 〔Second year of Duke Min.〕 Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant at the army’s encampment. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and the [illegible title] of Ju…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
杞伯同盟于蒲〔成公九年〕甲午晦晉侯
及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子鄭師敗績
〔成公十有六年〕
禮記
凡居民材必因天地寒暖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕重遲速
異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩
其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
處其所存禮之序也
===
大學始教皮弁祭菜示敬道也宵雅肄三
官其始也入學鼓篋孫其業也夏楚二
物收其威也未卜禘不視學游其志也
時觀而弗語存其心也幼者聽而弗問
學不躐等也此七者教之大倫也記曰
凡學官先事士先志其此之謂乎
作者之謂聖
第貳場
論
punctuated:
杞伯同盟于蒲。〔成公九年〕甲午，晦，晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績。〔成公十有六年〕

禮記

凡居民材，必因天地寒暖燥濕、廣谷大川異制。民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。

處其所存，禮之序也。

大學始教，皮弁祭菜，示敬道也；宵雅肄三，官其始也；入學鼓篋，孫其業也；夏楚二物，收其威也；未卜禘，不視學，游其志也；時觀而弗語，存其心也；幼者聽而弗問，學不躐等也。此七者，教之大倫也。記曰：「凡學，官先事，士先志。」其此之謂乎？

作者之謂聖。

第貳場

論
translation_en:
… and the Earl of Qi joined in a covenant at Pu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕 On the jiawu day, the last day of the lunar month, the Marquis of Jin fought against the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. The Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng suffered defeat. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕

Book of Rites

In settling the people according to their capacities, one must take account of differences in climate and terrain—cold and warmth, dryness and dampness, broad valleys and great rivers. The people born among these have differing customs. They differ in their dispositions toward firmness and gentleness, lightness and gravity, slowness and haste; in their blending of the five flavors; in the construction of their implements; and in what clothing suits them. Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; bring order to their government without changing what suits their circumstances.

To occupy one's proper place is the orderly arrangement of ritual.

At the beginning of instruction in the Great Learning, wearing the leather cap and offering vegetables demonstrates respect for the Way. Rehearsing the first three odes of the Lesser Odes guides students at the outset. Entering the school, sounding the drum, and opening their book boxes instills deference toward their studies. The two implements, the catalpa and thorn rods, maintain discipline. Not inspecting the school before divination for the di sacrifice allows their aspirations to develop freely. Observing them from time to time without speaking preserves their attentiveness. The younger students listen without asking questions, for learning must not skip stages. These seven are the great principles of teaching. A record says: “In all learning, officials give priority to their duties, and scholars to their aspirations.” Does this not refer to precisely this?

One who originates is called a sage.

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人法天立道
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉質樸敦厚遜讓有行者詔〔永光元年〕
擬唐以宋璟爲黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕
擬翰林學士胡廣等進五經四書大全及
性理大全表〔永樂十三年〕
判語〔五條〕
同僚代判署文案
器用布絹不如法
見任官輒自立碑
從征守禦官軍逃
僞造印信曆日等
===
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問宋儒論五經之有春秋猶法律之有斷
例信乎律例之足以擬經矣我
太祖高皇帝明先王之正法
punctuated:
聖人法天立道。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉質樸敦厚遜讓有行者詔〔永光元年〕。
擬唐以宋璟爲黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕。
擬翰林學士胡廣等進五經四書大全及性理大全表〔永樂十三年〕。

判語〔五條〕
同僚代判署文案。
器用布絹不如法。
見任官輒自立碑。
從征守禦官軍逃。
僞造印信曆日等。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：宋儒論五經之有春秋，猶法律之有斷例，信乎律例之足以擬經矣？我太祖高皇帝明先王之正法
translation_en:
The sage models himself on Heaven and establishes the Way.

Imperial edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials 〔one topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor calling for the recommendation of men who are plain and unaffected, sincere and generous, modest and yielding, and of virtuous conduct. 〔First year of Yongguang [43 BCE]〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Song Jing Vice Director of the Chancellery. 〔First year of Shenlong [705]〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of Hanlin Academician Hu Guang and his colleagues presenting the Complete Compendia of the Five Classics and Four Books and the Complete Compendium of Nature and Principle. 〔Thirteenth year of Yongle [1415]〕

Legal judgments 〔five items〕
A colleague renders judgments and signs case documents on another official’s behalf.
Utensils, cotton cloth, and silk fail to conform to statutory standards.
An incumbent official erects a commemorative stele for himself without authorization.
Officers and soldiers desert while on campaign or performing defensive duties.
Counterfeiting official seals, calendars, and the like.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔five questions〕
Question: Song Confucians argued that the place of the Spring and Autumn Annals among the Five Classics is like that of adjudicated precedents in the law. Is it indeed true that statutes and precedents can be compared to the Classics? Our Emperor Taizu Gao elucidated the correct laws of the former kings …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
製爲
大明律
大明令以昭示臣民眞
大聖人仁天下之書也其詳可得聞與
列聖相承益隆繼述又著爲問刑條例擴其所
未發增其所不備凡以濟律也五經春
秋之旨果無以異乎至於三典三居三
赦三宥五戒五禁皆古律也擬之今律
亦有相孚者與虞書所謂五刑周官所
謂五刑與後世所謂五刑可究其同異
之實與說者謂今律皆本於唐律而損
益之則其餘又皆有可法與諸士子窮
經致用其於法律斷例固嘗熟誦而詳
說之以爲致
君之術矣願攄其義
===
問先王制禮以節事脩樂以道志傳稱見
禮知政聞樂知德豈無謂哉三代而後
禮書猶有可考樂書不傳然代更世易
punctuated:
製爲《大明律》、《大明令》，以昭示臣民，眞大聖人仁天下之書也。其詳可得聞與？列聖相承，益隆繼述，又著爲《問刑條例》，擴其所未發，增其所不備，凡以濟律也。五經、春秋之旨，果無以異乎？至於三典、三居、三赦、三宥、五戒、五禁，皆古律也。擬之今律，亦有相孚者與？《虞書》所謂五刑，《周官》所謂五刑，與後世所謂五刑，可究其同異之實與？說者謂今律皆本於唐律而損益之，則其餘又皆有可法與？諸士子窮經致用，其於法律斷例，固嘗熟誦而詳說之，以爲致君之術矣。願攄其義。

問：先王制禮以節事，脩樂以道志。傳稱：「見禮知政，聞樂知德。」豈無謂哉？三代而後，禮書猶有可考，樂書不傳。然代更世易，
translation_en:
…compiled the Great Ming Code and the Great Ming Ordinances to make them clearly known to officials and commoners. These are truly books through which a great sage extends benevolence to all under Heaven. May we hear their particulars? The successive sage emperors further enhanced this inherited undertaking and also compiled the Regulations on the Adjudication of Punishments, expanding what had not been articulated and supplying what was lacking, all to supplement the Code. Is their purport indeed no different from that of the Five Classics and the Spring and Autumn Annals? As for the three penal codes, the three places of confinement [?], the three grounds for pardon, the three grounds for leniency, the five admonitions, and the five prohibitions, these are all ancient laws. When compared with the present Code, do they likewise correspond? Can you investigate the actual similarities and differences among the five punishments mentioned in the Book of Yu, those mentioned in the Offices of Zhou, and those of later ages? Commentators say that the present Code is entirely based on the Tang Code, with omissions and additions. Does this mean that everything else in the Tang Code also offers a model worth following? You candidates study the classics exhaustively in order to put them to practical use. Surely you have thoroughly recited and explained in detail the laws and judicial precedents as a means of guiding the ruler toward good government. We ask you to expound their significance.

Question: The former kings established ritual to regulate affairs and cultivated music to guide aspirations. The tradition states: “Observe the rites and you will know the government; hear the music and you will know its virtue.” Surely this was not said without reason? After the Three Dynasties, writings on ritual remained available for examination, whereas writings on music were not transmitted. Yet as dynasties succeeded one another and ages changed…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
有難以折衷焉者姑舉其一二論之叔
孫曹褒之制貞觀顯慶之儀夫孰曰非
禮而又有禮閣新儀曲臺新禮開寶通
禮禮閣新編者果孰爲得耶王禹獻二
十四卷劉向校二十三篇夫孰曰非樂
而又有嘉至永至之名休成永安之號
十二和十五和之法果孰爲優耶至於
黄初之裁定天始之削除梁之裁成隋
之述著制各不同也政亦有可取者與
===
劉宋以永爲名蕭梁以雅爲名陳以韶
爲名隋以夏爲名各有取義也德亦有
可錄者與夫致禮樂之道舉而措之天
下無難矣多士觀
昭代禮樂之盛必有達其本者也毋諉之曰未
能
問射所以觀德也古之王者以六藝設教
而尤重於射是故成周澤宮之制孔子
矍圃之觀所以序進賢能而孜見德行
punctuated:
有難以折衷焉者，姑舉其一二論之。叔孫、曹褒之制，貞觀、顯慶之儀，夫孰曰非禮？而又有《禮閣新儀》《曲臺新禮》《開寶通禮》《禮閣新編》者，果孰爲得耶？王禹獻二十四卷，劉向校二十三篇，夫孰曰非樂？而又有嘉至、永至之名，休成、永安之號，十二和、十五和之法，果孰爲優耶？至於黄初之裁定，天始之削除，梁之裁成，隋之述著，制各不同也，政亦有可取者與？劉宋以永爲名，蕭梁以雅爲名，陳以韶爲名，隋以夏爲名，各有取義也，德亦有可錄者與？夫致禮樂之道，舉而措之天下，無難矣。多士觀昭代禮樂之盛，必有達其本者也，毋諉之曰未能。

問：射所以觀德也。古之王者以六藝設教，而尤重於射。是故成周澤宮之制，孔子矍圃之觀，所以序進賢能而孜見德行。
translation_en:
…there are matters on which it is difficult to reach a balanced judgment. Let us select one or two for discussion. Who would deny that the institutions of Shusun and Cao Bao, or the ceremonies of the Zhenguan and Xianqing eras, constituted ritual? Yet there are also the New Ceremonies of the Ritual Repository (Lige xinyi), New Rites of the Curved Terrace (Qutai xinli), Comprehensive Rites of the Kaibao Era (Kaibao tongli), and New Compilation of the Ritual Repository (Lige xinbian). Which of these truly got it right? Wang Yu presented twenty-four scrolls, and Liu Xiang collated twenty-three chapters: who would deny that these concerned music? Yet there are also pieces named Jiazhi and Yongzhi, titles such as Xiucheng and Yong’an, and systems of twelve and fifteen Harmonies. Which of these was truly superior? As for the revisions and determinations of the Huangchu era, the deletions of the Tianshi era [?], the arrangements established under the Liang, and the writings compiled under the Sui, their institutions all differed. Were there also aspects of their government worth adopting?

The Liu Song used Yong in naming its music; the Xiao Liang used Ya, the Chen used Shao, and the Sui used Xia. Each choice conveyed a particular meaning. Were there also aspects of their virtue worth recording? Once one fully comprehends the Way of rites and music, putting it into practice throughout the realm presents no difficulty. You candidates, observing the flourishing rites and music of our illustrious dynasty, must include some who understand their foundations. Do not evade the matter by saying that you are not yet capable.

Question: Archery is a means of observing virtue. The kings of antiquity established instruction through the Six Arts and placed particular emphasis on archery. Thus the archery institution at the Marsh Palace of the Zhou and Confucius’s observation of archery at Juepu served to advance the worthy and capable in due order and to reveal moral conduct [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
其示人以讓道至矣然射有名物度器
之節尊卑上下之等官職有司之異何
與自是以降缺焉不講其間英明之主
有行大射于辟雍者有習射殿廷者有
演於武德殿前者有行於景福樓下者
果可以復于古與當時有志之士銳意
古道如舉古賓射於武昌而嘆其有洙
泗之風桑弧蓬矢以習射而縣令率屬
往觀之不可謂非觀德之舉也其亦有
===
裨于古道否與肆我
皇祖於開國之初命天下郡縣立學而并建射
圃於黌序以便肄習所以作興士類嘉
惠天下者至矣
皇上恪遵
成憲敦崇古制邇因撫臣建白禮官覆請
慨然俞允而申飭之薄海內外喁喁向風于
觀德之化行見禮讓行而風俗美比隆
三代之治而下陋叔季之習矣諸士由
punctuated: 其示人以讓道至矣。然射有名物度器之節、尊卑上下之等、官職有司之異，何與？自是以降，缺焉不講。其間英明之主，有行大射于辟雍者，有習射殿廷者，有演於武德殿前者，有行於景福樓下者，果可以復于古與？當時有志之士，銳意古道，如舉古賓射於武昌而嘆其有洙泗之風，桑弧蓬矢以習射而縣令率屬往觀之，不可謂非觀德之舉也。其亦有裨于古道否與？肆我皇祖於開國之初，命天下郡縣立學，而并建射圃於黌序，以便肄習，所以作興士類、嘉惠天下者至矣。皇上恪遵成憲，敦崇古制。邇因撫臣建白，禮官覆請，慨然俞允而申飭之。薄海內外，喁喁向風，于觀德之化，行見禮讓行而風俗美，比隆三代之治，而下陋叔季之習矣。諸士由
translation_en:
…Their instruction in the way of deference was consummate. Yet archery had prescribed names and objects, measures and implements; distinctions of rank between the honored and the lowly, superiors and inferiors; and differences among offices and the officials responsible. What were these? Thereafter, these practices fell into neglect and were no longer studied. Among the enlightened rulers of subsequent times, some performed the Great Archery Ceremony at the Biyong, the imperial ritual academy; some practiced archery in the palace court; some demonstrated it before Wude Hall; and some performed it below Jingfu Tower. Could these truly restore antiquity? Men of aspiration in those times devoted themselves to the ancient way. For example, ancient guest archery rites were performed at Wuchang and praised as possessing the spirit of the Zhu and Si rivers, the homeland of Confucius; archery was practiced with mulberry bows and arrows of fleabane stalks, and the district magistrate led his subordinates to observe. These certainly could be called occasions for observing virtue. But did they also contribute to the ancient way?
Thus, at the founding of the dynasty, our imperial ancestor ordered prefectures and counties throughout the realm to establish schools and also to construct archery grounds within their precincts, to facilitate practice. His efforts to encourage scholars and confer benefits upon the realm were consummate. His Majesty reverently follows the established statutes and deeply honors the ancient institutions. Recently, following a proposal by a grand coordinator and a subsequent petition by the officials of the Ministry of Rites, he readily granted approval and issued renewed injunctions. Throughout the realm and beyond, to the shores of the seas, all eagerly look toward this transforming influence of observing virtue. Soon we shall see ritual propriety and deference prevail and customs improve, matching the flourishing government of the Three Dynasties and relegating the habits of declining ages to an inferior place. You scholars who, through…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
茲選者其酌古準今言之毋該曰其義
難知也
問昔之人君嘗見均田圖慨然嘆曰此致
治之本也王者之政自此始夫均田王
政之一事爾何以爲致治之本耶今其
圖尚存推而行之果足以致治耶抑時
異世殊而猶有所未盡也試舉中州之
田而詳議之禹貢豫冀之地墳壚白壤
土不可謂不美也
===
國初得地二十九萬求樂間增而爲三十六
萬成化間復損而爲二十八萬疆域既
定孰從而增損之也豈農有勤惰地有
興廢政有得失而致之耶我
皇上視民如傷孳孳圖治每以及時耕耘勸諭
百姓天下之人皆仰窺
大聖人憂民之心無時不然中外臣工固罔敢
怠荒矣夫何務本者苦於盡力詭計者
巧於規避侵占者善於蠶食無異乎田
punctuated:
茲選者，其酌古準今言之，毋該曰其義難知也。

問：昔之人君嘗見均田圖，慨然嘆曰：「此致治之本也，王者之政自此始。」夫均田，王政之一事爾，何以爲致治之本耶？今其圖尚存，推而行之，果足以致治耶？抑時異世殊，而猶有所未盡也？試舉中州之田而詳議之。《禹貢》豫冀之地，墳壚白壤，土不可謂不美也。國初得地二十九萬，求樂間增而爲三十六萬，成化間復損而爲二十八萬。疆域既定，孰從而增損之也？豈農有勤惰，地有興廢，政有得失而致之耶？我皇上視民如傷，孳孳圖治，每以及時耕耘勸諭百姓。天下之人皆仰窺大聖人憂民之心，無時不然；中外臣工固罔敢怠荒矣。夫何務本者苦於盡力，詭計者巧於規避，侵占者善於蠶食，無異乎田
translation_en:
…Those selected through this examination should weigh ancient practice against present circumstances and explain the matter. Do not say [?] that its meaning is difficult to understand.

Question: A ruler of former times once saw a Diagram of Land Equalization and exclaimed with deep feeling: “This is the foundation of good government. The government of a true king begins here.” Now, land equalization is only one aspect of kingly government. Why should it be considered the foundation of good government? The diagram still survives today. Would putting it into practice truly suffice to bring about good government? Or have times and circumstances changed, so that it still leaves something unaddressed? Discuss this in detail, taking the land of Zhongzhou as your example. According to the Tribute of Yu, the lands of Yu and Ji have rich loam, dark hard soil, and white earth; their soil certainly cannot be called poor.

At the founding of the dynasty, the land obtained amounted to 290,000 [units unspecified]. During the “Qiule” period [?], this increased to 360,000, and during the Chenghua period it again declined to 280,000. Once the territorial boundaries were fixed, what caused these increases and decreases? Could they have resulted from differences in farmers’ diligence, the cultivation or abandonment of land, and successes or failures in government? Our Emperor cares for the people as though they were injured and works tirelessly for good government, repeatedly urging the common people to plough and weed at the proper seasons. All under Heaven look up and discern the great sage’s constant concern for the people; officials at court and in the provinces assuredly dare not neglect their duties. Why, then, do those engaged in agriculture, the fundamental occupation, suffer despite exhausting their strength, while schemers cleverly evade their obligations and encroachers excel at nibbling away at others’ holdings? Is it any wonder [?] that the fields…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
畝之不增也而有司者紛紛然議均田
以救其弊果可施於今日否與且今之
訟田土者曰一地二糧也地去糧存也
逃戶地糧也聽者咸以爲健且繁矣而
不知此乃近歲旣均之田也果何故耶
諸生抱策入比必有所以塞守臣之責
紓
九重之憂者當何施而可其詳著於篇
===
問禹之治水也行其所無事也古稱十三
年過家不入門隨山濬川任土作貢宜
萬世無弊也夫何黃河遷徙不常衝決
日甚故道之失已非一日然則禹之功
亦有所未盡與其治河之法言人人殊
或謂初平三策與至正三策治法無愈
之者其詳可得聞與邇歲大雨河溢王
家樓等處水氾濫入舊堤河之勢亦殺
矣且下流衝突曹縣幾沒而理河諸臣
方議開趙皮寨口以殺水勢苦其難者
punctuated:
畝之不增也。而有司者紛紛然議均田以救其弊，果可施於今日否與？且今之訟田土者，曰一地二糧也，地去糧存也，逃戶地糧也。聽者咸以爲健且繁矣，而不知此乃近歲旣均之田也，果何故耶？諸生抱策入比，必有所以塞守臣之責、紓九重之憂者，當何施而可？其詳著於篇。

問：禹之治水也，行其所無事也。古稱十三年過家不入門，隨山濬川，任土作貢，宜萬世無弊也。夫何黃河遷徙不常，衝決日甚，故道之失已非一日？然則禹之功亦有所未盡與？其治河之法，言人人殊。或謂初平三策與至正三策，治法無愈之者，其詳可得聞與？邇歲大雨河溢，王家樓等處水氾濫入舊堤，河之勢亦殺矣。且下流衝突，曹縣幾沒，而理河諸臣方議開趙皮寨口以殺水勢，苦其難者
translation_en:
…that the acreage does not increase. Yet the responsible officials are busily proposing the equalization of land assessments to remedy these abuses. Can this actually be implemented today? Moreover, present lawsuits over land concern such matters as two grain-tax assessments on a single plot, land that has passed out of one’s possession while its tax liability remains, and the land and grain-tax liabilities of absconded households. Those hearing these cases all regard them as contentious and numerous, yet do not realize that the land concerned has already undergone equalization in recent years. Why, indeed, is this so? You students have come with your proposals to compete in this examination. Surely you have means by which the officials charged with governing this territory may fulfill their responsibilities and relieve His Majesty’s concerns. What measures would be appropriate? Set them out in detail in your essays.

Question: In controlling the waters, Yu followed their natural course without unnecessary interference. Ancient accounts say that for thirteen years he passed his home without entering its gate, followed the mountains to dredge the rivers, and fixed tribute according to the capabilities of the soil. His work should have remained free of troubles for ten thousand generations. Why, then, does the Yellow River shift its course unpredictably, with breaches becoming daily more severe? Its departure from its former course is already of long standing. Was there, then, something left incomplete even in Yu’s achievement? Opinions differ from person to person about methods of controlling the river. Some say that no methods surpass the three proposals of the Chuping era [?] and the three proposals of the Zhizheng era. May we hear their details? In recent years, heavy rains have caused the river to overflow. At Wangjialou and other places, floodwaters entered the old embankments, and the force of the river was thereby reduced. Further downstream, however, the river surged and breached its banks, nearly submerging Cao County. The officials responsible for river management are now proposing to open an outlet at Zhaopizhai to reduce the force of the water. Those who find this difficult…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
又議開孫家渡口以邀近功果孰爲良
法與今計其勞費財與力不下十餘萬
縱使成功其水勢未必能殺而疏薄沙
鹵之土隨濬隨淤疲勞貧困之民日征
月役二議恐均有所未盡也况末流已
匯逼近
皇陵全河南徙爲漕洪深慮者耶兹欲節省而
不妨開濬之議輕減而不失保障之宜
土著者必有畫一之策矣其悉陳之當
轉聞於
上
punctuated: 又議開孫家渡口以邀近功，果孰爲良法與？今計其勞費，財與力不下十餘萬。縱使成功，其水勢未必能殺，而疏薄沙鹵之土，隨濬隨淤；疲勞貧困之民，日征月役。二議恐均有所未盡也。况末流已匯，逼近皇陵，全河南徙，爲漕洪深慮者耶？兹欲節省而不妨開濬之議，輕減而不失保障之宜，土著者必有畫一之策矣。其悉陳之，當轉聞於上。
translation_en:
…Others also propose opening the Sunjiadu outlet to secure immediate results. Which proposal would truly provide a sound method? Reckoning the toil and expenditure involved, the costs in money and labor would amount to over a hundred thousand. Even if the work succeeded, it would not necessarily diminish the force of the water. The loose, thin, sandy and saline soil would silt up as quickly as it was dredged, while the exhausted and impoverished people would face levies every day and labor service every month. Both proposals, I fear, leave matters inadequately considered. Moreover, the waters downstream have already converged and drawn close to the imperial mausoleums. Would not the southward migration of the entire river pose a grave concern for the grain-transport rapids [?]?

We now wish to economize without impeding plans for opening and dredging waterways, and to lighten burdens without compromising the necessary safeguards. Those native to the locality must surely have a coherent plan. Set it forth in full; it will duly be transmitted to His Majesty.

translation_en:
Eighty successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Lu Bangyan, an added-quota student at the Suizhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Second: Dong Xuan, a student at the Song County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Third: Li Bangqi, a student at the Ningling County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourth: Xu Yangxiang, a student at the Suizhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Fifth: Zhang Daochong, a student at the Guide Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Sixth: Wu Sanxing, an added-quota student at the Luoyang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Seventh: Zhang Zhu, a student at the Xincai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Eighth: Ma Sicu, an attached student at the Junzhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Ninth: Liu Xuan, a student at the Xiangfu County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Tenth: Gao Cai, a student at the Xinzheng County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Eleventh: Li Weiqin, a student at the Xuzhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Twelfth: Wang Yangsheng, a student at the Luoyang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Thirteenth: Li Sixuan, an attached student at the Qi County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourteenth: Li Yongbin, a student at the Junzhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Fifteenth: Liu Zhenyi, a student at the Tongxu County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

[Preceded by “jiwei,” a cyclical year designation of uncertain significance here.] Sixteenth: Niu Ruoyu, a student at the Kaifeng Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
