translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master went to Wei, with Ran You driving his carriage. The Master said, “How numerous the people are!” Ran You asked, “Once they are numerous, what more should be done for them?” He replied, “Enrich them.” “Once they are enriched, what more should be done for them?” He replied, “Teach them.”

Lu Bangyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: 〔The way emperors and kings govern amounts to just two matters: educating and nourishing the people. You have developed these through the two words “sustaining” and “perfecting,” standing conspicuously above all the other compositions. Moreover, your expression〕〔is full and fluent. You are an outstanding scholar of Zhongchuan [?]. Accept him.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Sound, correct, refined, and elegant. The discussion of enriching and teaching leaves scarcely anything unexplored and is sufficient to serve as a model for the many scholars.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔The language and reasoning are fluent and lucid. The intention of the sages and worthies to put the Way into practice for the people shines through the words. Commendable.〕

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: 〔Exceptional insight; pure and elegant expression. An outstanding scholar.〕

The sage, moved by the multitude of Wei’s people, proceeded to discuss the way to sustain and perfect them. For the highest attainment is that all things should each find their proper place. Once the people are numerous, to enrich them and then teach them is simply to benefit them to the fullest. How orderly the sequence of these measures is! Formerly, when the Master went to Wei with Ran You as his driver, the multitude of the people stirred him to express his feelings in words. For the land…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
闢民聚旣喜施澤之有地而濟時行道足慰其
利見之懷者也冉有從而請曰國以民爲依恒
患乎弗庶也旣庶而無以加之可乎子告之曰
君之於民也使司牧之勿使失所故庶而不富
非所以生之也民其如我何則爲脩六府以裕
其財焉定九賦以薄其征焉天地本有生民之
政而吾所以利導而撙節之者不過因民之所
利而利之俾羣然而生者亦熙熙然而樂焉斯可
矣可以庶而但已哉冉有又從而請曰民以食
爲天恒患乎弗富也旣富而無以加之可乎子
===
告之曰君之於民也使師保之勿使失性故富
而不敎非所以成之也我其如民何則爲脩七
敎以興其行焉敷五典以和其衷焉天地本有
成民之德而吾所以輔翼而匡直之者不過因
民之所固有者而裁之俾有是恒產者亦有是
恒心焉斯已矣可以富而自足哉夫庶而養養
而敎一荅問之間而經世之法備非聖人其孰
能之抑敎養之說昉於何時書曰政在養民敎
punctuated: 闢民聚，旣喜施澤之有地，而濟時行道足慰其利見之懷者也。冉有從而請曰：「國以民爲依，恒患乎弗庶也。旣庶而無以加之，可乎？」子告之曰：「君之於民也，使司牧之，勿使失所。故庶而不富，非所以生之也，民其如我何？則爲脩六府以裕其財焉，定九賦以薄其征焉。天地本有生民之政，而吾所以利導而撙節之者，不過因民之所利而利之，俾羣然而生者亦熙熙然而樂焉，斯可矣。可以庶而但已哉？」冉有又從而請曰：「民以食爲天，恒患乎弗富也。旣富而無以加之，可乎？」子告之曰：「君之於民也，使師保之，勿使失性。故富而不敎，非所以成之也，我其如民何？則爲脩七敎以興其行焉，敷五典以和其衷焉。天地本有成民之德，而吾所以輔翼而匡直之者，不過因民之所固有者而裁之，俾有是恒產者亦有是恒心焉，斯已矣。可以富而自足哉？」夫庶而養，養而敎，一荅問之間而經世之法備，非聖人其孰能之？抑敎養之說昉於何時？書曰：「政在養民，敎
translation_en:
…was opened up and the people gathered. He rejoiced that there was a place in which to bestow his beneficence, and that aiding his age and putting the Way into practice could satisfy his desire to appear in public service for others’ benefit.

Ran You then asked: “A state depends upon its people, and the constant concern is that they may not be numerous. Once they are numerous, can it be right to do nothing further for them?” The Master told him: “In his relationship with the people, the ruler must oversee and shepherd them, ensuring that none loses a proper place. Thus, to make them numerous without making them prosperous is no way to sustain their lives. How, then, would the people regard me? Accordingly, one should put the six resources in order to increase their wealth, and regulate the nine levies to lighten their taxation. Heaven and Earth inherently possess an ordering that sustains the people’s lives. What I do to guide this to their advantage and regulate its use amounts to no more than benefiting the people through what benefits them already. Let those who live together in multitudes also enjoy their lives in harmony and contentment: then it will be satisfactory. Can one stop merely at making them numerous?”

Ran You again asked: “The people regard food as Heaven, and the constant concern is that they may not be prosperous. Once they are prosperous, can it be right to do nothing further for them?” The Master told him: “In his relationship with the people, the ruler must teach and protect them, ensuring that they do not lose their inherent nature. Thus, to make them prosperous without educating them is no way to bring them to fulfillment. How, then, would I have dealt with the people? Accordingly, one should cultivate the seven teachings to promote their conduct, and disseminate the five constant norms to bring their inner dispositions into harmony. Heaven and Earth inherently possess the virtue that brings the people to fulfillment. What I do to assist and support them, correct and straighten them, amounts to no more than shaping what the people inherently possess. Let those who have a constant livelihood also have constant hearts: that is all. Can one be satisfied merely with making them prosperous?”

Once the people are numerous, sustain them; once sustained, educate them. Within a single exchange of questions and answers, the methods for ordering the world are fully set forth. Who but a sage could accomplish this? Yet when did this teaching concerning education and sustenance originate? The Book of Documents says: “Government lies in sustaining the people; instruction …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
敷五教堯舜以來相傳之法也夫子之世若齊
若晉若魯民非不庶而特發於衛焉蓋魯衛之
政兄弟也魯固以至道望之矣今於魯不可吾
舍衛何適哉此固夫子致嘆意也然而衛不能
用夫子且奈何哉雖然庶矣富矣教矣致治之
道萬代如見夫子未爲不遇也
致廣大而盡精微極高明而道中庸
李邦器
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔理明詞盡中庸義宜如〕
〔此作〕
考試官教諭林　批〔理性題作者多失之晦〕
〔此篇明暢典實是用錄式〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔語意峻潔發脩德凝道〕
〔之旨無遺敬服〕
===
君子脩德之功心體求復其初而事理必造于
極也蓋吾心與事理相資者也於此交致其功
則德脩矣道其有不凝乎且夫天下之道統會
於人心而散殊於事理君子脩德凝道固在存
punctuated:
敷五教，堯舜以來相傳之法也。夫子之世，若齊、若晉、若魯，民非不庶，而特發於衛焉。蓋魯衛之政，兄弟也。魯固以至道望之矣，今於魯不可，吾舍衛何適哉？此固夫子致嘆意也。然而衛不能用夫子，且奈何哉？雖然，庶矣，富矣，教矣，致治之道，萬代如見，夫子未爲不遇也。

致廣大而盡精微，極高明而道中庸。
李邦器
同考試官教諭鄭，批〔理明詞盡，中庸義宜如〕〔此作。〕
考試官教諭林，批〔理性題，作者多失之晦。〕〔此篇明暢典實，是用錄式。〕
考試官教諭敖，批〔語意峻潔，發脩德凝道〕〔之旨無遺，敬服。〕

君子脩德之功，心體求復其初，而事理必造于極也。蓋吾心與事理相資者也，於此交致其功，則德脩矣，道其有不凝乎？且夫天下之道，統會於人心，而散殊於事理。君子脩德凝道，固在存
translation_en:
…to disseminate the five teachings: this is the method handed down since Yao and Shun. In the Master's time, the populations of Qi, Jin, and Lu were certainly numerous, yet he made this observation specifically in Wei. For the governments of Lu and Wei were like brothers. He had indeed hoped that Lu would attain the highest Way. Now that nothing could be accomplished in Lu, where could he go if he abandoned Wei? This was surely what prompted the Master's sigh. Yet Wei could not employ the Master—what could be done about that? Even so, making the people numerous, enriching them, and teaching them: this way of achieving good government remains as clearly visible through ten thousand generations as though before our eyes. Thus the Master cannot be said to have found no opportunity to realize his aspirations.

“Extend breadth and greatness to the utmost while fully exploring the subtle and minute; reach the heights of clarity while following the Mean in ordinary practice.”
By Li Bangqi.

Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the wording exhaustive. An exposition of the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean should be like this composition.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “When writing on topics concerning principle and human nature, authors often fall into obscurity. This essay is clear, fluent, grounded in the classics, and substantial; it is therefore recorded as a model.”

Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: “The language and ideas are lofty and concise. It fully brings out the purport of cultivating virtue and firmly establishing the Way, leaving nothing out. I admire it respectfully.”

In the gentleman's work of cultivating virtue, he seeks to restore the original condition of the substance of his mind, while necessarily pursuing the principles of affairs to their utmost. For our mind and the principles of affairs sustain one another. If he applies his efforts fully to both, his virtue will be cultivated. How, then, could the Way fail to become firmly established? Now, the Way of all under Heaven is united in the human mind and diversely manifested in the principles of affairs. The gentleman's cultivation of virtue and firm establishment of the Way assuredly depend upon preserving…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
心致知夯然豈以一端盡乎彼吾心之體本自
廣大惟有所蔽始狹小矣要必不以私意自蔽
焉廓吾心以配天地而不見其不足也含萬物
以歸吾心而不見其有餘也則廣大致矣然心
與理相涵而物理之精微初不因廣大而或遺
也故必於禮儀威儀之散見者精義以入神通
微以作睿則析之極其精者合之盡其大心非
虛位而理有定歸矣脩德凝道其在此乎吾心
之體本自高明惟有所累始卑暗矣要必不以
===
私欲自累焉神運於天地之外而不可拘也見
超於萬物之表而不可眩也則高明極矣然心
與事相符而處事之中庸初不於高明而有外
也故必於禮儀威儀之發散者錯綜之以盡變
權度之以用中則旁行而不流者知周而不過
中有眞見而事有定執矣脩德凝道其在此乎
君子之學交相爲功如此此聖人之道必待君
子而行也雖然道有費隱無精粗有體用無內
外廣大精微非廣大尚粗而精微始精也高明
punctuated: 心致知，夯然豈以一端盡乎？彼吾心之體，本自廣大，惟有所蔽，始狹小矣。要必不以私意自蔽焉，廓吾心以配天地，而不見其不足也；含萬物以歸吾心，而不見其有餘也，則廣大致矣。然心與理相涵，而物理之精微，初不因廣大而或遺也。故必於禮儀威儀之散見者，精義以入神，通微以作睿，則析之極其精者，合之盡其大，心非虛位而理有定歸矣。脩德凝道，其在此乎？吾心之體，本自高明，惟有所累，始卑暗矣。要必不以私欲自累焉，神運於天地之外而不可拘也，見超於萬物之表而不可眩也，則高明極矣。然心與事相符，而處事之中庸，初不於高明而有外也。故必於禮儀威儀之發散者，錯綜之以盡變，權度之以用中，則旁行而不流者，知周而不過，中有眞見而事有定執矣。脩德凝道，其在此乎？君子之學，交相爲功如此，此聖人之道必待君子而行也。雖然，道有費隱，無精粗；有體用，無內外。廣大精微，非廣大尚粗而精微始精也；高明
translation_en:
…preserving the mind and extending knowledge—[the wording 夯然 is doubtful]—how could either aspect alone exhaust the task? The substance of our mind is inherently broad and great; only when obscured does it become narrow and small. Above all, we must not obscure ourselves with selfish intentions. Expand our mind to match Heaven and Earth, without finding it insufficient; encompass the myriad things and bring them into our mind, without finding them excessive: then breadth and greatness are attained. Yet mind and principle mutually contain one another, and the subtle refinements of the principles of things are never to be neglected on account of this breadth and greatness. Thus, in the various manifestations of ceremonial observances and dignified comportment, we must refine our understanding of what is right until we penetrate the numinous, and comprehend subtleties until we attain sagacity. Then, what we analyze to its utmost refinement we also bring together in its full greatness. The mind is no empty seat, and principle has a settled home. Does not cultivating virtue and consolidating the Way lie in this?

The substance of our mind is inherently lofty and luminous; only when encumbered does it become low and dark. Above all, we must not encumber ourselves with selfish desires. Let the spirit range beyond Heaven and Earth, incapable of being confined; let our vision transcend the myriad things, incapable of being dazzled: then loftiness and luminosity reach their utmost. Yet mind and affairs accord with one another, and the practice of the constant mean in handling affairs is never external to loftiness and luminosity. Thus, in the diverse expressions of ceremonial observances and dignified comportment, we must interweave and coordinate them to comprehend every variation, and weigh and measure them to apply the mean. Then we may move in every direction without drifting astray, and our understanding may encompass all without overstepping. Within there will be true insight, and in affairs a firm hold on what is right. Does not cultivating virtue and consolidating the Way lie in this?

In the learning of the gentleman, these pursuits contribute to one another in this way. This is why the Way of the sage must await the gentleman to be put into practice. Nevertheless, the Way has its widely manifest and hidden aspects, but no division into refined and coarse; it has substance and function, but no division into internal and external. As for breadth and greatness, and subtle refinement, it is not that breadth and greatness remain coarse and only subtle refinement is refined. As for loftiness and luminosity…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
中庸非高明在內而中庸在外也要之精微盡
者始爲廣大蔽於私者必雜而不精中庸道者
始爲高明累於私者其去中道遠矣此致一之
道也非深造君子其孰能知之
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取於
人以爲善
董選
同考試官教諭毛　批　詞氣渾成卓越羣作有
養之士也錄之
同考試官教諭黃　批　發明大舜公善之心殆
無餘蘊敬服
===
考試官教諭林　批　詞語充足而思致縝密
文字之最優者
考試官教諭敖　批　說理精切非有得於道
者不能作此
大賢表前聖之大必即其公天下之善者以見
之也蓋物理皆吾度內也聖人忘其善於人已
之間其斯以爲大乎孟子論聖賢樂善之意蓋
punctuated:
中庸，非高明在內而中庸在外也。要之，精微盡者始爲廣大，蔽於私者必雜而不精；中庸道者始爲高明，累於私者其去中道遠矣。此致一之道也，非深造君子，其孰能知之？

大舜有大焉，善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以爲善。
董選

同考試官教諭毛批：詞氣渾成，卓越羣作，有養之士也，錄之。
同考試官教諭黃批：發明大舜公善之心，殆無餘蘊，敬服。
考試官教諭林批：詞語充足，而思致縝密，文字之最優者。
考試官教諭敖批：說理精切，非有得於道者不能作此。

大賢表前聖之大，必即其公天下之善者以見之也。蓋物理皆吾度內也，聖人忘其善於人已之間，其斯以爲大乎？孟子論聖賢樂善之意，蓋
translation_en:
…and the constant mean: it is not that lofty illumination lies within while the constant mean lies without. In essence, only one who fully comprehends the refined and subtle achieves breadth and greatness; one obscured by selfishness is inevitably impure rather than refined. Only one who follows the way of the constant mean [?] achieves lofty illumination; one burdened by selfishness is far removed from the middle way. This is the way of attaining unity. Who but a gentleman of profound attainment could understand it?

“Great Shun had something still greater: he shared goodness with others, set aside his own views to follow others, and delighted in drawing upon others to do good.”
Dong Xuan

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “The language and spirit form a seamless whole, surpassing the other compositions. This is a man of cultivated character. Accept him.”
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “He elucidates Great Shun’s disposition to share goodness impartially, leaving scarcely anything unexplored. I respectfully admire it.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The language is ample, and the thought meticulous. This is among the finest compositions.”
Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: “The exposition of principle is precise and incisive. Only someone who has attained an understanding of the Way could write this.”

When a great worthy sets forth the greatness of an earlier sage, he must reveal it through that sage’s sharing of the goodness of all under Heaven. For the principles of things all fall within the compass of my understanding. The sage forgets distinctions between others and himself [?] concerning goodness: is this not what makes him great? In discussing how sages and worthies delight in goodness, Mencius meant to say…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰聖人以天下爲度取善以大同爲極彼禹與
子路好善之心固誠矣進而上之虞舜爲弗可
及矣乎吾見含弘廣大以天下之公理而與天
下共之渾然物我之兩忘焉明通公溥以斯民
之懿德而與斯世同之泯然形迹之俱化焉斯
其所以爲大也而何以見其然耶是故重華協
帝明物察倫舜固未嘗有未善也而自足者未
有不滯於是已矣彼則懋昭乎無我之衷每舍
已以從人遷善徙義之餘一物來順應之妙也
是其道可以配乎天地而望道猶有所未見夫
===
何有於係吝之私哉理無不在言弗可畧人固
有善之可錄也而忌能者未有不狹於取人矣
舜則式彰乎若虛之量恒取人以益已好問好
察之餘一執中用中之地也是其德既已躋乎
帝王而求善猶有所不及夫何有於勉强之意
哉夫始也虛其心以爲天下而終也聮天下以
成其身忘已忘人無內無外舜之大于禹子路
如此者宜孟子表之以示人也與抑舜之心其
punctuated: 曰：「聖人以天下爲度，取善以大同爲極。彼禹與子路，好善之心固誠矣；進而上之，虞舜爲弗可及矣乎！吾見含弘廣大，以天下之公理而與天下共之，渾然物我之兩忘焉；明通公溥，以斯民之懿德而與斯世同之，泯然形迹之俱化焉。斯其所以爲大也，而何以見其然耶？是故重華協帝，明物察倫，舜固未嘗有未善也，而自足者未有不滯於是已矣。彼則懋昭乎無我之衷，每舍已以從人，遷善徙義之餘，一物來順應之妙也。是其道可以配乎天地，而望道猶有所未見，夫何有於係吝之私哉！理無不在，言弗可畧，人固有善之可錄也，而忌能者未有不狹於取人矣。舜則式彰乎若虛之量，恒取人以益已，好問好察之餘，一執中用中之地也。是其德既已躋乎帝王，而求善猶有所不及，夫何有於勉强之意哉！夫始也虛其心以爲天下，而終也聮天下以成其身，忘已忘人，無內無外。舜之大于禹、子路如此者，宜孟子表之以示人也與！抑舜之心其
translation_en:
…says: “The sage takes all under Heaven as his measure and, in drawing upon goodness, takes universal concord as his ultimate aim. The hearts of Yu and Zilu were certainly sincere in their love of goodness; yet, ascending still higher, was Shun of Yu not beyond their reach? I see him embracing all with vast generosity, sharing with all under Heaven the principles common to all under Heaven, so completely that both self and things are forgotten. With luminous understanding and impartial breadth, he shares the excellent virtues of this people with the whole age, so thoroughly that outward distinctions and traces alike dissolve. This is what makes him great. But how can we see that this is so?

“Thus Chonghua [Shun] assisted the emperor, discerning things and examining human relationships. There was certainly nothing in Shun that was not good. Yet those who are self-satisfied invariably become stuck at this point. He, however, earnestly manifested his selfless heart, always setting himself aside to follow others. Beyond advancing toward goodness and turning toward righteousness, there was the subtle capacity to respond fittingly to each thing as it came [?]. His Way could thus match Heaven and Earth, yet he looked toward the Way as though there were still something he had not seen. How could there be any selfish attachment or reluctance to relinquish his own views?

“Principle is present everywhere, and no words may be disregarded; people certainly possess goodness worth recording. Yet those who resent others’ abilities invariably take a narrow view of what they can learn from them. Shun, however, displayed a capacity that seemed empty, constantly drawing upon others to enrich himself. Beyond his love of questioning and close examination, everything rested upon holding to and applying the Mean. His virtue had already attained the stature of emperors and kings, yet he sought goodness as though he had not caught up with it. How could there be any sense of forced effort?

“At first he emptied his heart for the sake of all under Heaven; in the end he united all under Heaven to perfect himself. Forgetting himself and others, he recognized neither an inner nor an outer realm. Such was Shun’s greatness in comparison with Yu and Zilu. Fitting indeed that Mengzi should have singled him out to instruct others! Or might Shun’s heart be…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
天地之心乎無不覆載者天地之體無不容納
者聖人之量苟有所遺天地之化且偏矣況聖
人乎是故衢室之訪非以飾智也岳牧之咨非
以眩觀也此天地積小成大之意聖人純亦不
已之心也學者未造乎至誠之地而欲以語聖
人樂善之心抑末也已
易
六二直方大不習无不利　吳三省
同考試官教諭毛　批〔易道之大此作盡之矣是無以崇易教者宜表出以式〕
===
同考試官教諭黃　批〔敷說詳明語意渾厚必學易而有得者〕
考試官教諭林　批〔說出不習無不利處真得聖人作易本意非苟作者宜錄〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔潔淨精微易義必如此乃佳〕
聖人於坤之六二著其德盛而安焉夫德有所
punctuated:
天地之心乎？無不覆載者，天地之體；無不容納者，聖人之量。苟有所遺，天地之化且偏矣，況聖人乎？是故衢室之訪，非以飾智也；岳牧之咨，非以眩觀也。此天地積小成大之意，聖人純亦不已之心也。學者未造乎至誠之地，而欲以語聖人樂善之心，抑末也已。
易
六二，直方大，不習无不利。吳三省
同考試官教諭毛，批〔易道之大，此作盡之矣。是無以崇易教者，宜表出以式。〕
同考試官教諭黃，批〔敷說詳明，語意渾厚，必學易而有得者。〕
考試官教諭林，批〔說出不習無不利處，真得聖人作易本意，非苟作者，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭敖，批〔潔淨精微，易義必如此乃佳。〕
聖人於坤之六二，著其德盛而安焉。夫德有所
translation_en:
…the heart of Heaven and Earth? To cover and support everything is the essential character of Heaven and Earth; to accommodate and embrace everything is the capacity of the sage. Were anything left out, even the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth would be partial—how much more so in the case of a sage? Thus, seeking counsel in the Hall of Inquiry was not intended to embellish his wisdom, nor was consulting the regional overseers intended to dazzle onlookers. This embodies Heaven and Earth’s purpose of accumulating the small to achieve the great, and the sage’s heart, pure and unceasing. For students who have not attained utmost sincerity to presume to discuss the sage’s delight in goodness is surely to concern themselves merely with the periphery.

Book of Changes

“Six in the second place: straight, square, great; without practice, nothing is unfavorable.” By Wu Sansheng.

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition fully encompasses the greatness of the Way of the Changes. This serves to exalt the teaching of the Changes [?]; it should be singled out as a model.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition is detailed and clear, its language and meaning substantial and profound. The author must have studied the Changes and gained understanding from it.〕

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔By explaining the point of “without practice, nothing is unfavorable,” this truly grasps the sage’s original intention in composing the Changes. It is no careless composition and deserves inclusion.〕

Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and clear, subtle and refined: an exposition of the meaning of the Changes must be like this to be excellent.〕

In the six in the second place of Kun, the sage makes manifest the fullness of its virtue and its ease therein. Now, when virtue has something…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
勉則未安也六二直方大而極其盛焉奚假於
習乎哉宜聖人著以示占也何以言之直方大
者坤之德也未有不出於自然者矣六二柔順
中正得坤道之純者是其性立天下之有而中
焉不倚道周事物之用而智爲不過生理本直
者不撓於攻取之私內焉與柔順正固同其直
也稱物平施者適得乎裒益之宜外焉與賦形
有定同其方也合內外而成其能備體用而造
其極直方之盛又與德合無疆同其大也夫是
===
謂德之盛矣然亦何者而非自然哉吾見性性
存神默成信於不言物物過化變通妙於無爲
心即體體即道非有所存而自不忘一坤德之
直無所於容心也欲即用用即義非有所理而
自不亂一坤德之方不見其應迹也內外兩忘
幾不在我顯微無間動皆以天非有所矯勉而
化不可知一坤德之大而有合一不可測之神
也夫是謂德之安安矣何假於習而後利哉吁
六二之德其同地者也占者而知所勉則六二
punctuated: 勉則未安也。六二直方大而極其盛焉，奚假於習乎哉？宜聖人著以示占也。何以言之？直方大者，坤之德也，未有不出於自然者矣。六二柔順中正，得坤道之純者。是其性立天下之有而中焉不倚，道周事物之用而智爲不過。生理本直者，不撓於攻取之私，內焉與柔順正固同其直也；稱物平施者，適得乎裒益之宜，外焉與賦形有定同其方也。合內外而成其能，備體用而造其極，直方之盛，又與德合無疆同其大也。夫是謂德之盛矣，然亦何者而非自然哉？吾見性性存神，默成信於不言；物物過化，變通妙於無爲。心即體，體即道，非有所存而自不忘，一坤德之直，無所於容心也。欲即用，用即義，非有所理而自不亂，一坤德之方，不見其應迹也。內外兩忘，幾不在我，顯微無間，動皆以天，非有所矯勉而化不可知，一坤德之大，而有合一不可測之神也。夫是謂德之安。安矣，何假於習而後利哉？吁！六二之德，其同地者也。占者而知所勉，則六二
translation_en:
…if effort is required, virtue is not yet at ease. The six in the second place is straight, square, and great, attaining the utmost fullness of virtue. Why should it need practice? It is fitting that the sage made this explicit to instruct those consulting the oracle. How can this be explained? Straightness, squareness, and greatness are the virtues of Kun, and none fails to arise spontaneously. The six in the second place is yielding and compliant, central and correct: it possesses the purity of the Way of Kun. Its nature establishes all that exists under Heaven, remaining centered without leaning to either side; its Way encompasses the functioning of things and affairs, while its understanding and action do not exceed their proper bounds. The principle of life is inherently straight and is not bent by selfish efforts to seize and acquire. Inwardly, its straightness accords with yielding compliance and steadfast correctness. In weighing things and distributing impartially, it achieves precisely the proper balance of reduction and increase. Outwardly, its squareness accords with the fixed forms bestowed upon things. Joining inward and outward, it fulfills its capacity; encompassing substance and function, it reaches the utmost. In the fullness of its straightness and squareness, its greatness likewise accords with virtue that joins with the boundless. This is what is called the fullness of virtue. Yet what in it does not arise spontaneously?

I see it fulfilling each nature and preserving spiritual efficacy, silently achieving trustworthiness without words; attending to each thing and transforming it through its passing presence, wondrously adapting to change without deliberate action. The mind is substance, and substance is the Way. Without deliberately holding anything in mind, it naturally does not forget. Wholly one with the straightness of Kun’s virtue, it leaves no place for deliberate mental intervention. Desire is function, and function is righteousness. Without deliberately putting anything in order, it naturally remains free of disorder. Wholly one with the squareness of Kun’s virtue, it shows no trace of its responses. Inward and outward are both forgotten; the incipient impulse does not lie in the self. Between the manifest and the subtle there is no gap, and every movement accords with Heaven. Without forced effort, its transforming activity cannot be fathomed. Wholly one with the greatness of Kun’s virtue, it possesses the unfathomable spiritual efficacy of unity. This is what is called virtue at ease. Once at ease, why should it require practice before becoming beneficial? Ah! The virtue of the six in the second place is the same as that of Earth. If those consulting the oracle know where to direct their efforts, then the six in the second place…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之德在我矣雖然乾之九二則不言德而即以
大人當之何耶蓋九二龍德而正中者也坤之
六二則猶始於敬義夾持而後其德始不孤九
二性之也六二反之也學者能盡敬義之功而
進於不習无不利之地則際出潛之日自亦可
成利見之功此乾坤二爻命詞之意學者合而
觀之聖學天德王道之始終性反之分陰陽之
義皆可見矣
可久則賢人之德可大則賢人之業易簡
而天下之理得矣天下之理得而成位
乎其中矣
===
董選
同考試官教諭毛 批〔渾雅精到殆邃於經學者〕
同考試官教諭黄 批〔根理之文蓬養之興讀〕
之令人起敬
考試官教諭林 批〔明潔精偉詞理燦然是〕
可式矣
考試官教諭敖 批〔明瑩透徹正是說理文字〕
punctuated:
之德在我矣。雖然，乾之九二則不言德，而即以大人當之，何耶？蓋九二龍德而正中者也。坤之六二則猶始於敬義夾持，而後其德始不孤。九二性之也，六二反之也。學者能盡敬義之功，而進於不習无不利之地，則際出潛之日，自亦可成利見之功。此乾坤二爻命詞之意，學者合而觀之，聖學、天德、王道之始終，性反之分，陰陽之義，皆可見矣。
可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。
董選
同考試官教諭毛批〔渾雅精到，殆邃於經學者。〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔根理之文，蓬養之興，讀〕之令人起敬。
考試官教諭林批〔明潔精偉，詞理燦然，是〕可式矣。
考試官教諭敖批〔明瑩透徹，正是說理文字。〕
translation_en:
…the virtue of the second, yin line will reside in me. Nevertheless, why does the second, yang line of Qian not speak of virtue, but directly identify its bearer as a great man? It is because this line possesses the dragon’s virtue and is precisely central. The second, yin line of Kun, however, still begins with reverence and righteousness sustaining it on either side; only then does its virtue cease to stand alone. The second, yang line possesses this by nature; the second, yin line returns to it through cultivation. If learners can fully accomplish the work of reverence and righteousness and advance to the state in which “without practice, nothing is unfavorable,” then, when they emerge from concealment, they too can achieve the beneficial effect of a great man’s appearing. This is the intent of the wording assigned to these two lines of Qian and Kun. If learners consider them together, they can discern the learning of sages, the virtue of Heaven, the kingly Way from beginning to end, the distinction between possessing virtue by nature and returning to it through cultivation, and the meaning of yin and yang.
“What can endure is the virtue of the worthy; what can become great is the undertaking of the worthy. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are apprehended. When those principles are apprehended, one establishes one’s position in their midst.”
Dong Xuan 董選
Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Integrated and elegant, refined and exact: the author must be deeply versed in classical learning.”
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Writing rooted in principle, with an inspiration nurtured in abundance [?]; reading it inspires respect.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Lucid and clean, refined and splendid; its language and reasoning shine brilliantly. This can serve as a model.”
Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: “Clear, luminous, and penetrating: this is precisely what writing that expounds principle should be.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人著法乾坤者學之所至由賢而入聖也夫
易簡盡天下之理也兼體不累何聖賢之不可
至哉大傳論乾坤之理而人兼體之至此蓋謂
易簡之道盡於乾坤效法於君子固其幾相感
而其理相須矣所造至此果何如哉蓋由易知
而有親焉是以獨得之妙驗人心之同志向於
是而專一矣故曰可久德至於此則體驗眞切
下學已造其極執復盡性上達將底於成雖非
不已之純亦守之而幾於化也由易從而有功
===
焉以樂取之善大同人之公體用於是而兼該
矣故曰可大業至於此則協力以踐其實功不
止於小成兼外以成其能效已獲於積累雖非
無疆之盛亦未達一間也其賢人之德業矣乎
夫賢者固不可及然道不終於此也過此以往
至健在我而合德於乾天下之理不外於易而
吾之心無遺理也至順在我而合德於坤天下
之理不外於簡而吾之事無遺理也德妙於日
新業成於富有人極以立參天地爲三才矣廣
punctuated: 聖人著法乾坤者，學之所至，由賢而入聖也。夫易簡盡天下之理也，兼體不累，何聖賢之不可至哉？大傳論乾坤之理，而人兼體之至此，蓋謂易簡之道盡於乾坤，效法於君子，固其幾相感，而其理相須矣。所造至此，果何如哉？蓋由易知而有親焉，是以獨得之妙，驗人心之同，志向於是而專一矣，故曰可久。德至於此，則體驗眞切，下學已造其極，執復盡性，上達將底於成。雖非不已之純，亦守之而幾於化也。由易從而有功焉，以樂取之善，大同人之公，體用於是而兼該矣，故曰可大。業至於此，則協力以踐其實，功不止於小成；兼外以成其能，效已獲於積累。雖非無疆之盛，亦未達一間也。其賢人之德業矣乎！夫賢者固不可及，然道不終於此也。過此以往，至健在我，而合德於乾，天下之理不外於易，而吾之心無遺理也；至順在我，而合德於坤，天下之理不外於簡，而吾之事無遺理也。德妙於日新，業成於富有，人極以立，參天地爲三才矣。廣
translation_en:
The sage manifestly takes Qian and Kun as models [?]: this is the attainment of learning, advancing from worthiness into sagehood. Ease and simplicity encompass all the principles under Heaven. If one embodies both without encumbrance, what attainment of worthiness or sagehood could be beyond reach? The Great Commentary discusses the principles of Qian and Kun—Heaven and Earth—and how people come to embody both to this extent. Its meaning is that the way of ease and simplicity finds its full expression in Qian and Kun, and that the gentleman takes them as his models. Their incipient impulses respond to one another, and their principles depend upon one another. What, then, is the attainment reached at this point?

Because one is easy to understand, one gains close affinity with others. Thus the subtle understanding attained for oneself is confirmed by what human hearts share, and one’s purpose becomes single and undivided. Hence the expression “capable of enduring.” When virtue reaches this point, its embodiment and experience are genuine and keen. Learning about things below has already reached its utmost; through holding fast and returning [?], one fully realizes one’s nature, and comprehension of what is above approaches completion. Although this is not yet the purity of unceasing activity, by maintaining it one comes close to transformation.

Because one is easy to follow, one achieves results. Through delighting in adopting what is good, one extends the impartiality of fellowship with others [?], and both substance and function are comprehensively embraced. Hence the expression “capable of greatness.” When achievement reaches this point, one joins forces with others to put it into practice, and one’s accomplishments go beyond minor successes. By encompassing what is external, one brings one’s capacities to fulfillment, and results have already accrued through accumulation. Although this is not yet boundless flourishing, only a single interval remains before attainment. Surely this is the virtue and achievement of the worthy!

The worthy are indeed difficult to equal, yet the Way does not end here. Advancing beyond this, utmost vigor resides in me, and my virtue accords with Qian. The principles of all under Heaven lie within ease, and my heart leaves no principle uncomprehended. Utmost compliance resides in me, and my virtue accords with Kun. The principles of all under Heaven lie within simplicity, and my affairs leave no principle unfulfilled. Virtue attains its subtle excellence through daily renewal; achievement reaches fulfillment through abundant possession. The ultimate standard of humanity is thereby established, and humanity joins Heaven and Earth as the Three Powers. Vast…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
大悉備也內外合一也成位乎中配造化於兩
間矣其聖人之能事矣乎此體道之極功不外
於易簡而得之也希賢希聖者其知法乾坤之
道與大抵吾身之理卽天地之理求天地之理
於吾身則吾身一天地矣夫何學易者謂易簡
不足以盡道而求遠且難者是故日用而不知
也成天地之能使百姓與能者其唯聖人乎體
易者止諸至足由賢而聖亦易易也
書
克明俊德以親九族九族既睦平章百姓
百姓昭明協和萬邦黎民於變時雍
魯邦彥
===
同考試官教諭葛　批　〔破意用善推成化于經解甚明且據理爲文體格平正可以知子之能道〕
同考試官教諭周　批　〔俊德全用欽明二句語意渾成以親上補身脩意出則齊治平亦爲有本〕
〔經學之明無踰子矣敬服〕
punctuated:
大悉備也，內外合一也。成位乎中，配造化於兩間矣，其聖人之能事矣乎！此體道之極功，不外於易簡而得之也。希賢希聖者，其知法乾坤之道與！大抵吾身之理卽天地之理，求天地之理於吾身，則吾身一天地矣。夫何學易者謂易簡不足以盡道，而求遠且難者？是故日用而不知也。成天地之能，使百姓與能者，其唯聖人乎！體易者止諸至足，由賢而聖，亦易易也。

書
克明俊德，以親九族；九族既睦，平章百姓；百姓昭明，協和萬邦。黎民於變時雍。
魯邦彥

同考試官教諭葛，批：〔破意用善推成化，于經解甚明，且據理爲文，體格平正，可以知子之能道。〕
同考試官教諭周，批：〔俊德全用欽明二句，語意渾成，以親上補身脩意，出則齊治平亦爲有本。〕〔經學之明，無踰子矣，敬服。〕
translation_en:
…greatness is fully realized, and inner and outer are united. Taking one's proper place between Heaven and Earth, one matches their creative transformation. Is this not the consummate accomplishment of the sage? This supreme achievement in embodying the Way is attained through nothing beyond ease and simplicity. Let those who aspire to become worthies and sages understand the way of taking Qian and Kun as their models! In general, the principles within ourselves are precisely those of Heaven and Earth. If we seek the principles of Heaven and Earth within ourselves, each of us becomes a Heaven and Earth. Why, then, do students of the Changes claim that ease and simplicity cannot encompass the Way, and seek what is remote and difficult? This is indeed to use it daily without understanding it. Surely only the sage can fulfill the capacities of Heaven and Earth and enable the common people to participate in them! Those who embody the Changes rest in utter sufficiency; progressing from worthy to sage is also perfectly easy.

Book of Documents

“He was able to make manifest his outstanding virtue, and thereby bring affection to the nine degrees of kinship. Once these were harmonious, he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans. Once the hundred clans were enlightened, he harmonized the myriad states. The common people were thus transformed and became harmonious.”

Lu Bangyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: “The opening interpretation uses the idea of skillfully extending virtue to accomplish moral transformation, making the interpretation of the classic very clear. Moreover, the composition is grounded in principle, and its form and style are balanced and correct. This shows your ability to articulate the Way.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The treatment of ‘outstanding virtue’ draws entirely upon the two phrases beginning with ‘reverent and discerning’; wording and meaning form a seamless whole. Before ‘thereby bring affection,’ the essay supplies the idea of cultivating oneself, so that, when virtue is extended outward, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world likewise have a foundation.” “No one surpasses you in clarity of understanding of the classics. I respectfully admire you.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林 批〔理明詞達蓋得于典謨〕
〔之深者可式〕
考試官教諭敖 批〔典雅縝密僅見此篇〕
聖君能明其大德而善推以成化焉蓋德以敷
化則其出爲有本矣而家國天下推之有弗準
者乎史臣言此以著帝堯放勲之實也意曰大
哉堯之爲君也其德業之盛固大而無所不至
矣然果何所徵耶彼德者夫人之所同具限于
天者不可以言大而爲物蔽者不可以言明惟
===
帝欽明文思安安也允恭克讓也蓋德之性諸
天者無一之不備而其備諸已者無一之不明
則德極其盛而身無不脩矣而推行豈無其漸
乎故于家而九族焉以是德而親之則情誼洽
于彝倫之厚仁讓興于惇敘之深親親恩篤而
家於是乎齊矣于國而百姓焉以是德而平章
之則大道公而人紀可立軌物彰而民彝以全
式昭明德而國於是乎治矣以至萬邦之廣則
盡乎天下矣以是德而協和之但見合同而化
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批〔理明詞達，蓋得于典謨〕〔之深者，可式。〕
考試官教諭敖批〔典雅縝密，僅見此篇。〕
聖君能明其大德，而善推以成化焉。蓋德以敷化，則其出爲有本矣，而家國天下推之，有弗準者乎？史臣言此，以著帝堯放勲之實也。意曰：大哉，堯之爲君也！其德業之盛，固大而無所不至矣，然果何所徵耶？彼德者，夫人之所同具，限于天者不可以言大，而爲物蔽者不可以言明。惟帝欽明文思安安也，允恭克讓也。蓋德之性諸天者，無一之不備，而其備諸已者，無一之不明，則德極其盛，而身無不脩矣。而推行豈無其漸乎？故于家而九族焉，以是德而親之，則情誼洽于彝倫之厚，仁讓興于惇敘之深，親親恩篤，而家於是乎齊矣。于國而百姓焉，以是德而平章之，則大道公而人紀可立，軌物彰而民彝以全，式昭明德，而國於是乎治矣。以至萬邦之廣，則盡乎天下矣。以是德而協和之，但見合同而化
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔The reasoning is clear and the language expressive; this evidently derives from a deep understanding of the Canons and Counsels〕〔and may serve as a model.〕
Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical elegance and meticulous composition: only this essay displays them.〕
The sage ruler can illuminate his great virtue and skillfully extend it to accomplish moral transformation. When virtue spreads its transforming influence, its outward effects have a foundation. When extended to the family, the state, and all under Heaven, could it fail to provide a standard anywhere? The historian says this to reveal the substance of Emperor Yao’s vast achievements. His meaning is as follows: Great indeed was Yao as ruler! The flourishing of his virtue and achievements was assuredly so great that it reached everywhere. But what, in fact, attests to this? Virtue is something everyone possesses alike. What is ‘limited by Heaven’ [?] cannot be called great, and what is obscured by external things cannot be called luminous. The emperor alone was reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, naturally at ease in these qualities; he was truly respectful and capable of yielding. Of the virtues endowed by Heaven, he lacked none; of those possessed within himself, none remained unilluminated. Thus his virtue attained its fullest flourishing, and his person was cultivated in every respect. Could its extension into practice lack a gradual progression?
Thus, within the family were the nine degrees of kinship. He drew them close through this virtue, so that affection and a sense of duty permeated the depth of the constant human relationships, while benevolence and deference arose from the care with which kinship ranks were ordered. His kindness toward his kin was profound, and thereby his family was brought into order. Within the state were the hundred clans. Through this virtue he equitably distinguished and ordered them, so that the Great Way prevailed impartially and the bonds of human society could be established. Standards of conduct were manifest, and the people’s constant moral nature was preserved intact. Luminous virtue was thus made manifest, and thereby the state was well governed. Extending to the breadth of the myriad states, it encompassed all under Heaven. Through this virtue he brought them into concord, and one saw only their union and transformation …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
大順之俗成焉從欲以治雍熙之象昭焉順帝
則而不知忘帝力于何有則於變時雍而天下
不其平乎是則俊德克明于一身而大化遂成
于天下所謂放勳之實于玆見矣而被四表格
上下豈虛語也耶大抵天道不言而神化聖人
法天而難名其所以然者要亦有德以爲之先
焉耳今觀堯能明德而家國天下之治舉不外
此然則有治平之責者曷亦端其本乎本端則
化成而帝堯之治夫何難致也耶
我聞在昔成湯旣受命時則有若伊尹格
于皇天在太甲時則有若保衡
馬斯祖
===
同考試官教諭葛 批
通篇脫去凡俗而詞語
敷暢體裁峻整轉束處尤有思致明經之士也
同考試官教諭周 批
以輔聖輔賢立意甚得
本旨且保衡下補對格天之意迥出諸作宜冠多士
考試官教諭林 批
周公留召公之意究然
在目可以爲文矣
punctuated:
大順之俗成焉，從欲以治，雍熙之象昭焉。順帝則而不知，忘帝力于何有，則於變時雍，而天下不其平乎？是則俊德克明于一身，而大化遂成于天下，所謂放勳之實于玆見矣。而被四表，格上下，豈虛語也耶？大抵天道不言而神化，聖人法天而難名，其所以然者，要亦有德以爲之先焉耳。今觀堯能明德，而家國天下之治舉不外此，然則有治平之責者，曷亦端其本乎？本端則化成，而帝堯之治夫何難致也耶？
「我聞在昔成湯旣受命，時則有若伊尹，格于皇天；在太甲時，則有若保衡。」
馬斯祖
同考試官教諭葛批：通篇脫去凡俗，而詞語敷暢，體裁峻整，轉束處尤有思致，明經之士也。
同考試官教諭周批：以輔聖輔賢立意，甚得本旨。且保衡下補對格天之意，迥出諸作，宜冠多士。
考試官教諭林批：周公留召公之意，究然在目，可以爲文矣。
translation_en:
…customs of perfect concord take shape. Governing in accordance with the people's desires, he makes manifest a scene of harmony and prosperity. They follow the emperor's standards without knowing it, oblivious to his power, asking, “What has the emperor's power to do with us?” Thus transformed, they live in harmony: would not all under Heaven then be at peace? His great virtue is made bright in his own person, and a profound transformation is thereby accomplished throughout the world. Here we see the substance of what is called his “far-reaching achievement.” How could the words “extending to the four outer bounds and reaching above and below” be empty talk? In general, the Way of Heaven transforms mysteriously without speaking; the sage models himself on Heaven, and his achievement defies description. The reason for this is, essentially, that virtue comes first. Now we see that Yao could make his virtue bright, and that the ordering of family, state, and all under Heaven lay entirely within this. Should not those responsible for good government and peace likewise set their foundation right? Once the foundation is right, transformation is accomplished. What difficulty would there then be in attaining the government of Emperor Yao?
“I have heard that formerly, when Cheng Tang had received the Mandate, there was Yi Yin, who reached August Heaven; in the time of Tai Jia, there was Bao Heng.”
Ma Sizu
Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: The entire essay rises above the commonplace. Its language unfolds fluently, and its structure is rigorous and orderly. The transitions and conclusion show particular thoughtfulness. Here is a scholar who understands the Classics.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: By making assistance to a sage and assistance to a worthy ruler its central conception, the essay captures the fundamental meaning extremely well. Moreover, after mentioning Bao Heng, it supplies the idea corresponding to “reaching Heaven.” It far surpasses the other compositions and deserves to rank first among the candidates.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The Duke of Zhou's intention in retaining the Duke of Shao is plainly [?] before our eyes. This may indeed be counted a worthy composition.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭敖　批　意精詞雅經義之最佳者宜錄以式
大臣舉有商之元聖旣輔聖以成治復輔賢以
保治夫治至格天治之極也商臣兩相其君而
功化若此其斯爲聖之任也與想昔周公勉留
召公之意葢曰迓衡固得于天休而致理寔資
乎相道然我之所以不欲公去者葢嘗聞之商
事而知其然矣夫啓運之君有成湯焉盛德受
命宜無賴于賢臣之輔矣時則有若伊尹者應
===
元聖之求肇維新之命一德咸有克立夫昭受
之基萬民誕保寔弘乎丕冒之績商邑之用協
也四方之見德也其道化漸被葢與天之無不
覆幬者同其用矣而左右之功焉可誣耶所謂
輔聖以成治者如此其嗣運之君有太甲焉繼
體守成亦足以致一時之治矣時則有若保衡
者葢伊尹以宗臣之舊任阿衡之職匡救之資
殆一身而二任輔理之助將異世而同功用協
者如昔也見德者如昔也其奕葉相承葢與湯
punctuated:
考試官敎諭敖批：意精詞雅，經義之最佳者，宜錄以式。

大臣舉有商之元聖，旣輔聖以成治，復輔賢以保治。夫治至格天，治之極也。商臣兩相其君，而功化若此，其斯爲聖之任也與！想昔周公勉留召公之意，葢曰：迓衡固得于天休，而致理寔資乎相道。然我之所以不欲公去者，葢嘗聞之商事而知其然矣。夫啓運之君，有成湯焉，盛德受命，宜無賴于賢臣之輔矣。時則有若伊尹者，應元聖之求，肇維新之命，一德咸有，克立夫昭受之基；萬民誕保，寔弘乎丕冒之績。商邑之用協也，四方之見德也，其道化漸被，葢與天之無不覆幬者同其用矣，而左右之功焉可誣耶？所謂輔聖以成治者如此。其嗣運之君，有太甲焉，繼體守成，亦足以致一時之治矣。時則有若保衡者，葢伊尹以宗臣之舊，任阿衡之職，匡救之資，殆一身而二任；輔理之助，將異世而同功。用協者如昔也，見德者如昔也，其奕葉相承，葢與湯
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: “The conception is refined and the language elegant. This is among the very best essays on the meaning of the Classics and should be recorded as a model.”

The great minister cited the supreme sage of Shang: having assisted a sage ruler in establishing good government, he then assisted a worthy ruler in preserving it. When government reaches Heaven, it has attained its highest perfection. This minister of Shang served two rulers as chief minister, and his achievements and transforming influence were such as these. Was this not the responsibility of a sage? Imagine the intention with which the Duke of Zhou once urged the Duke of Shao to remain. He was, in effect, saying: “To secure lasting equilibrium certainly depends upon Heaven’s favor, but achieving good order truly relies upon the way of the chief minister. Yet my reason for wishing you not to leave is that I have heard of the affairs of Shang and learned from them why this is so.”

Among rulers who inaugurated a dynasty was Cheng Tang. Possessing abundant virtue and receiving the Mandate, he might seem to have had no need of assistance from worthy ministers. Yet at that time there was Yi Yin, who answered the search for a supreme sage and inaugurated the renewed Mandate. Possessing single-minded virtue together with his ruler, he established the foundation for gloriously receiving the Mandate; greatly protecting the myriad people, he extended the achievement of sheltering all. The capital of Shang was thereby brought into harmony, and the four quarters manifested virtue. The gradual diffusion of his moral transformation matched the workings of Heaven, whose shelter excludes nothing. How, then, could his contribution as the ruler’s assistant be denied? Such was his assistance to a sage ruler in establishing good government.

Among rulers who inherited the dynasty was Tai Jia. Succeeding to the throne and preserving what had been accomplished, he too could have achieved good government in his time. Yet at that time there was the Baoheng: Yi Yin, with his long service as a minister of the ruling house, held the office of Aheng, or chief minister. In providing correction and rescue, he effectively fulfilled two charges in one person; in assisting government, he achieved the same merit under different reigns. Harmony prevailed as before, and virtue was manifested as before. Through the succession of generations, this was comparable to Tang’s …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之丕釐耿命者同其休矣而格天之治曷有艾
耶所謂輔賢以保治者又如此是則伊尹始相
成湯以成治者非有所冀也君臣道合自莫遏
其達行之機其繼相太甲以保治者亦非有所
繫也而老成謀國蓋有不忍于去者矣今公亦
周之舊臣也而自處顧異于伊尹者意獨何哉
雖然召公非有異于尹也即其相周輔武王以
開永清之治輔成王以致鳴鳳之符其格天之
功業亦懋矣而周公猶致懇懇于公者蓋以滋至
===
之休非一人所能戡而篤棐之責必同心乃可
濟而示以凝命圖終之道也噫此則周公勉留
之意也此召公之所以爲公留也其致主之義
俱可識矣
詩
如切如磋如琢如磨瑟兮僩兮赫兮咺兮
張洼
同考試官教諭鄭　批　詞古而理足三讀之有
餘味錄式
punctuated:
之丕釐耿命者同其休矣，而格天之治曷有艾耶？所謂輔賢以保治者又如此。是則伊尹始相成湯以成治者，非有所冀也，君臣道合，自莫遏其達行之機；其繼相太甲以保治者，亦非有所繫也，而老成謀國，蓋有不忍于去者矣。今公亦周之舊臣也，而自處顧異于伊尹者，意獨何哉？雖然，召公非有異于尹也。即其相周，輔武王以開永清之治，輔成王以致鳴鳳之符，其格天之功業亦懋矣。而周公猶致懇懇于公者，蓋以滋至之休，非一人所能戡，而篤棐之責，必同心乃可濟，而示以凝命圖終之道也。噫！此則周公勉留之意也，此召公之所以爲公留也，其致主之義俱可識矣。
詩
如切如磋，如琢如磨，瑟兮僩兮，赫兮咺兮。
張洼
同考試官教諭鄭，批：詞古而理足，三讀之有餘味，錄式。
translation_en:
…shared in the glory of Tang’s grand reception of the illustrious Mandate. How could such government, reaching Heaven itself, ever come to an end? Such, again, was his assistance to a worthy ruler in preserving good government. Thus, when Yi Yin first served Cheng Tang as minister and brought good government to fruition, he did so without seeking any personal gain. Ruler and minister were united in the Way, and nothing could obstruct the opportunity to put it fully into practice. When he subsequently served Tai Jia as minister and preserved good government, neither was he bound by any personal attachment. Rather, as a seasoned elder planning for the state, he could not bear to leave. Now you, my lord, are likewise a longstanding servant of Zhou; yet you conduct yourself differently from Yi Yin. What can your intention be?
Nevertheless, the Duke of Shao was not different from Yi Yin. In serving Zhou, he assisted King Wu in inaugurating an enduring age of peace and King Cheng in bringing forth the auspicious sign of the singing phoenix. His achievements in reaching Heaven were indeed great. Yet the Duke of Zhou continued to entreat him earnestly, because the blessings arriving in increasing abundance could not be secured by one man alone, and the responsibility of providing devoted assistance could be fulfilled only through unity of purpose. He thus showed him the way to consolidate the Mandate and plan for its fulfillment to the end. Ah! This was the Duke of Zhou’s intention in urging him to remain, and this was why the Duke of Shao remained for his sake. We can thus understand the commitment of both to bringing their ruler to perfection.
Book of Odes
“As if cut and filed, as if carved and polished; solemn and dignified, radiant and illustrious.”
Zhang Wa 張洼
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The diction is antique and the reasoning ample. Even after three readings, it leaves a lingering savor. Selected as a model.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林　批　文思簡古字義精當場
中無以踰此矣
考試官教諭敖　批　發明武公爲學處精切
典雅可嘉
詩人擬賢侯盡脩德之功而極著外之盛焉夫
功已至而益求其極德無不脩矣然則其容之
盛又惡可已哉衛人美武公作此蓋曰學每病
於止足道莫貴於勉脩我公德裕于身固吾人
所望而震矣而其始之脩德也何如彼物理無
===
窮之妙非致知無以會其通也彼則考德於講
習之餘理既明矣而探索之益至極深研幾務
求至乎精義入神之域猶之治骨角者既切而
復磋焉殆已精而益精者耶天人貞勝之機非
力行無以致其決也彼則省察於理欲之間幾
已審矣而克治之益力釋回增美務求造夫萬
理明淨之天猶之治玉石者既琢而復磨焉殆
已密而益密者耶至是知行之功盡所以致養
乎內者不足言矣而其發之於外也何如吾見
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批：文思簡古，字義精當，場中無以踰此矣。

考試官教諭敖批：發明武公爲學處，精切典雅，可嘉。

詩人擬賢侯盡脩德之功，而極著外之盛焉。夫功已至而益求其極，德無不脩矣。然則其容之盛，又惡可已哉？衛人美武公，作此蓋曰：學每病於止足，道莫貴於勉脩。我公德裕于身，固吾人所望而震矣。而其始之脩德也何如？彼物理無窮之妙，非致知無以會其通也。彼則考德於講習之餘，理既明矣，而探索之益至，極深研幾，務求至乎精義入神之域，猶之治骨角者，既切而復磋焉，殆已精而益精者耶？天人貞勝之機，非力行無以致其決也。彼則省察於理欲之間，幾已審矣，而克治之益力，釋回增美，務求造夫萬理明淨之天，猶之治玉石者，既琢而復磨焉，殆已密而益密者耶？至是知行之功盡，所以致養乎內者不足言矣。而其發之於外也何如？吾見
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The conception is spare and antique in style; the wording and interpretation are precise and apt. Nothing in this examination surpasses it.”

Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: “Its elucidation of Duke Wu’s pursuit of learning is penetrating, exact, and classically elegant. Commendable.”

The poet portrays the worthy lord as bringing the work of cultivating virtue to completion and fully manifesting its outward splendor. Once his efforts had attained their goal, he sought still further to reach their utmost limit, leaving no virtue uncultivated. How, then, could the splendor of his bearing fail to appear? The people of Wei composed this poem to praise Duke Wu, saying, in effect: Learning is often impaired by stopping in complacent satisfaction; in pursuing the Way, nothing is more precious than diligent cultivation. Our lord’s person abounds in virtue, and we assuredly look up to him in awe. But how did he cultivate virtue at the outset? The inexhaustible subtleties of the principles of things cannot be comprehended in their interconnectedness without extending knowledge. Thus, beyond discussion and study, he examined virtue. Though principle was already clear to him, he pursued his inquiries still further, plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient stirrings of things, striving to reach the realm where refined understanding of meaning enters into the numinous. He was like one working bone and horn, who, having cut them, files them further. Was this not to become ever more refined after refinement had already been achieved? In the contest between Heaven’s principle and human desires, where constancy determines victory, decisive resolution cannot be attained without vigorous practice. Thus he scrutinized the distinction between principle and desire. Though he had already discerned their incipient stirrings, he exerted himself still more in overcoming and regulating his faults, casting off perversity and augmenting goodness, striving to attain a heavenly state in which all principles are clear and pure. He was like one working jade and stone, who, having carved them, polishes them further. Was this not to become ever more thorough after thoroughness had already been achieved? At this point, the work of knowing and acting was complete; there is no need to speak further of how he fully nourished his inner self. But how did this manifest itself outwardly? I see …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
敬足以勝怠儼然而臨之以莊禮足以治躬肅
然人望之而畏德既盛而容亦盛瑟焉僩焉有
莫知其所爲者其有道之氣象矣乎暢於四支
皆英華之旁達發於面背一睟盎之流形養既
充而發亦充赫焉喧焉有莫測其所以者其君
子之暉吉矣乎至是光輝之謂大所以豫利乎
外者不足言矣是則功純於積久德發於內充
此天理自然之妙非武公其孰能與於斯抑此
其乾坤之義乎乾曰君子以自强不息而於坤
===
之六二有取于中順之德蓋天地之道相禪無
窮而君子之學緝熙不已仁以爲已任雖一息
尚存而不懈道足以物身有不知老之將至云
爾衛武公知此蓋亦聖賢之徒也讀詩者合易
而觀之思過半矣
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之儀式刑
文王之典日靖四方伊嘏文王既右享
之我其夙夜畏天之威于時保之
高才
punctuated:
敬足以勝怠，儼然而臨之以莊；禮足以治躬，肅然人望之而畏。德既盛而容亦盛，瑟焉僩焉，有莫知其所爲者，其有道之氣象矣乎！暢於四支，皆英華之旁達；發於面背，一睟盎之流形。養既充而發亦充，赫焉喧焉，有莫測其所以者，其君子之暉吉矣乎！至是，光輝之謂大，所以豫利乎外者不足言矣。是則功純於積久，德發於內充，此天理自然之妙，非武公，其孰能與於斯？抑此其乾坤之義乎？乾曰：「君子以自强不息。」而於坤之六二，有取于中順之德。蓋天地之道相禪無窮，而君子之學緝熙不已。仁以爲已任，雖一息尚存而不懈；道足以物身，有不知老之將至云爾。衛武公知此，蓋亦聖賢之徒也。讀詩者合易而觀之，思過半矣。

我將我享，維羊維牛，維天其右之。儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。伊嘏文王，既右享之。我其夙夜，畏天之威，于時保之。

高才
translation_en:
…Reverence suffices to overcome indolence: he approaches others with solemn dignity. Ritual propriety suffices to regulate his conduct: people behold his solemn bearing and stand in awe. His virtue is abundant, and his bearing is likewise impressive. Grave and dignified, he has something about him whose workings none can fathom—is this not the bearing of one who possesses the Way? It courses through his four limbs, its finest essence spreading everywhere; it appears in his face and back, pure and abundant, taking visible form. His inward cultivation is full, and its outward expression is likewise full. Brilliant and illustrious, he has something about him whose source none can fathom—is this not the gentleman’s radiance [?]? At this point, he attains what is called “greatness” through his shining brilliance; merely speaking of its outward benefits [?] cannot do it justice. Thus sustained effort becomes perfected through long accumulation, and virtue manifests itself from inward fullness. Such is the spontaneous subtlety of heavenly principle. Who but Duke Wu could attain this? Might this also be the meaning of Qian and Kun? Qian says: “The gentleman strengthens himself without ceasing.” And in Kun’s second yin line, there is instruction to be drawn from the virtue of centrality and compliance. For the ways of Heaven and Earth succeed one another without end, while the gentleman’s learning grows ever brighter without ceasing. He takes benevolence as his own responsibility and does not slacken while a single breath remains. The Way suffices to govern his person [?], so that he is unaware that old age is approaching. Duke Wu of Wei understood this; surely he too belonged among the followers of the sages and worthies. Those who read the Book of Odes together with the Book of Changes will have grasped more than half its meaning.

I present my offerings—sheep and oxen. May Heaven accept them! I follow and emulate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace to the four quarters. Ah, great King Wen, you have accepted and enjoyed these offerings! Morning and night I shall stand in awe of Heaven’s majesty, and thereby preserve this.

Gao Cai

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭　批　〔文思典健得周人敬天〕
〔法祖意〕
考試官教諭林　批　〔精警可誦〕
考試官教諭敖　批　〔醇正之作〕
周人尊親配帝有所以冀其享者而思以保之
焉夫奉祭固貴於盡誠也然謂誠之足以格神
而或弛焉豈能永保其享乎周人所以深致意
也蓋曰明堂之禮固由於義起矣然唯仁人孝
子爲能享帝享親也顧我今日之祭何如哉彼
===
至尊莫如天也我則以牲雖不樂於篠大而繭
栗豈足以盡情進以少牢而儀物之甚備享以
太牢而牲特之甚充其志厚者其義章其心誠
者其禮辨意者有皇上帝如或鑒之以慰吾洞
屬之念乎至親莫如文也我則以感通雖原於
一本而繼體實妙於善承率乃攸行以靖今之
天下鑒于成憲以撫今之萬民爲於前者美而
章爲於後者盛而傳吾知伊嘏文王享之來享
以綏吾思成之懷乎夫天與文王既皆右享我
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭　批：〔文思典健，得周人敬天法祖意。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔精警可誦。〕
考試官教諭敖　批：〔醇正之作。〕
周人尊親配帝，有所以冀其享者，而思以保之焉。夫奉祭固貴於盡誠也，然謂誠之足以格神而或弛焉，豈能永保其享乎？周人所以深致意也。蓋曰：明堂之禮，固由於義起矣，然唯仁人孝子爲能享帝享親也。顧我今日之祭何如哉？彼至尊莫如天也，我則以牲。雖不樂於篠大，而繭栗豈足以盡情？進以少牢，而儀物之甚備；享以太牢，而牲特之甚充。其志厚者其義章，其心誠者其禮辨。意者有皇上帝，如或鑒之，以慰吾洞屬之念乎？至親莫如文也，我則以感通。雖原於一本，而繼體實妙於善承。率乃攸行，以靖今之天下；鑒于成憲，以撫今之萬民。爲於前者美而章，爲於後者盛而傳。吾知伊嘏文王享之來享，以綏吾思成之懷乎！夫天與文王既皆右享我
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The conception and expression are dignified and vigorous, capturing the Zhou people's intention to revere Heaven and emulate their ancestors.〕
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Incisive and perceptive; worthy of recitation.〕
Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: 〔A work of purity and rectitude.〕
The people of Zhou honored their parent by associating him with the Supreme Lord in sacrifice. They had grounds for hoping that their offerings would be accepted, and sought to ensure that this acceptance would endure. In presenting sacrifices, fully realizing one's sincerity is certainly paramount. Yet if one supposes that sincerity suffices to move the spirits, and consequently sometimes grows lax, how can one ensure that they will forever accept the offerings? This is why the people of Zhou gave the matter such profound attention.
The meaning is this: the rites of the Hall of Enlightenment arose from considerations of righteousness; yet only a humane person and a filial son can offer fitting sacrifices to the Supreme Lord and to his parent. How, then, does my sacrifice today measure up? None is more exalted than Heaven, and I present sacrificial animals to it. Although it takes no pleasure in “slender bamboo and largeness” [?], how could a calf whose horns are no larger than a cocoon or a chestnut suffice to express all my feelings? I present the lesser animal offering, with its ceremonial provisions most fully prepared; I sacrifice the greater animal offering, with its victims most amply supplied. When one's purpose is devoted, its righteousness is manifest; when one's heart is sincere, its ritual expression is distinct. Might the august Supreme Lord behold these offerings and thereby console my thoughts of profound devotion [?]?
None is closer in kinship than King Wen, and I seek communion with him through heartfelt feeling. Although this relationship originates in a single ancestral source, the true excellence of succession lies in carrying on his work well. I follow the course you pursued, to bring peace to the world today; I take your established statutes as my guide, to care for all the people today. What was accomplished before was beautiful and illustrious; what is accomplished afterward flourishes and is handed down. I know that great King Wen will accept the offerings and come to partake of them, thereby bringing peace to my longing to realize his presence through remembrance. Since Heaven and King Wen have both graciously accepted my offerings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣其所以右享者誠也我其可但已乎必時幾
以惕其志肅然明命之有嚴庶神與天游所以
鑒我者無已焉否則一時不謹而怠心生可冀
天之常格哉夙夜以警諸懷儼然明威之是畏
庶心與文合所以享我者不窮焉否則斯須不
敬而慢心作可保文之永綏哉吁玆見周人無
時而非敬天法祖之心則無往而非祈天永命
之道矣明堂之祀而豈徒哉雖然祭不可瀆不
欲煩也南郊之祭旣尊稷以配天而玆復以文
===
王配焉何與王者德厚可以流光力大足以及
遠茍可以致吾敬而以天下儉焉仁人孝子之
心兩有歉矣况祖功宗德禮尤不可已乎故尊
尊所以廣仁而亦以達義也親親所以崇孝而
亦以示信也周道之備其不在玆乎茍不闇性
與天道其孰能知之
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕
張道充
punctuated:
矣。其所以右享者，誠也。我其可但已乎？必時幾以惕其志，肅然明命之有嚴，庶神與天游，所以鑒我者無已焉。否則一時不謹而怠心生，可冀天之常格哉？夙夜以警諸懷，儼然明威之是畏，庶心與文合，所以享我者不窮焉。否則斯須不敬而慢心作，可保文之永綏哉？吁！玆見周人無時而非敬天法祖之心，則無往而非祈天永命之道矣。明堂之祀而豈徒哉！雖然，祭不可瀆，不欲煩也。南郊之祭旣尊稷以配天，而玆復以文王配焉，何與？王者德厚，可以流光；力大，足以及遠。茍可以致吾敬，而以天下儉焉，仁人孝子之心兩有歉矣。况祖功宗德，禮尤不可已乎？故尊尊所以廣仁，而亦以達義也；親親所以崇孝，而亦以示信也。周道之備，其不在玆乎？茍不闇性與天道，其孰能知之？

春秋

秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕
張道充
translation_en:
… indeed. What moves them to favor us and accept our offerings is sincerity. Can we simply stop here? We must remain vigilant in our resolve at every moment and at the first stirring of thought [?], solemnly recognizing the majesty of Heaven’s luminous mandate. Then our spirit may commune with Heaven, and Heaven’s watch over us may never cease. Otherwise, if we are careless for even a moment and indolence arises in our hearts, can we hope that Heaven will continually come to us? Morning and night we must keep our hearts alert, reverently fearing that manifest majesty. Then our hearts may accord with King Wen’s, and his acceptance of our offerings may be unending. Otherwise, if we lack reverence for even an instant and arrogance arises in our hearts, can we ensure that King Wen will forever grant us peace? Ah! Here we see that the people of Zhou never ceased to revere Heaven and emulate their ancestors; thus everything they did was a means of praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. How could the sacrifice in the Hall of Light have been an empty observance!

Nevertheless, sacrifices must not become irreverently frequent: excessive repetition is undesirable. At the sacrifice in the southern suburb, Hou Ji was already honored as the associate of Heaven. Why, then, was King Wen also made Heaven’s associate here? A true king’s abundant virtue can transmit its radiance, and his great power can reach far. If something enables us to express our reverence, yet we, possessing all under Heaven, practice parsimony in it, we fall short both in the heart of a benevolent person and in that of a filial son. Moreover, when honoring ancestors for their achievements and ancestral sovereigns for their virtue, how much less may these rites be abandoned! Thus honoring the honored broadens benevolence and also gives expression to righteousness; cherishing one’s kin exalts filial devotion and also demonstrates faithfulness. Does not the completeness of the Zhou Way lie here? Unless one understands human nature and the Way of Heaven [?], who could comprehend this?

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔The fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

By Zhang Daochong.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭羅　批〔有才識有斷制〕
考試官教諭林　批〔詞正理明〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔謹嚴〕
春秋紀兵舉而見伯業之未成望其孚衆志也
甚矣衆志孚而後大業集也伐郳之舉序宋於
首其望齊桓盡孚衆之道與曷爲乎伐郳也宋
公討叛桓伯偕行其序宋下何猶未成乎伯也
何以知之以諸侯之未孚知之今夫天下之勢
之一也誠以喻之則易力以合之斯難桓自北
===
杏有盟于鄄兩會欲長諸夏伯圖漸張雖王迹
已熄而天下尚知宗周故桓伯初起而疑信之
者過半是伐也奉號令以馳驅聽指揮而左右
初不嫌于屈焉蓋前乎此者宋雖見從尚懐會
伐之嫌後乎此者鄭復間好敢肆侵宋之逆且
魯又人望也如齊一舉締好方新夫郳宋役也
馬首是瞻乃爲宋以討叛魯宋黨也率賦以從
欲因魯以結宋吾意其經營圖謀期得上公之
歡心以風動乎小國謙巳下人欲因近者之孚
punctuated:
同考試官教諭羅批〔有才識，有斷制。〕
考試官教諭林批〔詞正理明。〕
考試官教諭敖批〔謹嚴。〕
春秋紀兵舉而見伯業之未成，望其孚衆志也甚矣！衆志孚而後大業集也。伐郳之舉，序宋於首，其望齊桓盡孚衆之道與？曷爲乎伐郳也？宋公討叛，桓伯偕行。其序宋下，何？猶未成乎伯也。何以知之？以諸侯之未孚知之。今夫天下之勢之一也，誠以喻之則易，力以合之斯難。桓自北杏有盟，于鄄兩會，欲長諸夏，伯圖漸張。雖王迹已熄，而天下尚知宗周，故桓伯初起，而疑信之者過半。是伐也，奉號令以馳驅，聽指揮而左右，初不嫌于屈焉。蓋前乎此者，宋雖見從，尚懐會伐之嫌；後乎此者，鄭復間好，敢肆侵宋之逆。且魯又人望也，如齊一舉，締好方新。夫郳，宋役也，馬首是瞻，乃爲宋以討叛；魯，宋黨也，率賦以從，欲因魯以結宋。吾意其經營圖謀，期得上公之歡心，以風動乎小國，謙巳下人，欲因近者之孚
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Possesses talent and discernment, and exercises decisive judgment.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The language is correct and the reasoning clear.”
Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: “Careful and rigorous.”
In recording this military undertaking, the Spring and Autumn Annals reveals that the hegemonic enterprise was not yet complete. How earnestly it hoped that he would win the confidence of all! Only after winning their confidence could the great enterprise be accomplished. In the expedition against Ni, Song is listed first. Does this not express the hope that Duke Huan of Qi would fully pursue the way of winning everyone’s confidence? Why was Ni attacked? The Duke of Song was suppressing a rebellion, and Huan, the hegemon, accompanied him. Why is Huan listed after Song? Because he had not yet fully established his hegemony. How do we know this? From the fact that the feudal lords had not yet placed their confidence in him.
Now, unifying the forces of the realm is easy if one enlightens people through sincerity, but difficult if one brings them together through force. Beginning with the covenant at Beixing and two meetings at Juan, Huan sought to lead the states of the Chinese realm, and his plans for hegemony gradually expanded. Although the legacy of kingly rule had faded, the realm still knew to honor Zhou. Thus, when Huan’s hegemony first arose, more than half remained uncertain whether to trust him. On this expedition, he hastened to carry out orders and followed directions in every movement, without taking offense at occupying a subordinate position.
Before this, although Song had followed him, it still harbored resentment over the assembled forces’ attack. After this, Zheng again disrupted friendly relations, daring to commit the hostile act of invading Song. Moreover, Lu was a state to which people looked with respect; its ruler’s visit to Qi had only just established friendly relations. Ni was subject to Song and should have followed its lead; Huan therefore suppressed the rebellion on Song’s behalf. Lu was Song’s ally and led its levied forces in attendance; Huan wished to use Lu to secure Song’s friendship. I believe that his arrangements and deliberations aimed to win the goodwill of the senior duke and thereby sway the smaller states. Humbling himself and yielding precedence to others, he wished to build upon the confidence of those nearby …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
喻以協同於四方蓋遑遑焉以恤宗周之闕篤
簡書之義是究是圖眷矣據其迹所伐之國甚
小而事淺所附之宋甚寡而勢弱爲桓仲謀者
當何如其盡宰衆之本以振賜復之舊勳乎故
于玆役而猶序宋下若曰伯業未成所以謀之
之心不能已耳其深望之以爲世道慮也至矣
抑于是時管仲相桓爲政已五年矣懲戒遊逸
寄政軍令是以民皆勉于善而安其居其規模
次第亦可想見惜乎以節制之兵輕爲譚遂之
===
滅諸侯來同而鄭詹之執不旋踵焉律之王者
反身脩德之懿其有愧乎春秋與之也蓋有不
得已焉爾
冬齊高子來盟〔閔公二年〕楚屈完來盟于
師〔僖公四年〕
尉元康
同考試官教諭羅　批〔發明精切〕
考試官教諭林　批〔融會傳意明白可誦〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔詞意俱足〕
punctuated:
喻，以協同於四方。蓋遑遑焉以恤宗周之闕，篤簡書之義，是究是圖，眷矣。據其迹，所伐之國甚小而事淺，所附之宋甚寡而勢弱。爲桓仲謀者，當何如其盡宰衆之本，以振賜復之舊勳乎？故于玆役而猶序宋下，若曰：「伯業未成，所以謀之之心不能已耳。」其深望之以爲世道慮也至矣！抑于是時，管仲相桓，爲政已五年矣。懲戒遊逸，寄政軍令，是以民皆勉于善而安其居。其規模次第亦可想見。惜乎以節制之兵，輕爲譚遂之滅！諸侯來同，而鄭詹之執不旋踵焉。律之王者反身脩德之懿，其有愧乎？春秋與之也，蓋有不得已焉爾。
冬，齊高子來盟〔閔公二年〕。楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕。
尉元康
