考試官教諭敖　批〔詞意俱足〕
translation_en:
…understanding, thereby securing concord throughout the four quarters. He was anxiously concerned to remedy the deficiencies of the Zhou royal house, earnestly upholding the obligations conveyed in its written commands. These he investigated and planned for with devoted concern. Judging by his actions, the state he attacked was very small and the affair of little consequence; Song, to which he attached himself, had few supporters and little strength. What should those advising Duke Huan and Guan Zhong have done to fulfill the fundamental requirements of governing the multitude and revive the former achievements of “bestowal and restoration” [?]? Thus, in recording this campaign, the text still places him below Song, as if to say: “His hegemonic enterprise was not yet accomplished, and his determination to pursue it could not cease.” How profound were its expectations of him, and how complete its concern for the course of the world!
Yet by this time Guan Zhong had assisted Duke Huan in government for five years. He curbed idle pleasures and incorporated civil administration into military ordinances, so that the people all strove toward goodness and lived contentedly in their homes. The scope and sequence of his arrangements can readily be imagined. What a pity that he so lightly used disciplined troops to destroy Tan and Sui! The regional lords came together in concord, yet the arrest of Zhan of Zheng followed almost immediately. Measured against the admirable practice of true kings, who examine themselves and cultivate virtue, did he not fall short? The Spring and Autumn Annals’ approval of him was, after all, a concession compelled by circumstances.
“In winter, Gaozi of Qi came to conclude a covenant.” 〔Second year of Duke Min.〕 “Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant at the army’s encampment.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
Wei Yuankang.
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, commented: 〔The elucidation is precise and incisive.〕
Examiner Lin, Instructor, commented: 〔It integrates the material and conveys its meaning clearly; it merits recitation.〕
Examiner Ao, Instructor, commented: 〔Both expression and meaning are fully realized.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
平內難者伯臣奉使之權服伯義者外臣奉使
之權觀春秋賢傒之定魯進完之服齊皆以其
明臣義而不辱君命也夫魯自慶父搆禍武闈
再釁于是曠年弗戢矣高子奉桓公之命來省
難也蓋欲覘其虛實以行兼國之私非有汲汲
焉申安危繼絕之義也傒乃憫周公之明祀將
湮僖公立焉以正我是急念龜蒙之人心未定
鹿門城焉以安我是遑桓始以利動而傒乃以
義行使魯受平難善鄰之德桓免幸災樂禍之
===
愆賢哉傒之盟魯也故稱子不稱使而曰來盟
權在高子也且桓率八國侵蔡命管仲問楚于
是次陘以待之屈完奉楚成之命來觀師也蓋
姑伺其强弱尚蓄倔强之念非有惴惴焉輸降
心聽命之誠也完乃知戴冀宗周之明德諾以包
茅之賦欲同于夾輔審德力之輕重承以寡君
之願欲附于諸侯成以觀釁爲先而完以效順
是急使齊收攘夷尊主之功楚專輸誠納欵之
美美哉完之盟齊也故以姓氏通不稱使而曰
punctuated:
平內難者，伯臣奉使之權；服伯義者，外臣奉使之權。觀《春秋》賢傒之定魯，進完之服齊，皆以其明臣義而不辱君命也。夫魯自慶父搆禍，武闈再釁，于是曠年弗戢矣。高子奉桓公之命來省難也，蓋欲覘其虛實，以行兼國之私，非有汲汲焉申安危繼絕之義也。傒乃憫周公之明祀將湮，僖公立焉，以正我是急；念龜蒙之人心未定，鹿門城焉，以安我是遑。桓始以利動，而傒乃以義行，使魯受平難善鄰之德，桓免幸災樂禍之愆。賢哉，傒之盟魯也！故稱子，不稱使，而曰「來盟」，權在高子也。
且桓率八國侵蔡，命管仲問楚，于是次陘以待之。屈完奉楚成之命來觀師也，蓋姑伺其强弱，尚蓄倔强之念，非有惴惴焉輸降心聽命之誠也。完乃知戴冀宗周之明德，諾以包茅之賦，欲同于夾輔；審德力之輕重，承以寡君之願，欲附于諸侯。成以觀釁爲先，而完以效順是急，使齊收攘夷尊主之功，楚專輸誠納欵之美。美哉，完之盟齊也！故以姓氏通，不稱使，而曰
translation_en:
To quell internal disorder is an exercise of discretion by a hegemon’s minister serving as an envoy; to submit to a hegemon’s righteousness is an exercise of discretion by a minister from an outside state serving as an envoy. Consider how the Spring and Autumn Annals esteems Xi for stabilizing Lu and accords recognition to Wan for submitting to Qi: both judgments rest on their understanding of a minister’s duty and their not dishonoring their rulers’ commands. Since Qingfu had brought calamity upon Lu, bloodshed had twice occurred within the palace precincts, and the disorder had remained unchecked for years. Master Gao came on Duke Huan’s orders to investigate the troubles. The duke’s intention was presumably to ascertain Lu’s weaknesses and strengths and pursue his private ambition of annexing the state, rather than earnestly to fulfill the righteous duty of securing those in danger and perpetuating a line threatened with extinction. Xi, however, grieved that the illustrious sacrifices to the Duke of Zhou were about to lapse: he established Duke Xi, making the restoration of rightful order in Lu his urgent concern. Mindful that the people around Mounts Gui and Meng were still unsettled, he fortified the Lu Gate, devoting himself to securing their peace. Huan initially acted for advantage, but Xi acted according to righteousness. Thus Lu benefited from his virtue in quelling disorder and fostering good relations between neighboring states, while Huan escaped the fault of delighting in another’s calamity and rejoicing in its misfortune. Worthy indeed was Xi’s covenant with Lu! Accordingly, the Annals calls him “Master,” does not say that he was sent, and states that he “came to make a covenant”: the discretion rested with Master Gao.
Furthermore, Huan led eight states in an invasion of Cai and ordered Guan Zhong to call Chu to account; he then encamped at Xing to await its response. Qu Wan came on the orders of King Cheng of Chu to observe the army. The king presumably wished merely to assess its strength or weakness and still harbored thoughts of defiance; he had no anxious sincerity in offering submission and obeying commands. Wan, however, recognized the illustrious virtue of upholding [?] the ancestral Zhou house. He promised the tribute of bundled mao grass, wishing to join in supporting the royal house; he weighed the relative importance of virtue and force and responded by expressing his ruler’s wishes, seeking association with the other feudal lords. Cheng gave priority to looking for an opening, whereas Wan made a demonstration of obedience his urgent concern. Thus Qi gained the merit of repelling the barbarians and honoring the sovereign, while Chu received full credit for offering sincerity and pledging allegiance. Admirable indeed was Wan’s covenant with Qi! Accordingly, the Annals identifies him by his surname and clan name, does not say that he was sent, and states …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
來盟權在屈完也吁使人臣而知此義可以廣
君人之德識奉使之道此固聖人之意乎由是
觀之君制命者臣守義者君人者必得正己物
正之臣與之論道經邦斯能以義制事而命令
信人臣必能道濟智周不以成敗利鈍移易其
心斯咸有一德如書傳所紀皆在我矣惜乎傒
完二子器局淺而習染深不足以副春秋期待
之深意焉
禮記
===
處其所存禮之序也
徐養相
同考試官教諭劉　批〔此題上言聖人所以制禮下言斯民所以由禮作者多不以處存爲制禮〕
〔不知所處者何事殊爲欠通此作認理親切而措詞不苟蓋深於禮者〕
考試官教諭林　批〔雄渾典雅可以爲文矣〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔詞嚴義正宜錄以式〕
記者推聖人制禮之原而因及禮之所由定也
punctuated:
來盟，權在屈完也。吁！使人臣而知此義，可以廣君人之德，識奉使之道，此固聖人之意乎？由是觀之，君制命者，臣守義者。君人者必得正己物正之臣，與之論道經邦，斯能以義制事而命令信；人臣必能道濟智周，不以成敗利鈍移易其心，斯咸有一德。如書傳所紀，皆在我矣。惜乎傒、完二子，器局淺而習染深，不足以副春秋期待之深意焉！

禮記

處其所存，禮之序也。

徐養相

同考試官教諭劉批〔此題上言聖人所以制禮，下言斯民所以由禮。作者多不以處存爲制禮〕〔不知所處者何事，殊爲欠通。此作認理親切，而措詞不苟，蓋深於禮者。〕

考試官教諭林批〔雄渾典雅，可以爲文矣。〕

考試官教諭敖批〔詞嚴義正，宜錄以式。〕

記者推聖人制禮之原，而因及禮之所由定也。
translation_en:
…“came to conclude a covenant”: the authority lay with Qu Wan. Ah! If ministers understood this principle, they could enlarge their ruler’s virtue and understand the proper conduct of an envoy. Was this not indeed the Sage’s intention? Viewed in this light, the ruler issues commands, while the minister upholds righteousness. A ruler must obtain ministers who rectify themselves and thereby rectify others, and discuss the Way and the governance of the state with them. Only then can he regulate affairs through righteousness and make his commands trustworthy. Ministers must possess a Way adequate to their tasks and comprehensive wisdom, never changing their resolve because of success or failure, favorable or unfavorable circumstances. Only then will all share a single virtue. What the Documents and commentaries record will thus all lie within our own power. Alas, Xi and Wan were limited in capacity and deeply affected by acquired habits; they could not fulfill the profound expectations embodied in the Spring and Autumn Annals!

Record of Rites

“To place things where they belong is the proper ordering of ritual.”

Xu Yangxiang

Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “The first part of this topic concerns how the sages established ritual; the latter concerns how the people follow ritual. Most writers do not understand ‘placing’ and ‘preserving’ as referring to the establishment of ritual. They do not know what it is that is being placed, showing a marked lack of comprehension. This essay grasps the principle closely and expresses it with care. Its author clearly has a deep understanding of ritual.”

Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “Powerful and full-bodied, classically refined and elegant: this merits the name of literary composition.”

Examiner Ao, an Instructor, comments: “Its language is rigorous and its meaning correct. It should be recorded as a model.”

The compiler of the Record traces the source from which the sages established ritual and thus proceeds to discuss the basis upon which ritual was determined.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
蓋造化禮之原也以是制禮者而復何疑於天
下哉此可以見聖人參竝之實矣記者欲人君
求端於天也故言此以爲聖人所以參竝造化
者夫旣在於治政矣而治政安在哉亦曰禮而
已蓋天地之闔闢雖無言矣而固禮之所由始
也聖人欲殺以降命也則仰觀俯察於天高地
下之間鬼神之屈伸雖無形矣而固禮之所由
寓也聖人欲揭以示人也則極深研幾於萬物
散殊之內本高卑之體形之而爲倫理之別焉
===
經畫區處皆所以體天地之撰乎本殊散之理
昭之而爲節文之著焉衆伍錯綜皆所以建陰
陽之情乎如此而禮有不達者哉蓋作之者非
出於一己之私則有以盡天下之制而所以防
範人情者皆約之於中正不易之規出之者不
鑿以一人之智則有以盡天下之倫而所以綱
維世變者皆律之以常久不已之則大而倫理
之分至不齊也而性命之各正以類聚者以羣
分矣是何也聖人本天地以成能而自不出其
punctuated: 蓋造化，禮之原也。以是制禮者，而復何疑於天下哉？此可以見聖人參竝之實矣。記者欲人君求端於天也，故言此以爲聖人所以參竝造化者。夫旣在於治政矣，而治政安在哉？亦曰禮而已。蓋天地之闔闢雖無言矣，而固禮之所由始也。聖人欲殺以降命也，則仰觀俯察於天高地下之間；鬼神之屈伸雖無形矣，而固禮之所由寓也。聖人欲揭以示人也，則極深研幾於萬物散殊之內。本高卑之體，形之而爲倫理之別焉，經畫區處，皆所以體天地之撰乎！本殊散之理，昭之而爲節文之著焉，衆伍錯綜，皆所以建陰陽之情乎！如此而禮有不達者哉？蓋作之者非出於一己之私，則有以盡天下之制，而所以防範人情者，皆約之於中正不易之規；出之者不鑿以一人之智，則有以盡天下之倫，而所以綱維世變者，皆律之以常久不已之則。大而倫理之分，至不齊也，而性命之各正，以類聚者以羣分矣。是何也？聖人本天地以成能，而自不出其
translation_en:
For the creative transformations of nature are the source of ritual. When ritual is established on this basis, what further doubts can there be concerning its application throughout the world? Here we can see the substance of the sages’ standing alongside Heaven and Earth. The author of the Record wishes rulers to seek the beginnings in Heaven, and therefore speaks of this as the means by which the sages stand alongside the creative transformations of nature. This indeed lies in governing; but wherein does governing lie? Simply in ritual.

Though Heaven and Earth open and close without speech, they are assuredly the source from which ritual begins. When the sages wish to issue commands in graded measure, they look upward and examine downward, between Heaven above and Earth below. Though the withdrawing and extending of ghosts and spirits have no visible form, they are assuredly where ritual resides. When the sages wish to reveal it and display it to the people, they probe the depths and investigate the incipient workings within the manifold diversity of things. Taking the disposition of high and low as their basis, they give it form in the distinctions of human relationships: their planning and ordering all embody the workings of Heaven and Earth! Taking the principle of diversity as their basis, they make it manifest in the observable refinements and gradations of ritual: their grouping and interweaving all establish the inherent patterns of yin and yang! With this being so, could ritual fail to reach anywhere?

Since those who create it do not proceed from their own private interests, they can encompass all the institutions of the world; the means by which they restrain human feelings thus bring them within balanced, correct, and unchanging standards. Since those who promulgate it do not contrive it through one person’s ingenuity, they can encompass all the relationships of the world; the means by which they hold changing social conditions in order thus regulate them by enduring and unceasing rules. On the larger scale, the distinctions of human relationships are unequal in the extreme; yet each being’s nature and allotted destiny find their proper place, and those gathered according to kind are differentiated according to group. Why is this? The sages take Heaven and Earth as their foundation in bringing their capacities to fulfillment, and naturally do not go beyond their…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
範圍之外耳小而節文之著至不一也而等級
之甚嚴其統同者其辨異矣是何也聖人本萬
物以順治而自不能出其曲成之外耳是則禮
制於上見聖人效法之有本禮達於下見聖人
成功之有合此其所以參天地而竝鬼神也而
豈徒哉雖然此固人君法天之事也然所謂天
者理而已天地覆載陰陽往來固莫非天也而
謂天專在是焉則末也古人有見於此出王游
衍樂且不違基命宥密畏天者也蓋眞有以識
此矣噫天其可以他求哉
===
作者之謂聖
李惟勤
同考試官教諭劉　批〔聖人所知者情也所作者由情以達文也似不難解及至作文往往混而無〕
別明白簡潔如此篇者可謂知作者之心矣
考試官教諭林　批〔平淡中有餘味可嘉可嘉〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔精切簡當非苟作者〕
樂記於禮樂之創始者而定之以極至之名焉
punctuated:
範圍之外耳。小而節文之著，至不一也，而等級之甚嚴，其統同者，其辨異矣。是何也？聖人本萬物以順治，而自不能出其曲成之外耳。是則禮制於上，見聖人效法之有本；禮達於下，見聖人成功之有合。此其所以參天地而竝鬼神也，而豈徒哉！雖然，此固人君法天之事也。然所謂天者，理而已。天地覆載，陰陽往來，固莫非天也，而謂天專在是焉，則末也。古人有見於此，出王游衍，樂且不違；基命宥密，畏天者也。蓋眞有以識此矣。噫！天其可以他求哉！

作者之謂聖
李惟勤

同考試官教諭劉，批〔聖人所知者，情也；所作者，由情以達文也。似不難解，及至作文，往往混而無〕別。明白簡潔如此篇者，可謂知作者之心矣。
考試官教諭林，批〔平淡中有餘味，可嘉！可嘉！〕
考試官教諭敖，批〔精切簡當，非苟作者。〕

樂記於禮樂之創始者，而定之以極至之名焉。
translation_en:
…beyond those bounds. In their finer details, the manifest forms and embellishments of ritual are exceedingly diverse, yet their gradations are rigorously ordered: they unite what is alike and distinguish what is different. Why is this? The sages take the myriad things as their basis in bringing about orderly governance, and cannot themselves go beyond the process of bringing each to fulfillment according to its particular nature. Thus, ritual established above shows that the sages have a foundation for what they emulate; ritual extending below shows that their achievements accord with that foundation. This is how they form a triad with Heaven and Earth and stand alongside ghosts and spirits. How could this be without substance? Nevertheless, this is indeed the ruler’s task of modeling himself on Heaven. Yet what is called Heaven is simply principle. Heaven’s covering and Earth’s bearing, and the coming and going of yin and yang, are certainly all manifestations of Heaven; but to say that Heaven resides exclusively in these is to attend only to the periphery. The ancients understood this: in going forth and roaming [?], they rejoiced without transgressing; in establishing the foundation of their mandate with profound tranquility, they stood in awe of Heaven. They truly understood this. Ah! Can Heaven be sought elsewhere?

“He Who Creates Is Called a Sage”
By Li Weiqin

Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “What the sage understands is the essential nature of things; what he creates proceeds from that essential nature to its formal expression. This seems easy enough to explain, yet when people come to write essays, they frequently confuse the two without distinguishing them. An essay as clear and concise as this may be said to understand the creator’s mind.”
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “Within its plainness there is a lingering richness. Admirable! Admirable!”
Examiner Ao, an Instructor, comments: “Precise, penetrating, concise, and apt: this is no carelessly composed work.”

The Record of Music bestows upon those who first created rites and music a designation expressing the highest attainment.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
蓋禮樂之道至大而自我作始焉固亦難矣非
天下之至聖其孰能以與於此且夫至難知者
禮樂之情也至難作者禮樂之事也旣識情而
能作矣謂之作者本其所先覺之理而以之議
禮考度焉凡所以嘉天下之會者皆於我乎成
能卽其所獨得之妙而以之審音正律焉凡可
以平天下之情者皆於我乎托始雖曰起先王
之所未有而所以開物成務者此也雖曰創曠
古之所未聞而所以繼天立極者此也若此者
===
不特作之爲君可以臨天下而已而其性之所
賦夫固聰明睿智之盡者也不特作之爲師可
以覺天下而已而其中之所涵夫固仁義中正
之極者也內妙聖敬之躋外觀會通之典而凡
儀文之設皆幾微爲之妙應也不曰天縱之將
聖乎而何以能創所未有如此也心建中和之
極耳妙聲氣之元而凡音律之正皆天機爲之
默契也不曰聖其合德矣乎而何以能開所未
聞如此也是聖人之未作也而道在天地聖人
punctuated: 蓋禮樂之道至大，而自我作始焉，固亦難矣。非天下之至聖，其孰能以與於此？且夫至難知者，禮樂之情也；至難作者，禮樂之事也。旣識情而能作矣，謂之作者，本其所先覺之理，而以之議禮考度焉，凡所以嘉天下之會者，皆於我乎成能；卽其所獨得之妙，而以之審音正律焉，凡可以平天下之情者，皆於我乎托始。雖曰起先王之所未有，而所以開物成務者，此也；雖曰創曠古之所未聞，而所以繼天立極者，此也。若此者，不特作之爲君，可以臨天下而已，而其性之所賦，夫固聰明睿智之盡者也；不特作之爲師，可以覺天下而已，而其中之所涵，夫固仁義中正之極者也。內妙聖敬之躋，外觀會通之典，而凡儀文之設，皆幾微爲之妙應也。不曰天縱之將聖乎？而何以能創所未有如此也？心建中和之極，耳妙聲氣之元，而凡音律之正，皆天機爲之默契也。不曰聖其合德矣乎？而何以能開所未聞如此也？是聖人之未作也，而道在天地；聖人
translation_en:
For the Way of rites and music is supremely great, and to originate it oneself is indeed difficult. Who but the utmost sage in all the world could participate in this? Moreover, what is most difficult to understand is the underlying nature of rites and music; what is most difficult to create is their practical expression. Having understood their nature and become capable of creating them, one is called a creator. Drawing upon the principles to which he has awakened before others, he deliberates upon rites and examines standards: all that brings excellence to the gatherings of the world finds its full realization in him. Drawing upon the subtleties that he alone has grasped, he scrutinizes tones and rectifies pitch standards: all that can bring harmony to the feelings of the world takes its beginning from him. Though this may be called bringing forth what the former kings never possessed, it is through this that he discloses the nature of things and brings undertakings to completion. Though this may be called creating what had never been heard of throughout antiquity, it is through this that he carries on Heaven’s work and establishes the supreme standard.
Such a person does more than arise as a ruler capable of presiding over the world: the endowment of his nature embodies the fullest perceptiveness, clarity, sagacity, and wisdom. He does more than arise as a teacher capable of awakening the world: what he holds within embodies the utmost benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness. Inwardly, he wondrously attains ever greater sagely reverence; outwardly, he observes the canons that comprehend and connect all things. Every ceremonial form he institutes is a wondrous response to the subtlest incipient movements. Is he not what is called a great sage endowed by Heaven? How else could he create what had never existed in this way? His mind establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony; his ear wondrously apprehends the source of sound and vital energy. Every correction of tones and pitch standards silently accords with the workings of Heaven. Is he not what is called a sage whose virtue accords with Heaven? How else could he bring forth what had never been heard of in this way? Thus, before the sage arises, the Way resides in Heaven and Earth; the sage …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之旣作也而道在禮樂然則聖人其天地矣而
豈述者所能擬議之哉抑觀聖王之制作以經
世也周自平王而後王道不行雖述者之明亦
不可復得由是而經世之意微矣夫子斟酌四
代之禮樂而發之顔子固萬世常行之典也道
在而位不在焉作者之難不其然乎必有聖人
之德而在天子之位然後可
第貳場
論
===
聖人法天立道
魯邦彦
同考試官教諭葛　批　氣象恢宏詞意雅健讀
之有一倡三歎之遺音焉高薦何忝
同考試官教諭周　批　發揚題意滾滾千餘言
有才氣有學識敬服敬服
考試官教諭林　批　通篇論議不出乎本題
之外非留心經史而有得者耶
考試官教諭敖　批　步驟不𣈆議論豐出眞
punctuated:
之旣作也，而道在禮樂。然則聖人其天地矣，而豈述者所能擬議之哉？抑觀聖王之制作以經世也，周自平王而後，王道不行，雖述者之明，亦不可復得，由是而經世之意微矣。夫子斟酌四代之禮樂，而發之顔子，固萬世常行之典也。道在而位不在焉，作者之難，不其然乎？必有聖人之德，而在天子之位，然後可。
第貳場
論
聖人法天立道
魯邦彦
同考試官教諭葛批：氣象恢宏，詞意雅健，讀之有一倡三歎之遺音焉，高薦何忝？
同考試官教諭周批：發揚題意，滾滾千餘言，有才氣，有學識，敬服，敬服！
考試官教諭林批：通篇論議，不出乎本題之外，非留心經史而有得者耶？
考試官教諭敖批：步驟不𣈆，議論豐出，眞
translation_en:
…once the sage has arisen, the Way resides in rites and music. Thus the sage is indeed like Heaven and Earth: how could a transmitter presume to fathom or discuss him? Consider, moreover, how sage kings created institutions to order the world. In the Zhou dynasty, from King Ping onward, the kingly Way was no longer practiced; even the discernment of a transmitter could no longer be found. Consequently, the purpose of ordering the world grew obscure. The Master weighed the rites and music of the four dynasties and expounded them to Yanzi: these were assuredly enduring norms to be practiced for ten thousand generations. He possessed the Way but lacked the position. Is this not precisely the difficulty faced by an originator? Only one who possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of the Son of Heaven can accomplish this.

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Models Himself on Heaven and Establishes the Way”
Lu Bangyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: “Its scope is expansive, and its language and ideas are refined and vigorous. Reading it, one hears lingering echoes of ‘one voice leading and three responding.’ How could recommending it highly be undeserved?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “It develops the meaning of the topic in a torrent of more than a thousand words. It displays talent and vigor, learning and insight. Admirable, admirable!”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Throughout the piece, the argument never strays beyond the topic. Is this not the work of someone who has devoted himself to the classics and histories and gained understanding from them?”

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: “Its progression does not advance [?], and its arguments emerge abundantly. Truly …”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
高古之作也宜錄
道其原於天乎聖人之治天下憲諸天而已矣
夫仁者天之道也聖人者道之管也天以仁覆
萬物而不有其迹是故天下之物取足於天之
化而忘其爲仁聖人生萬民而其道與天並是
故天下亦囿於聖人之仁而不知其同于天故
其道始大而與天爲一也苟然以有我之私則
與天道不相似而至仁之用幾於息矣然則聖
人之所以治天下其諸憲天之道而不私者乎
===
今夫立天之道曰陰曰陽而已陽之舒也而爲
春爲夏有生殖之道焉固仁之所以出也陰之
慘也而爲秋爲冬有振耀之德焉固義之所以
出也斡流而不息闔闢而不窮顯仁藏用而不
匱天何嘗有心於物而爲之者耶然喙息蠕動
根著之物自是廣育各正不相假借天道之大
於是乎不可測矣聖人者作將以承天之道立
人之極齊物之軌其責負爲甚重而天下之紛
紛焉相率而求以遂其欲使無以副其望亦或
punctuated:
高古之作也，宜錄。
道其原於天乎？聖人之治天下，憲諸天而已矣。夫仁者，天之道也；聖人者，道之管也。天以仁覆萬物而不有其迹，是故天下之物取足於天之化而忘其爲仁。聖人生萬民而其道與天並，是故天下亦囿於聖人之仁而不知其同于天，故其道始大而與天爲一也。苟然以有我之私，則與天道不相似，而至仁之用幾於息矣。然則聖人之所以治天下，其諸憲天之道而不私者乎？
今夫立天之道，曰陰曰陽而已。陽之舒也，而爲春爲夏，有生殖之道焉，固仁之所以出也；陰之慘也，而爲秋爲冬，有振耀之德焉，固義之所以出也。斡流而不息，闔闢而不窮，顯仁藏用而不匱。天何嘗有心於物而爲之者耶？然喙息蠕動、根著之物，自是廣育，各正，不相假借。天道之大，於是乎不可測矣。聖人者作，將以承天之道，立人之極，齊物之軌，其責負爲甚重。而天下之紛紛焉，相率而求以遂其欲，使無以副其望，亦或
translation_en:
…a work of lofty, antique character. It merits inclusion.
Does not the Way originate in Heaven? In governing all under Heaven, the sage simply takes Heaven as his model. Benevolence is Heaven’s Way; the sage is the conduit of that Way. Heaven shelters the myriad things with benevolence without leaving any trace of doing so. Thus the things under Heaven find all they need in Heaven’s transforming activity and remain unaware of its benevolence. The sage sustains the myriad people, and his Way stands alongside Heaven’s. Thus all under Heaven likewise dwell within the sage’s benevolence without knowing that it accords with Heaven. Only then does his Way become great and one with Heaven. If he harbors the selfish partiality of an individual ego, he ceases to resemble Heaven’s Way, and the workings of perfect benevolence almost come to a halt. Is not the sage’s means of governing all under Heaven, then, to model himself on Heaven’s Way without partiality?
What establishes Heaven’s Way is simply yin and yang. Yang unfolds as spring and summer, embodying the way of generation and growth: this is indeed the source of benevolence. Yin’s severity produces autumn and winter, possessing an awe-inspiring power: this is indeed the source of righteousness. Heaven revolves and flows without rest, closes and opens without end, manifests benevolence and conceals its workings without exhaustion. When has Heaven ever acted upon things with deliberate intent? Yet creatures that breathe through mouths or crawl, and things fixed by roots, thereby flourish abundantly, each attaining its proper nature without borrowing from the others. In this the greatness of Heaven’s Way is beyond fathoming. The sage arises to carry forward Heaven’s Way, establish the highest standard for humanity, and set the course of things in order. His responsibility is exceedingly weighty. Meanwhile, the multitudes under Heaven follow one another in seeking to satisfy their desires. If he has no means to fulfill their expectations, or perhaps…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
肆其臆見強爲法制以把持之欲天下之順吾
治吾知其必不能矣聖人憲天以爲聰明固不
敢妄有所事以絶天下之望亦豈敢自諉而不
爲之所以負上天付托之重哉吾知其承天之
意以爲民用者固有所不容已焉耳自今觀之
六府三事之脩以遂民之生也五典之惇以成
民之性也五禮之庸以防民之欲也勞來匡直
以翼民之行也物采之彰藝極之陳以端民之
趨也五服之命以彰民之有德也五刑之用以
===
罰民之有罪也聖人所以爲民之道若是亦旣
詳且備矣或者曰聖人之所以愛養者仁吾民
者也刑罰者適以戕吾民而非聖人之仁也若
無與於天也不知天道至大至正不能以獨運
不得不待聖人以成其能而聖人敦大覆正亦
兢兢焉以奉若乎天道愛養刑罰之用一皆代
天而行之一毫有我之私不與焉至有殺之而
不怨及刑期於無刑卒以成其愛而後能使天
下被聖人之仁於無窮所以爲仁也夫道者天
punctuated:
肆其臆見，強爲法制以把持之，欲天下之順吾治，吾知其必不能矣。聖人憲天以爲聰明，固不敢妄有所事以絶天下之望，亦豈敢自諉而不爲之，所以負上天付托之重哉？吾知其承天之意以爲民用者，固有所不容已焉耳。自今觀之，六府三事之脩，以遂民之生也；五典之惇，以成民之性也；五禮之庸，以防民之欲也；勞來匡直，以翼民之行也；物采之彰、藝極之陳，以端民之趨也；五服之命，以彰民之有德也；五刑之用，以罰民之有罪也。聖人所以爲民之道若是，亦旣詳且備矣。
或者曰：「聖人之所以愛養者，仁吾民者也；刑罰者，適以戕吾民，而非聖人之仁也，若無與於天也。」不知天道至大至正，不能以獨運，不得不待聖人以成其能，而聖人敦大覆正，亦兢兢焉以奉若乎天道。愛養刑罰之用，一皆代天而行之，一毫有我之私不與焉。至有殺之而不怨，及刑期於無刑，卒以成其愛，而後能使天下被聖人之仁於無窮，所以爲仁也。夫道者，天
translation_en:
…give free rein to their own conjectures and forcibly establish laws and institutions to keep the people under control, wishing all under Heaven to submit to their government—I know that they assuredly cannot succeed. The sage takes Heaven as his model in exercising discernment. He certainly dares not act recklessly and thereby dash the hopes of all under Heaven; how, then, could he dare evade his responsibility and do nothing, thereby betraying the weighty trust that Heaven has placed in him? I know that, in carrying out Heaven’s intent for the people’s benefit, there are things he cannot refrain from doing. Consider this now: putting the six resources and three undertakings in order enables the people to sustain their lives; strengthening the five ethical relationships brings their nature to fulfillment; employing the five rites restrains their desires; encouraging, drawing them near, correcting, and straightening them supports their conduct; displaying ceremonial distinctions and setting forth standards of accomplishment [?] directs their aspirations aright; bestowing the five grades of ceremonial dress honors those among the people who possess virtue; and employing the five punishments chastises those who are guilty. Such are the sage’s ways of acting for the people: they are indeed both detailed and complete.
Someone may say: “The sage’s loving nurture treats our people benevolently. Punishments, however, serve only to injure our people and are no expression of the sage’s benevolence; they seem to have no connection with Heaven.” Such a person does not understand that the Way of Heaven, supremely great and supremely correct, cannot operate alone: it must depend upon the sage to bring its capacities to fruition. The sage, too, in his generous breadth, encompassing care, and rectitude [?], reverently and vigilantly follows the Way of Heaven. In employing loving nurture and punishments alike, he acts entirely on Heaven’s behalf; not the slightest trace of selfish interest enters into it. This extends even to putting people to death without arousing resentment, and to using punishments with the aim of making punishments unnecessary. Ultimately, this fulfills his love; only then can he enable all under Heaven to receive the benefits of the sage’s benevolence without end. This is how he practices benevolence. Now, the Way is Heaven’s …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之用也仁者道之用也聖人者嘗是者也道立
則天用彰仁昭則聖功溥其理一而已矣惟理
之一也故典曰天敘禮曰天秩德曰天命刑曰
天討凡羣動之宜亦不過因美利而導之上下
是何與於聖人耶若果出於聖人之爲則是出
於有我之私而其所以愛也養也爲私恩爲小
惠賞也刑也爲私喜爲私怒其出也無本其究
也易窮而何以立道于天下耶是故其愛養者
聖人之仁也而其所以爲愛養者固天之生長
===
於春夏也陽之舒也刑罰者聖人之義也而其
所以爲刑罰者固天之秋肅也陰之慘也天覆
萬物而無所偏聖人憲天之道亦溥愛而無所
私天無私故能極其大聖人無私故能立其道
而以仁覆天下庶無負於天之所以付托於聖
人之意而天下之所以望於聖人者始爲不孤
矣夫天以是道付之聖人聖人亦能任其責於
我以天之道神天下之化裁成輔相率本於天
之所爲而不敢有所欣戚震懼于天下以孤其
punctuated: 之用也，仁者道之用也，聖人者嘗是者也。道立則天用彰，仁昭則聖功溥，其理一而已矣。惟理之一也，故典曰天敘，禮曰天秩，德曰天命，刑曰天討。凡羣動之宜，亦不過因美利而導之上下，是何與於聖人耶？若果出於聖人之爲，則是出於有我之私，而其所以愛也養也，爲私恩，爲小惠；賞也刑也，爲私喜，爲私怒。其出也無本，其究也易窮，而何以立道于天下耶？是故其愛養者，聖人之仁也，而其所以爲愛養者，固天之生長於春夏也，陽之舒也；刑罰者，聖人之義也，而其所以爲刑罰者，固天之秋肅也，陰之慘也。天覆萬物而無所偏，聖人憲天之道，亦溥愛而無所私。天無私，故能極其大；聖人無私，故能立其道，而以仁覆天下，庶無負於天之所以付托於聖人之意，而天下之所以望於聖人者始爲不孤矣。夫天以是道付之聖人，聖人亦能任其責於我，以天之道神天下之化，裁成輔相，率本於天之所爲，而不敢有所欣戚震懼于天下，以孤其
translation_en: …is the operation of Heaven; benevolence is the operation of the Way; and the sage is one who has experienced these [?]. When the Way is established, Heaven’s operation becomes manifest; when benevolence shines forth, the sage’s achievements extend everywhere. Their underlying principle is one and the same. Precisely because this principle is one, the established norms are called Heaven’s ordering, ritual is called Heaven’s ranking, virtue is called Heaven’s mandate, and punishment is called Heaven’s chastisement. Whatever is fitting for the myriad activities of beings amounts simply to following what benefits them and guiding them above and below. What part in this belongs to the sage himself? If it truly arose from the sage’s own contrivance, it would proceed from selfish partiality: his love and nurture would become personal favors and petty kindnesses, and his rewards and punishments would become expressions of personal pleasure and anger. Such actions would have no foundation at their source and would readily reach their limit in the end. How, then, could they establish the Way throughout the world? Thus, loving and nurturing express the sage’s benevolence, yet what makes such love and nurture possible is indeed Heaven’s generation and growth in spring and summer, the unfolding of yang. Punishments express the sage’s righteousness, yet what makes such punishments possible is indeed Heaven’s autumnal severity, the harshness of yin. Heaven covers the myriad things without partiality; the sage models himself upon Heaven’s Way and likewise extends his love everywhere without favoritism. Because Heaven is impartial, it can realize its greatness to the fullest; because the sage is impartial, he can establish his Way and cover the world with benevolence. In this way he may avoid betraying Heaven’s intention in entrusting its charge to him, and only then will the world’s expectations of the sage remain unfulfilled no longer. Heaven entrusts this Way to the sage, and the sage can take its responsibility upon himself. Through Heaven’s Way, he brings about wondrous transformation throughout the world; in shaping things to completion and assisting their development, he always takes Heaven’s workings as his basis. He dares not give way to joy, sorrow, alarm, or fear concerning the world, thereby disappointing its…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
所望是故其政惻怛而不徇優游而不驟幷覆
包函而不遺卒而天下之治而與天者同其用
故天下之人老有所終少有所養鰥寡孤獨得
其所君臣以義父子以親兄弟以順上下以序
仁誼行而禮節重敎化成而風俗美天下之衆
舉不叛於其道而道立矣由是行帝道而帝者
此也行王道而王者此也爲而不有應而不求
至順而天下治則天與聖人爲一而法天之能
事畢矣故曰聖人之治天下憲諸天而已矣雖
然憲天豈易言哉必有純天之德而後有格天
===
之心有格天之心而後有憲天之治有憲天之
治而後有同天之功若昔大猷時雍風動神化
極矣嗣東周以後王者迹熄道術遂裂衣漢武帝
承秦之敝不能洗而除之乃廢先王德敎之官
而專任執法之吏蓋至是而法天立道之意荒
矣宜有以激仲舒之爲是言也治天下者能鑒
於玆存至公無我之心體天地至仁之道以溥
其德愛於天下而不徒事乎法制文爲之末則
punctuated:
所望。是故其政惻怛而不徇，優游而不驟，幷覆包函而不遺。卒而天下之治，而與天者同其用。故天下之人，老有所終，少有所養，鰥寡孤獨得其所；君臣以義，父子以親，兄弟以順，上下以序。仁誼行而禮節重，敎化成而風俗美，天下之衆舉不叛於其道，而道立矣。由是行帝道而帝者，此也；行王道而王者，此也。爲而不有，應而不求，至順而天下治，則天與聖人爲一，而法天之能事畢矣。故曰：「聖人之治天下，憲諸天而已矣。」
雖然，憲天豈易言哉？必有純天之德，而後有格天之心；有格天之心，而後有憲天之治；有憲天之治，而後有同天之功。若昔大猷時雍，風動神化，極矣。嗣東周以後，王者迹熄，道術遂裂。衣漢武帝承秦之敝，不能洗而除之，乃廢先王德敎之官，而專任執法之吏。蓋至是而法天立道之意荒矣，宜有以激仲舒之爲是言也。治天下者能鑒於玆，存至公無我之心，體天地至仁之道，以溥其德愛於天下，而不徒事乎法制文爲之末，則
translation_en:
…what they hope for. Thus his government is compassionate without being indulgent, unhurried without being precipitous, encompassing and sheltering all without omission. Ultimately, the ordering of the realm has the same operation as Heaven. Thus, among the people of the realm, the old have provision to the end of their lives, the young are nurtured, and widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless elderly each find their proper place. Ruler and minister are bound by righteousness, father and son by affection, elder and younger brothers by concord, and superiors and inferiors by due order. Benevolence and righteousness prevail, ritual observances are honored, moral instruction takes effect, and customs become admirable. None of the multitude throughout the realm turns against his Way, and the Way is established. This is how those who practice the Way of the ancient emperors become emperors, and those who practice the kingly Way become kings. Acting without possessing, responding without seeking anything, he brings the realm to order through perfect accord. Heaven and the sage then become one, and the work of taking Heaven as a model is complete. Hence it is said: “In governing the realm, the sage simply takes Heaven as his model.”
Nevertheless, how could taking Heaven as a model be a matter lightly spoken of? Only with virtue as pure as Heaven can one possess a heart that reaches Heaven; only with a heart that reaches Heaven can one establish government modeled on Heaven; and only with government modeled on Heaven can one achieve accomplishments equal to Heaven’s. In antiquity, the great Way brought harmony to the age; its influence moved like the wind and transformed like a spirit—this was the utmost achievement. From the Eastern Zhou onward, the traces of true kingship faded, and the teachings of the Way consequently fragmented. [?] Emperor Wu of Han inherited the abuses of Qin but could not cleanse and remove them. Instead, he abolished the offices through which the former kings had imparted virtue and moral instruction, and relied exclusively on officials who enforced the law. By this point, the intent of modeling oneself on Heaven and establishing the Way had fallen into neglect. It is understandable that this should have stirred Zhongshu to make these statements. If those who govern the realm can take warning from this, preserve a heart of utmost impartiality and selflessness, embody the Way of the supreme benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and thereby extend their virtue and love throughout the realm, rather than merely occupying themselves with the secondary details of laws, institutions, and formal observances, then…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
所以求厎民生導迎善氣而祈天凝命之本在
是矣唐虞之治豈得專美於前也哉
同前
牛若愚
同考試官教諭毛　批　此作以乾卦月令發明
法天立道義甚眞切且篇末歸重董子正心之說
尤爲有見擅場之作也宜錄以式
同考試官教諭黃　批　天道之春生秋殺同歸
于仁聖人仁育義正皆法乎天乃董子闡道扶
時本意此作援引經傳發明聖同天之意一一
詳盡且體裁高古豈讀漢文而有得者乎錄之
===
以竝三策
考試官教諭林　批　就題立論而切近精實
意自無窮殆如有制之兵而操縱闔闢舉在吾手
子其學博而取約者與允宜高薦
考試官教諭敖　批　是題場中作者類多浮
襲時言敷演成文麈雜可厭此篇援經質史順題
發明反覆千言英華疊出蓋造詣精邃不可以時
punctuated:
所以求厎民生、導迎善氣而祈天凝命之本，在是矣。唐虞之治，豈得專美於前也哉？

同前。
牛若愚。

同考試官教諭毛批：此作以乾卦、月令發明法天立道，義甚眞切。且篇末歸重董子正心之說，尤爲有見，擅場之作也，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭黃批：天道之春生秋殺，同歸于仁；聖人仁育義正，皆法乎天，乃董子闡道扶時本意。此作援引經傳，發明聖同天之意，一一詳盡。且體裁高古，豈讀漢文而有得者乎？錄之以竝三策。

考試官教諭林批：就題立論，而切近精實，意自無窮。殆如有制之兵，而操縱闔闢，舉在吾手。子其學博而取約者與？允宜高薦。

考試官教諭敖批：是題場中作者，類多浮襲時言，敷演成文，麈雜可厭。此篇援經質史，順題發明，反覆千言，英華疊出。蓋造詣精邃，不可以時
translation_en:
…Herein lies the foundation for seeking to bring stability to the people's livelihood, ushering in auspicious influences, and praying to Heaven to secure its mandate. How, then, could the rule of Tang and Yu alone claim preeminence in antiquity?

Same topic as above.
Niu Ruoyu.

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: This composition uses the Qian hexagram and the Monthly Ordinances to elucidate how to take Heaven as one's model and establish the Way. Its meaning is most true and apposite. Moreover, its conclusion places particular weight on Master Dong's teaching concerning the rectification of the heart, showing exceptional insight. This is a composition that surpasses its competitors and should be recorded as a model.

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The Way of Heaven brings forth life in spring and kills in autumn; both alike conduce to benevolence. The sage nurtures through benevolence and corrects through righteousness, in both respects taking Heaven as his model. This was Master Dong's original intention in elucidating the Way and sustaining his age. This composition cites the classics and their commentaries to explain how the sage accords with Heaven, treating every point thoroughly. Its form and style are also lofty and antique. Could its author have gained this understanding from reading Han prose? Record it alongside the three policy essays.

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: The argument is grounded in the topic, closely pertinent, precise, and substantial, yet inexhaustible in its implications. It is almost like a well-disciplined army: its deployment and withdrawal, its closing and opening of ranks, are all in one's hands. Are you not one whose learning is broad but whose selection is concise? You certainly deserve recommendation at a high rank.

Examiner Ao, Instructor, comments: Most candidates writing on this topic in the examination hall superficially imitate current expressions and elaborate them into compositions, producing a tiresome, dusty jumble [?]. title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
士之文曰子也敬服敬服
聖人之仁天下其事甚詳而其爲道甚約也何
也聖人承天意理萬物視天下弗獲其所誠若
恫瘝其身凡吾政教慶恵惟恐旦發而夕不至
也况天下求仁於吾者意甚切至吾將慱觀遠
覽靡所究竟雖竭智畢議而天下無少裨益則
豈所以奉神靈之統而操化理之術哉乃思曰
吾位天位理天職期以與致太平甚盛而吾所
爲有不求端於天則謬矣於是法天立道天無
===
私吾亦無私天以生道仁萬物吾亦以生道仁
萬物則操約施慱太平可立致矣夫所謂法天
者何聖人始作設卦觀象六陽之卦其名爲乾
乾者天道故其辭曰元亨利貞以此見天之道
大通至正溥愛而無私也孔子析爲四德明君
人之道凖於四序故元爲春爲仁亨爲夏爲禮
利爲秋爲義貞爲冬爲智惟元兼總四者故曰
乾始能以美利利天下不言所利明君人體元
之義亦溥愛而無私也今夫天之於物必有日
punctuated:
士之文曰子也。敬服，敬服！

聖人之仁天下，其事甚詳，而其爲道甚約也，何也？聖人承天意，理萬物，視天下弗獲其所，誠若恫瘝其身。凡吾政教慶恵，惟恐旦發而夕不至也。况天下求仁於吾者，意甚切至，吾將慱觀遠覽，靡所究竟，雖竭智畢議，而天下無少裨益，則豈所以奉神靈之統而操化理之術哉？乃思曰：「吾位天位，理天職，期以與致太平甚盛，而吾所爲有不求端於天，則謬矣。」於是法天立道。天無私，吾亦無私；天以生道仁萬物，吾亦以生道仁萬物，則操約施慱，太平可立致矣。夫所謂法天者何？聖人始作，設卦觀象，六陽之卦，其名爲乾。乾者，天道，故其辭曰：「元亨利貞。」以此見天之道，大通至正，溥愛而無私也。孔子析爲四德，明君人之道凖於四序。故元爲春爲仁，亨爲夏爲禮，利爲秋爲義，貞爲冬爲智。惟元兼總四者，故曰：「乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利。」明君人體元之義，亦溥愛而無私也。今夫天之於物，必有日
translation_en:
…judge your work as the writing of ordinary scholars [?]. I am deeply impressed—deeply impressed!

The sage’s benevolence toward all under Heaven involves exceedingly numerous particulars, yet the Way by which he practices it is exceedingly simple. Why is this? The sage receives Heaven’s intent and orders the myriad things. When he sees anyone under Heaven failing to find their proper place, he feels it truly as pain and suffering in his own body. In all his government, instruction, rewards, and acts of kindness, his sole fear is that what he issues at dawn may not reach the people by evening. Moreover, those under Heaven who seek benevolence from him are most earnest in their desire. If he were to survey broadly and look far afield without reaching any conclusion, then, even if he exhausted his intelligence and deliberated to the utmost, he would bring not the slightest benefit to the realm. How could this be the means of upholding the authority entrusted by the divine powers and wielding the arts of transforming and governing?

He therefore reflects: “The position I occupy is Heaven’s position; the duties I discharge are Heaven’s duties. I aspire thereby to bring about the utmost flourishing of Great Peace. If anything I do fails to seek its source in Heaven, I shall be in error.” Thus he models himself on Heaven and establishes the Way. Heaven has no partiality; neither does he. Heaven extends benevolence to the myriad things through the Way of generating life; he too extends benevolence to the myriad things through that Way. By holding to what is simple and applying it broadly, Great Peace can be brought about at once.

What, then, does modeling oneself on Heaven mean? When the sage first undertook his work, he established the hexagrams and contemplated their images. The hexagram consisting of six yang lines is named Qian. Qian is the Way of Heaven; hence its text says: “Origination, free course, benefit, and constancy.” This shows that Heaven’s Way is supremely pervasive and perfectly correct, loving universally without partiality. Confucius distinguished these as four virtues, making clear that the Way of ruling people takes the four seasons as its standard. Thus origination corresponds to spring and benevolence; free course to summer and ritual propriety; benefit to autumn and righteousness; and constancy to winter and wisdom. Origination alone embraces all four. Hence it is said: “Qian’s power of beginning can benefit all under Heaven with its excellent benefits, without specifying what it benefits.” This illuminates the meaning of a ruler’s embodying origination: he too loves universally without partiality. Now, in its dealings with things, Heaven must have the sun…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
月風雨以運之陰陽寒暑以經之故少陽見春
物始孚甲太陽見夏物始長羸少陰見秋物始
斂藏太陰見冬物始凝結皆各司其命以順元
化非有假借者也今謂春生夏長是天仁萬物
則信矣秋冬萬物剝落天之仁宜無可見而仁
則存焉者氣不翕不聚聚然後物成成之也者
將生之也聖人觀乾見天則觀復見天心蓋謂
此也是故聖人之理天下春居青陽行春令則
親農桑發倉廩安萌芽養幼少夏居明堂行夏
===
令則斷薄刑出輕繫行水利達道塗秋居總章
行秋令則簡兵實詰暴慢脩法制繕囹圄冬居
玄堂行冬令則培城郭固封疆備邊境完要塞
夫聖人終歲之間無少休暇若此而又因朝日
以脩陽政習地德因夕月以治陰教紀天刑則
自昧爽至于晦息殆無一念不在天下也聖人
豈樂詳於事哉夫天運而不積故能成其大溥
而不私故能成其公吾所為有一弗當天心弗
協天道而欲含氣之物無夭昏札瘥之憂視聽
punctuated:
月、風、雨以運之，陰陽、寒暑以經之。故少陽見春，物始孚甲；太陽見夏，物始長羸；少陰見秋，物始斂藏；太陰見冬，物始凝結。皆各司其命，以順元化，非有假借者也。今謂春生夏長，是天仁萬物，則信矣。秋冬萬物剝落，天之仁宜無可見，而仁則存焉者，氣不翕不聚，聚然後物成。成之也者，將生之也。聖人觀乾見天則，觀復見天心，蓋謂此也。
是故聖人之理天下，春居青陽，行春令，則親農桑，發倉廩，安萌芽，養幼少；夏居明堂，行夏令，則斷薄刑，出輕繫，行水利，達道塗；秋居總章，行秋令，則簡兵實，詰暴慢，脩法制，繕囹圄；冬居玄堂，行冬令，則培城郭，固封疆，備邊境，完要塞。夫聖人終歲之間，無少休暇若此，而又因朝日以脩陽政、習地德，因夕月以治陰教、紀天刑，則自昧爽至于晦息，殆無一念不在天下也。聖人豈樂詳於事哉？夫天運而不積，故能成其大；溥而不私，故能成其公。吾所為有一弗當天心、弗協天道，而欲含氣之物無夭昏札瘥之憂，視聽
translation_en:
…the moon, wind, and rain to set them in motion, and yin and yang, cold and heat to regulate them. Thus lesser yang manifests in spring, when things begin to sprout and break through their seed coverings; greater yang manifests in summer, when things begin to grow [?]; lesser yin manifests in autumn, when things begin to draw inward and store themselves away; and greater yin manifests in winter, when things begin to congeal. Each fulfills its appointed charge in accordance with the primordial transforming power, without borrowing anything from elsewhere. To say that spring’s generation and summer’s growth constitute Heaven’s benevolence toward the myriad things is indeed true. In autumn and winter, the myriad things wither and fall away, and Heaven’s benevolence would seem nowhere apparent. Yet benevolence remains present: unless vital energy draws inward, it cannot gather, and only after it gathers can things reach completion. To bring them to completion is to prepare for their generation. When the sage contemplates Qian, the Creative, he sees Heaven’s pattern; when he contemplates Fu, Return, he sees Heaven’s heart. This, surely, is what is meant.
Thus, in governing the world, the sage resides in the Qingyang, the Azure Yang Hall, in spring and carries out the spring ordinances: he personally attends to agriculture and sericulture, opens the granaries, safeguards budding growth, and nurtures the young. In summer he resides in the Mingtang, the Hall of Light, and carries out the summer ordinances: he adjudicates cases involving minor punishments, releases those detained for minor offenses, undertakes water-control works, and keeps roads open. In autumn he resides in the Zongzhang, the Hall of Full Manifestation, and carries out the autumn ordinances: he inspects military resources, calls the violent and negligent to account, puts laws and regulations in order, and repairs prisons. In winter he resides in the Xuantang, the Dark Hall, and carries out the winter ordinances: he strengthens city walls, secures territorial boundaries, prepares frontier defenses, and puts strategic fortifications in good repair. Throughout the year the sage thus has not the slightest leisure. Moreover, through the morning rite to the sun he cultivates yang governance and practices Earth’s virtue; through the evening rite to the moon he orders yin instruction and regulates Heaven’s punishments. From the first light of dawn until he rests at night, scarcely a single thought is ever apart from the world. Does the sage take pleasure in attending to affairs in such detail? Heaven moves without stagnating and thus achieves its greatness; it extends everywhere without partiality and thus achieves its impartiality. If even one thing I do fails to accord with Heaven’s heart or harmonize with Heaven’s Way, yet I wish living creatures to be free from the afflictions of premature death, blindness, pestilence, and disease, and those endowed with sight and hearing…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之類各得其所不可得已是故聖人春令不同
其爲生之一也夏令不同其爲長之一也秋令
不同其爲收之一也冬令不同其爲藏之一也
四時之令各不同其爲仁一也故曰其事雖詳
其爲道甚約也東周之時民困已極孔子雖以
天自處不得位故退而脩春秋惇典庸禮命德
討罪皆原諸天則又繫王於天畀之體元之責
其曰元年春王正月者示君人謹元始而大居
正也隕霜不殺桃李冬華則謂天之不仁春秋
===
惡之明秋冬而行春令亦非所以威懾不軌保
全元元也孔孟既沒天道不明邪說暴行有作
申韓李斯之徒壹切細苛上操下急民不堪命
蓋至秦而壞亂已極是豈徒闇於天道哉亦不
睹之春秋矣董生爲漢大儒深明斯旨思以天
道興起漢治故其言曰春者天之所以生也夏
者天之所以長也霜者天之所以殺也見殺之
者亦生之德刑非可偏廢也又曰聖人法天立
道溥愛而無私其意尤欲人主任德不任刑者
punctuated: 之類各得其所，不可得已。是故聖人春令不同，其爲生之一也；夏令不同，其爲長之一也；秋令不同，其爲收之一也；冬令不同，其爲藏之一也。四時之令各不同，其爲仁一也。故曰：「其事雖詳，其爲道甚約也。」東周之時，民困已極。孔子雖以天自處，不得位，故退而脩《春秋》。惇典庸禮，命德討罪，皆原諸天，則又繫王於天，畀之體元之責。其曰「元年春王正月」者，示君人謹元始而大居正也。隕霜不殺，桃李冬華，則謂天之不仁，《春秋》惡之，明秋冬而行春令，亦非所以威懾不軌、保全元元也。孔孟既沒，天道不明，邪說暴行有作。申韓李斯之徒，壹切細苛，上操下急，民不堪命。蓋至秦而壞亂已極，是豈徒闇於天道哉？亦不睹之《春秋》矣。董生爲漢大儒，深明斯旨，思以天道興起漢治。故其言曰：「春者，天之所以生也；夏者，天之所以長也；霜者，天之所以殺也。」見殺之者亦生之，德刑非可偏廢也。又曰：「聖人法天立道，溥愛而無私。」其意尤欲人主任德不任刑者
translation_en:
…for all beings endowed with sight and hearing to find their proper places would be impossible. Thus, the sage’s ordinances for spring differ, but are one in fostering birth; his ordinances for summer differ, but are one in fostering growth; his ordinances for autumn differ, but are one in bringing in the harvest; and his ordinances for winter differ, but are one in storing things away. The ordinances of the four seasons all differ, yet are one in their benevolence. Hence the saying: “Although his undertakings are detailed, the Way he follows is exceedingly simple.”

In the Eastern Zhou, the people’s distress had reached its utmost limit. Although Confucius took Heaven as his own standpoint, he obtained no position. He therefore withdrew and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals. Upholding the established norms, employing ritual, appointing the virtuous, and punishing the guilty all had their source in Heaven. He thus also bound the king to Heaven, entrusting him with the responsibility of embodying the primal beginning. The words “First year, spring, the king’s first month” show that a ruler must attend carefully to the primal beginning and hold firmly to what is correct as a matter of paramount importance. When frost fell but failed to kill vegetation, and peach and plum trees blossomed in winter, this was called Heaven’s failure of benevolence, and the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned it. This makes clear that carrying out spring’s ordinances in autumn and winter is likewise no way to overawe the lawless and preserve the common people.

After Confucius and Mengzi died, the Way of Heaven became obscure, and pernicious doctrines and violent conduct arose. Men such as Shen Buhai, Han Fei, and Li Si imposed uniformly petty and harsh measures; those above tightened their control, and those below were hard pressed. The people could not endure their commands. By the Qin, indeed, disorder and ruin had reached their utmost extent. Was this merely ignorance of the Way of Heaven? They had also failed to discern it in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Master Dong, a great Confucian scholar of the Han, understood this purport deeply and sought to revitalize Han government through the Way of Heaven. Thus he said: “Spring is that by which Heaven brings things to life; summer is that by which Heaven makes things grow; frost is that by which Heaven kills.” This shows that what kills also gives life: neither virtue nor punishment may be discarded in favor of the other. He also said: “The sage models himself on Heaven in establishing the Way, extending love universally and without partiality.” As for his particular intention that the ruler should rely on virtue rather than punishment…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
非偏也漢承秦敝宜專務德化博大敦裕斯可
舉明主於上世之隆俾至德揚詡薰爲太和跂
行喙息蠕動之物無不咸若而天道始終也惜
哉武帝昧此誠使君人者能明於春秋之旨體
乾元之義順月令之宜捄偏而不舉之處而又
從董生正心之說求所謂天道無私者於吾心
則仁覆天下興致太平信無難矣
表
擬翰林學士胡廣等進五經四書大全及
===
性理大全表永樂十三年
劉選
同考試官教諭毛　批　以典雅之詞發理性之
旨表之最佳者取之
同考試官教諭黃　批　用事切實措詞典雅讀
之如聆韶頀之音不覺神思飛越也敬服
考試官教諭林　批　麗而則樸而文四六之
難得者錄之以式多士
考試官教諭敖　批　體裁正大鋪敘詳明可佳
punctuated:
非偏也。漢承秦敝，宜專務德化，博大敦裕，斯可舉明主於上世之隆，俾至德揚詡，薰爲太和，跂行喙息蠕動之物無不咸若，而天道始終也。惜哉，武帝昧此！誠使君人者能明於春秋之旨，體乾元之義，順月令之宜，捄偏而不舉之處，而又從董生正心之說，求所謂天道無私者於吾心，則仁覆天下，興致太平，信無難矣。
表
擬翰林學士胡廣等進五經四書大全及性理大全表，永樂十三年。
劉選
同考試官教諭毛批：以典雅之詞發理性之旨，表之最佳者，取之。
同考試官教諭黃批：用事切實，措詞典雅，讀之如聆韶頀之音，不覺神思飛越也。敬服。
考試官教諭林批：麗而則，樸而文，四六之難得者，錄之以式多士。
考試官教諭敖批：體裁正大，鋪敘詳明，可佳。
translation_en:
…was not one-sided. The Han inherited the ravages left by the Qin and ought to have devoted itself wholly to transformation through virtue, with breadth, generosity, earnestness, and liberality. Only thus could an enlightened ruler have been raised to the flourishing heights of antiquity, allowing consummate virtue to spread abroad and imbue all with supreme harmony. Every creature that walks, breathes through a beak, or crawls would then attain its proper condition, and Heaven’s Way would be fulfilled from beginning to end. Alas, Emperor Wu failed to understand this! If rulers could truly understand the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals, embody the meaning of Qian’s originating power, follow the appropriate prescriptions of the Monthly Ordinances, remedy imbalances and matters left unattended [?], and further follow Master Dong’s teaching on rectifying the heart, seeking within their own hearts what is called the impartiality of Heaven’s Way, then benevolence would shelter all under Heaven. Bringing about supreme peace would surely present no difficulty.
Memorial
A memorial composed in the person of Hu Guang, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and his colleagues, submitting the Comprehensive Compendia of the Five Classics and the Four Books and the Comprehensive Compendium of Nature and Principle; the thirteenth year of Yongle [1415].
By Liu Xuan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “With refined and elegant language, it elucidates the purport of principle and nature. Among the very best memorials; accept it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Its allusions are apt and sound, its phrasing refined and elegant. Reading it is like hearing the music of the Shao and Hu: before one knows it, the spirit and thoughts soar aloft. I respectfully admire it.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Ornate yet disciplined, plain yet polished: a rare achievement in four-and-six prose. Record it as a model for the many scholars.”
Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: “Its form is correct and dignified, and its exposition detailed and clear. Admirable.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
永樂十三年九月十五日翰林學士臣胡
廣等謹奉
欽命編輯五經四書大全及性理大全今繕寫
已完總二百二十九卷
進呈者伏以
聖王繼天立極弘昭道統之傳
明主稽古右文聿闡休明之化心法實相爲授
受治功由是以彌綸畏也大成匪徒小補
臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟洪濛判而
===
儀象分風氣開而人文著帝王之治本於
道恒因性以牖民帝王之道寓於書必隨
時而立政龍圖獻瑞八卦始畫於伏羲龜
兆呈祥九疇載敘於神禹虞廷精一之訓
萬古有光成湯執中之言百王不易文演
易于殷室丕顯文謨武受戒于丹書茂承
武烈姬旦兼三王而施四事孔丘列羣聖
而集大成心印獨授於顏曾眞派竝流於
思孟郎其親炙私淑之微旨無非天德王
punctuated:
永樂十三年九月十五日，翰林學士臣胡廣等謹奉欽命，編輯五經四書大全及性理大全，今繕寫已完，總二百二十九卷，進呈者。伏以：聖王繼天立極，弘昭道統之傳；明主稽古右文，聿闡休明之化。心法實相爲授受，治功由是以彌綸。畏也大成，匪徒小補。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
竊惟洪濛判而儀象分，風氣開而人文著。帝王之治本於道，恒因性以牖民；帝王之道寓於書，必隨時而立政。龍圖獻瑞，八卦始畫於伏羲；龜兆呈祥，九疇載敘於神禹。虞廷精一之訓，萬古有光；成湯執中之言，百王不易。文演易于殷室，丕顯文謨；武受戒于丹書，茂承武烈。姬旦兼三王而施四事，孔丘列羣聖而集大成。心印獨授於顏曾，眞派竝流於思孟。郎其親炙私淑之微旨，無非天德王
translation_en:
On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Yongle [1415], your servant Hu Guang, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and his colleagues respectfully submit the works compiled in obedience to the imperial command: the Complete Compendia of the Five Classics and Four Books and the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle. Fair copies have now been completed, totaling 229 juan.
We humbly consider that the sage king succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, gloriously illuminating the transmission of the succession of the Way; the enlightened ruler examines antiquity and esteems letters, thereby extending a splendid and enlightened transforming influence. The teachings of the mind are indeed transmitted from one to another, and through them the achievements of government become all-encompassing. An awe-inspiring grand synthesis [?], this is no mere minor contribution. We, your servants, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow.
We humbly reflect that when primordial chaos divided, the forms and images of the cosmos became distinct; when the prevailing influences unfolded, human culture became manifest. The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way and constantly guides the people toward enlightenment in accordance with their nature. The Way of emperors and kings resides in books, and government must be established in accordance with the times. The dragon diagram offered an auspicious sign, and Fuxi first drew the Eight Trigrams; the tortoise markings presented a favorable omen, and the divine Yu set forth the Nine Categories. The instruction at the court of Yu to be discerning and single-minded shines through all ages; Cheng Tang’s words about holding fast to the mean remain unaltered through a hundred kings. King Wen elaborated the Changes under the Yin dynasty, splendidly manifesting his civil designs; King Wu received admonitions from the Cinnabar Writing, nobly carrying forward martial achievements. Ji Dan combined the ways of the Three Kings and carried out the four undertakings; Kong Qiu stood among the assembled sages and brought their work to its great culmination. The seal of the mind was transmitted exclusively to Yan Hui and Zeng Shen, and the authentic lineage flowed through both Zisi and Mengzi. The subtle purport of learning through direct personal instruction or through the transmitted teachings [?] was nothing other than the practical realization of heavenly virtue and the kingly…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
道之實功異端起而大義乖邪說滋而正
經息嗟羣籍大厄于秦灰幸斯文僅存于
漢壁詩書不事自安馬上之風禮樂未遑
何補躬脩之治橫經講道臨雍徒侈乎彌
文午夜觀書乙躬祇益夫慚德自玆以降
鮮有可稱逮宋室之隆興煥星纏而奎聚
濂洛關閩之儒迭出堯舜禹湯之緒彌光
宏開正學之宗大掃橫途之塞聖經賢傳
衆星紛雜辨之天諸子百家萬水支流歸
諸海遭胡元之竊據致治教之陵夷道不
虛行時將有待恭惟
===
皇帝陛下
重華協帝
一德格天
丕闡鴻圖恢創業守成之道
嗣承寶曆奮南征北伐之威
允武允文
克明克類
punctuated: 道之實功。異端起而大義乖，邪說滋而正經息。嗟羣籍大厄于秦灰，幸斯文僅存于漢壁。詩書不事，自安馬上之風；禮樂未遑，何補躬脩之治？橫經講道，臨雍徒侈乎彌文；午夜觀書，乙躬祇益夫慚德。自玆以降，鮮有可稱。逮宋室之隆興，煥星纏而奎聚。濂洛關閩之儒迭出，堯舜禹湯之緒彌光。宏開正學之宗，大掃橫途之塞。聖經賢傳，衆星紛雜辨之天；諸子百家，萬水支流歸諸海。遭胡元之竊據，致治教之陵夷。道不虛行，時將有待。恭惟皇帝陛下，重華協帝，一德格天，丕闡鴻圖，恢創業守成之道；嗣承寶曆，奮南征北伐之威。允武允文，克明克類。
translation_en:
…the substantive achievements of the kingly Way. When heterodox teachings arose, the great principles were distorted; when pernicious doctrines proliferated, the orthodox classics fell silent. Alas, the collected writings suffered a great calamity in the ashes of Qin; fortunately, this cultural inheritance barely survived within walls in Han times. Neglecting the Odes and Documents, rulers complacently relied on the ways of horseback conquest; with no leisure for rites and music, how could they further government grounded in personal cultivation? Unrolling the classics and expounding the Way, their visits to the imperial school merely magnified elaborate ceremony; reading books at midnight only increased their shame at their deficient virtue [the wording 乙躬 is doubtful]. From then onward, little deserved praise. With the flourishing rise of the Song house, the celestial stations shone brilliantly and the stars gathered in the constellation Kui. The Confucian scholars of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min emerged in succession, and the tradition of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang grew ever more radiant. They opened wide the lineage of orthodox learning and swept away the obstructions of deviant paths. The sages’ classics and the worthies’ commentaries were like multitudinous stars distinguished in heaven [?]; the various masters and hundred schools were like myriad tributary streams returning to the sea. Then the usurpation of the non-Han Yuan brought government and moral instruction into decline. The Way cannot operate in a vacuum; it must await its proper time.

We reverently consider Your Majesty the Emperor: your renewed brilliance accords with the ancient emperor, and your single-minded virtue reaches Heaven. You grandly unfold the magnificent imperial design, extending the Way of founding an enterprise and preserving its achievements; you inherit the precious imperial succession, displaying the might of southern campaigns and northern expeditions. Truly martial and truly cultured, capable of discernment and of distinguishing things according to their kinds…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
體元協夫四大
定鼎式于九圍
著聖學心法之書
頒歷代臣鑑之訓治已至而猶以為未至道
已純而猶以為未純乃於投戈講藝之餘
爰舉重道崇儒之典謂經書為列聖傳心
之要時允貴于表章以性理為諸儒衛道
之言善尤資於兼體乃涣
大號於彤陛兼開經局於銅龍裒延文學之
臣均給
===
尚方之恵繼膏油于藜火窮緗袠于木天神
會心融仰贊
化工之妙條分縷析率循敷訓之章惟
聖王能自得師故君子與人為善
經筵進講致詳於出入起居之間士庶均陶
悉納於平康正直之域淵源遠矣雖百世
而可知綱目瞭然指諸掌而易見聲為律
身為度學務底於惟精尊所聞行所知俗
punctuated: 體元協夫四大，定鼎式于九圍，著聖學心法之書，頒歷代臣鑑之訓。治已至而猶以為未至，道已純而猶以為未純。乃於投戈講藝之餘，爰舉重道崇儒之典。謂經書為列聖傳心之要，時允貴于表章；以性理為諸儒衛道之言，善尤資於兼體。乃涣大號於彤陛，兼開經局於銅龍，裒延文學之臣，均給尚方之恵。繼膏油于藜火，窮緗袠于木天，神會心融，仰贊化工之妙；條分縷析，率循敷訓之章。惟聖王能自得師，故君子與人為善。經筵進講，致詳於出入起居之間；士庶均陶，悉納於平康正直之域。淵源遠矣，雖百世而可知；綱目瞭然，指諸掌而易見。聲為律，身為度，學務底於惟精；尊所聞，行所知，俗
translation_en:
…embodying the primal principle and standing in harmony with the Four Great Ones; establishing the dynastic tripods and serving as a model throughout the nine regions; composing the book Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning and promulgating the teachings of the Mirror for Ministers through the Dynasties. Though your governance has reached perfection, you still regard it as imperfect; though your Way is pure, you still regard it as not yet pure. Thus, in the intervals between laying aside weapons and discussing the arts of learning, you have instituted ceremonies honoring the Way and exalting Confucian scholarship. You regard the canonical books as the essentials through which successive sages transmitted their minds, and truly prize their elucidation. You take the writings on human nature and principle as the words through which the Confucian scholars defended the Way, and the attainment of goodness depends especially upon embodying their teachings comprehensively.

You therefore issued your great proclamation from the vermilion steps and opened offices for work on the classics within the palace’s bronze-dragon gates. You assembled and welcomed ministers of literary learning, bestowing upon all alike the bounty of the imperial provisioning offices. You supplied lamp oil to sustain their scholarly labors, evoking the light of the goosefoot staff, and had them exhaustively study the volumes in yellow silk covers within the imperial library. Through spiritual apprehension and inward assimilation, they reverently assisted the wondrous work of your transforming influence; distinguishing each category and unraveling every thread, they followed the established forms for expounding instruction. Only a sage king can find teachers for himself; thus does the gentleman help others to practice goodness.

Lectures at the Classics Colloquium bring detailed instruction into your movements and daily life. Scholars and commoners alike receive this formative influence, and all are brought into a realm of peace and uprightness. These teachings have deep and distant sources, yet they can be understood even after a hundred generations; their guiding principles and particulars are so clear that they are as readily seen as something pointed out in one’s palm. Your voice serves as the pitch standard, your person as the measure; learning strives to attain utmost refinement. Honoring what they have heard and putting what they know into practice, the people’s customs…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
期封於比屋一洗襲沿之陋期回淳古之
風俾吾道如日中天庶萬年若水行地俟
後聖而不惑質鬼神以無疑信
帝王自有眞惟
聖人乃立極也〔臣〕等衡茅下士章句燕儒學素
慚於面墻識僅同於窺管身膺珮綬稽古
僭擬夫桓榮志切經綸談經竊比于劉向
幸際
文明之運濫叨校讎之司編輯成書裝潢進
===
御共効雕虫之技庸塵
淸燕之觀豈惟上助乎
聖脩亦可取裁於治化伏願
學懋緝熙煥周文之郁郁
德隆廣運欽堯思之安安
作之君作之師與治同道
得其名得其壽以經法天
咸五登三建億兆臣民之極
參天兩地收中和位育之功
punctuated:
期封於比屋，一洗襲沿之陋，期回淳古之風，俾吾道如日中天，庶萬年若水行地，俟後聖而不惑，質鬼神以無疑。信帝王自有眞，惟聖人乃立極也。
〔臣〕等衡茅下士，章句燕儒，學素慚於面墻，識僅同於窺管。身膺珮綬，稽古僭擬夫桓榮；志切經綸，談經竊比于劉向。幸際文明之運，濫叨校讎之司，編輯成書，裝潢進御，共効雕虫之技，庸塵淸燕之觀。豈惟上助乎聖脩，亦可取裁於治化。
伏願學懋緝熙，煥周文之郁郁；德隆廣運，欽堯思之安安。作之君，作之師，與治同道；得其名，得其壽，以經法天。咸五登三，建億兆臣民之極；參天兩地，收中和位育之功。
translation_en:
…with the hope that every household may merit enfeoffment, sweeping away the shortcomings of inherited convention and restoring the customs of pristine antiquity. May our Way shine like the sun at the zenith and, for ten thousand years, flow like water across the earth: awaiting a future sage without perplexity, and submitting it to the spirits without doubt. Truly, emperors and kings possess the genuine essence; only the sage establishes the supreme standard.
We, your servants, are lowly scholars from humble thatched dwellings, scholars of textual minutiae [?]. In learning we have long been ashamed of facing a blank wall; our understanding is scarcely better than looking through a narrow tube. Wearing the pendants and ribbons of office, we presumptuously liken our study of antiquity to that of Huan Rong; earnestly aspiring to order the realm, we privately compare our discussions of the classics to those of Liu Xiang. Fortunately encountering an age of cultural enlightenment, we have undeservedly been entrusted with textual collation. We have compiled and edited these writings into a book, mounted and bound it, and presented it for imperial inspection. Together we offer our paltry literary skills, venturing to intrude upon Your Majesty’s reading in quiet leisure. This may not only aid Your Majesty’s sage self-cultivation, but also provide a basis for decisions in government and moral transformation.
We humbly pray that Your Majesty’s learning will advance in continuous illumination, displaying the luxuriant cultural brilliance of Zhou; that Your Majesty’s virtue will grow vast and far-reaching, revering the serenity of Yao’s thought. As ruler and teacher of the people, may you follow the Way that brings good government; attaining renown and longevity, may you take Heaven as your model through the classics. May you equal the Five Emperors and rise to the Three Sovereigns, establishing the supreme standard for your countless subjects; may you join Heaven’s three with Earth’s two, achieving the work of equilibrium and harmony, whereby Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things flourish…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
綿萬年景運之長
洽四海篤恭之治〔臣廣〕等謹以經書性理大
全若干卷隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
劉貞一
===
同考試官教諭鄭　批　〔我〕
皇上好生之德同符
聖祖遠邁百王子能鋪張揚厲且于歷代刑名之制考究精詳可式
考試官教諭林　批　〔律例一策諸士子類能〕
〔言之悉未得肯綮此作援古證今條析無遺可以〕
〔知子他日之服政矣錄之以式〕
考試官教諭敖　批　〔以制刑成德立意甚是〕
〔且體格平正詞采充瑩高薦〕
punctuated:
綿萬年景運之長，洽四海篤恭之治。〔臣廣〕等謹以經書性理大全若干卷，隨表上進以聞。

第叁場，策，第一問。劉貞一。

同考試官教諭鄭批：〔我〕皇上好生之德，同符聖祖，遠邁百王。子能鋪張揚厲，且于歷代刑名之制考究精詳，可式。

考試官教諭林批：〔律例一策，諸士子類能〕〔言之，悉未得肯綮。此作援古證今，條析無遺，可以〕〔知子他日之服政矣。錄之以式。〕

考試官教諭敖批：〔以制刑成德立意甚是，〕〔且體格平正，詞采充瑩，高薦。〕
translation_en:
… prolong the glorious fortune of the dynasty for ten thousand years, and extend throughout the Four Seas a rule of profound reverence. Your servant Guang and the others respectfully submit several volumes of the Complete Compendia of the Classics and of Nature and Principle (Jingshu Xingli Daquan), accompanying this memorial, for Your Majesty’s consideration.

Third Session. Policy Essay. First Question.
Liu Zhenyi.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Our Emperor’s virtue of cherishing life accords with that of the Sagely Ancestor and far surpasses that of the hundred kings. You have expounded and extolled it fully; moreover, your investigation of the penal institutions of successive dynasties is precise and thorough. This may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “On this policy question concerning statutes and substatutes, most candidates could offer a discussion, but none reached the essential points. This essay draws on antiquity to illuminate the present and analyzes each matter without omission. From it one can discern how you will conduct government in the future. It is recorded here as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: “The central argument—that establishing punishments brings virtue to completion—is most sound. Moreover, the composition is balanced and correct, and its language rich and lustrous. Highly recommended.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人以道御天下不得已而詳於法者義
也示民不可犯者仁也是故法豈聖人樂
爲用哉天下日趨於僞猶江河日趨於下
不以法坊之則不止故坊民之僞甚於坊
川川壅而潰傷人則多民僞而滋害治尤
甚聖人以爲驅天下麗於法則吾豈忍縱
天下入於亂又焉用司牧者爲哉是故詳
於法以明有義示之不可犯以明有仁仁
義茲用則久安長治之策也知乎此則可
===
竊我
皇祖創法之意暨我
列聖保治之謨矣嘗攷
國家所著定刑書自
大誥之外科指精切可世世通行者三一曰
令二曰律三曰條例
皇祖御極卽
布令于天下爲類有六爲條百四十有三亦
既隱括事情根極理要俾民易知難犯矣
punctuated:
聖人以道御天下，不得已而詳於法者，義也；示民不可犯者，仁也。是故法豈聖人樂爲用哉？天下日趨於僞，猶江河日趨於下，不以法坊之則不止。故坊民之僞甚於坊川，川壅而潰，傷人則多；民僞而滋，害治尤甚。聖人以爲驅天下麗於法，則吾豈忍？縱天下入於亂，又焉用司牧者爲哉？是故詳於法以明有義，示之不可犯以明有仁。仁義茲用，則久安長治之策也。知乎此，則可竊我皇祖創法之意暨我列聖保治之謨矣。
嘗攷國家所著定刑書，自《大誥》之外，科指精切、可世世通行者三：一曰令，二曰律，三曰條例。皇祖御極，卽布令于天下，爲類有六，爲條百四十有三，亦既隱括事情，根極理要，俾民易知難犯矣。
translation_en:
The sage governs All-under-Heaven through the Way. That he must, despite his reluctance, formulate laws in detail is righteousness; that he shows the people what must not be transgressed is benevolence. How, then, could law be something the sage delights in employing? The world tends daily toward deceit, just as rivers flow ever downward. Unless restrained by law, this tendency will not cease. Thus restraining the people's deceit is more urgent than embanking rivers. When a river is obstructed and bursts its banks, many people are injured; when deceit among the people proliferates, the harm to good government is greater still. The sage considers: “How could I bear to drive everyone into the grasp of the law? Yet if I let the world descend into disorder, what purpose would its governors serve?” Thus he formulates laws in detail to manifest righteousness and shows the people what must not be transgressed to manifest benevolence. Employing benevolence and righteousness in this way is the means to lasting peace and enduring order. Understanding this, one may venture to discern the intent with which our imperial ancestor established the laws and the plans by which our successive sage emperors preserved good government.
I have examined the penal texts established by our dynasty. Apart from the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), there are three whose provisions and purport are precise and pertinent, and which can remain generally applicable for generation after generation: first, the Ordinances (ling); second, the Code (lü); and third, the Regulations (tiaoli). Upon ascending the throne, our imperial ancestor immediately promulgated ordinances throughout the realm. Arranged in six categories and comprising 143 articles, they comprehensively encompassed practical affairs and thoroughly grounded themselves in essential principles, making them easy for the people to understand and difficult to transgress.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
民果無犯則律可無作旣而復
命尚書劉惟謙損益舊文著爲
大明律者是非
皇祖所得已也律之爲書上揆天道下悉民情
兼總古今條酌化理可謂至極宜無復加
矣
列聖相承復有條例至弘治間乃
命尚書白昂等兼采
廷議彙爲成書是條例之設又豈
===
孝廟所得已哉民生有欲情僞相感蓋自上世
以來漸趨於僞故軒轅之世即有刑官有
虞氏興象刑斯著夏有政典商有官刑皆
是物也成周儀鑒前代置法益詳列在秋
官不可殫述姑從明問攷之虞有三居此
量遠邇言仁在遠邇間也周有三典此權
輕重言仁在輕重間也五禁五戒士師掌
之仁在未罪前也三赦三宥司刺掌之仁
在已罪後也墨劓剕宮大辟者虞周所謂
punctuated:
民果無犯，則律可無作。旣而復命尚書劉惟謙損益舊文，著爲《大明律》者，是非皇祖所得已也。律之爲書，上揆天道，下悉民情，兼總古今，條酌化理，可謂至極，宜無復加矣。列聖相承，復有條例。至弘治間，乃命尚書白昂等兼采廷議，彙爲成書。是條例之設，又豈孝廟所得已哉？

民生有欲，情僞相感，蓋自上世以來，漸趨於僞。故軒轅之世，即有刑官；有虞氏興，象刑斯著；夏有政典，商有官刑，皆是物也。成周儀鑒前代，置法益詳，列在《秋官》，不可殫述。姑從明問攷之：虞有三居，此量遠邇，言仁在遠邇間也；周有三典，此權輕重，言仁在輕重間也。五禁五戒，士師掌之，仁在未罪前也；三赦三宥，司刺掌之，仁在已罪後也。墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟者，虞周所謂
translation_en:
If the people truly committed no offenses, there would be no need to compile a penal code. Subsequently, however, the imperial ancestor again ordered Minister Liu Weiqian to revise the earlier text, making additions and deletions, and compile the Great Ming Code. This was something the imperial ancestor could not avoid. As a work, the Code accords above with the Way of Heaven and comprehends below the circumstances of the people. It encompasses past and present, weighing in its provisions the principles of moral transformation and governance. It may be called the utmost achievement, to which nothing further should have needed to be added. Yet under the succession of sage emperors, supplementary regulations were introduced. During the Hongzhi reign, Minister Bai Ang and others were ordered to draw also upon court deliberations and compile these into a finished work. Could the establishment of these regulations have been something Emperor Xiaozong could avoid?

People are born with desires, and sincerity and deceit act upon one another. Since high antiquity, the tendency has gradually been toward deceit. Thus, already in the age of Xuanyuan there were officials responsible for punishments. When the ruler of Yu arose, emblematic punishments were instituted. The Xia had its Statutes of Government, and the Shang its Official Punishments: all were of this kind. The Zhou took preceding dynasties as models and warnings, establishing increasingly detailed laws. These are set out in the Offices of Autumn and cannot be exhaustively recounted. Let us examine them in accordance with your illuminating question. Yu had three places of confinement: this weighed distance, showing that benevolence lay in the choice between far and near. Zhou had three penal codes: this weighed severity, showing that benevolence lay in the choice between lighter and heavier penalties. The five prohibitions and five admonitions were administered by the Chief Judicial Officer (shishi): here benevolence operated before an offense was committed. The three grounds for pardon and three grounds for leniency were administered by the judicial review official (sici): here benevolence operated after an offense was committed. Tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputation of the feet, castration, and execution were what Yu and Zhou called…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
五刑笞杖徒流死者後世所謂五刑然觀
皐陶之命則笞杖徒流虞已用之國語稱
薄刑用鞭扑而周禮有嘉石役法則周亦
用是也但肉刑著在令甲如周禮所載爲
條二千五百呂刑所載爲屬三千雖詳畧
不同其示民不可犯一也由此觀之聖人
用刑義在法中仁周法外不得已而用之
固未始廢刑也史稱有虞氏畫衣冠異章
服以爲戮其說始於愼到而尚書大傳白
===
虎通論皆踵言之是泥於五刑有服而不
知所謂服者乃謂服罪若謂冠服可以示
戮又何須三就五宅哉我
國家定律上倣虞周兼采唐律令觀舊律凡
六百有六條爲篇十有二後又別爲六類
而析戶婚爲戶役婚姻鬭訟爲鬭毆獄訟
廄庫爲廄牧倉庫職制爲公式受贓撮要
舉凡去苛就簡殆非唐律可及然所以獨
采唐律者以其吏李悝蕭何陳羣劉邵賈
punctuated:
五刑，笞、杖、徒、流、死者，後世所謂五刑。然觀皐陶之命，則笞、杖、徒、流，虞已用之。《國語》稱薄刑用鞭扑，而《周禮》有嘉石役法，則周亦用是也。但肉刑著在令甲，如《周禮》所載爲條二千五百，《呂刑》所載爲屬三千，雖詳畧不同，其示民不可犯一也。由此觀之，聖人用刑，義在法中，仁周法外，不得已而用之，固未始廢刑也。史稱有虞氏畫衣冠、異章服以爲戮，其說始於愼到，而《尚書大傳》、《白虎通論》皆踵言之。是泥於五刑有服，而不知所謂服者乃謂服罪。若謂冠服可以示戮，又何須三就五宅哉？
我國家定律，上倣虞周，兼采唐律令。觀舊律，凡六百有六條，爲篇十有二，後又別爲六類，而析戶婚爲戶役、婚姻，鬭訟爲鬭毆、獄訟，廄庫爲廄牧、倉庫，職制爲公式、受贓。撮要舉凡，去苛就簡，殆非唐律可及。然所以獨采唐律者，以其吏李悝、蕭何、陳羣、劉邵、賈
translation_en:
…the Five Punishments. Beating with the light stick, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, exile, and death are what later ages call the Five Punishments. Yet, examining the charge to Gao Yao, we find that beating with the light and heavy sticks, penal servitude, and exile were already employed under Yu. The Discourses of the States says that light punishments employed whips and switches, while the Rites of Zhou provides for compulsory labor associated with the fine stone; thus Zhou also used these punishments. Corporal mutilations, however, were expressly set out in the statutes: the Rites of Zhou records 2,500 provisions, and the “Punishments of Lü” records 3,000 categories. Although they differ in detail and scope, they are alike in showing the people what they must not transgress. Viewed in this light, when the sages employed punishments, righteousness resided within the law, while benevolence extended beyond it. They employed punishments only when compelled to do so, but certainly never abolished them.
Historical accounts say that the ruler of Yu used painted garments and caps and distinctive ceremonial clothing as punishment. This explanation originated with Shen Dao, and both the Great Commentary on the Book of Documents and the Comprehensive Discussions of the White Tiger Hall repeated it. This clings to a literal reading of “the Five Punishments have their fu,” without understanding that fu here means submitting to punishment for one's crime. If caps and clothing could serve to display punishment, what need would there have been for the three places of execution and the five places of confinement?
In establishing its code, our dynasty took ancient Yu and Zhou as its models and also drew upon the Tang statutes and ordinances. Examining the former code, we find 606 articles arranged in twelve sections. These were subsequently regrouped into six categories. “Households and Marriage” was divided into “Households and Labor Service” and “Marriage”; “Fighting and Litigation” into “Affrays” and “Judicial Proceedings”; “Stables and Storehouses” into “Stables and Pasturage” and “Granaries and Storehouses”; and “Official Regulations” into “Official Procedures” and “Acceptance of Illicit Payments.” It gathered the essentials and set out the general principles, eliminating onerous provisions in favor of simplicity—an achievement scarcely matched by the Tang code. Yet the reason it drew specifically upon the Tang code was that the latter had passed through [?] Li Kui, Xiao He, Chen Qun, Liu Shao, Jia…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
充王敘諸人秦漢魏晉齊隋諸代而長孫
無忌輩特集其大成耳昔胡安國謂五經
有春秋猶法律有斷例愚亦謂
大明律一書眞可與五經竝行于世明吉凶則
盡易之變定經制則述書之事飾喜怒則
發詩之情正名分則體禮之經薄過誤則
導樂之和而尤謹華夷之防詳義利之辨
別故失之等定首從之差雖春秋謹嚴亦
不是過是卽虞之象刑周之中典而與五
===
禁五戒三赦三宥相爲出入大抵使人易
避難犯以仁天下之心行正天下之義也
知五經不可裒益則知律文不可增損乃
復設有條例非以濟律之不及也凡民之
情重刑易入輕刑易犯故弘治十年詳擬
罪名卽死刑眞犯雜犯並加斟酌懼其易
入也明年始著條例欲其難犯也我
孝廟仁天下之心至此極矣然條例之中間有
過重是當時諸臣議擬未精至正德間雜
banxin: 浙江鄉試錄文 四十五
punctuated:
充、王敘諸人，秦、漢、魏、晉、齊、隋諸代，而長孫無忌輩特集其大成耳。昔胡安國謂：「五經有春秋，猶法律有斷例。」愚亦謂：《大明律》一書，眞可與五經竝行于世。明吉凶則盡易之變，定經制則述書之事，飾喜怒則發詩之情，正名分則體禮之經，薄過誤則導樂之和，而尤謹華夷之防，詳義利之辨，別故失之等，定首從之差。雖春秋謹嚴，亦不是過。是卽虞之象刑、周之中典，而與五禁、五戒、三赦、三宥相爲出入。大抵使人易避難犯，以仁天下之心，行正天下之義也。
知五經不可裒益，則知律文不可增損。乃復設有條例，非以濟律之不及也。凡民之情，重刑易入，輕刑易犯。故弘治十年詳擬罪名，卽死刑眞犯、雜犯，並加斟酌，懼其易入也。明年始著條例，欲其難犯也。我孝廟仁天下之心，至此極矣。然條例之中，間有過重，是當時諸臣議擬未精。至正德間，雜
translation_en:
…Chong and Wang Xu, among others, through the Qin, Han, Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui dynasties; Changsun Wuji and his colleagues merely brought these achievements together in their fullest form. Hu Anguo once said: “The Five Classics have the Spring and Autumn Annals, just as laws have precedents for deciding cases.” I too venture to say that the Great Ming Code truly deserves to circulate in the world alongside the Five Classics. In clarifying good and ill fortune, it comprehends the changes of the Book of Changes; in establishing enduring institutions, it sets forth the affairs recorded in the Book of Documents; in regulating joy and anger, it gives expression to the sentiments of the Book of Odes; in rectifying distinctions of status, it embodies the enduring principles of the Rites; and in treating inadvertent wrongdoing leniently, it promotes the harmony of Music. It is particularly scrupulous in maintaining the boundary between Chinese and barbarians, precise in distinguishing righteousness from profit, discriminating in grading intentional and inadvertent offenses, and exact in differentiating principals from accomplices. Even the rigor of the Spring and Autumn Annals does not surpass it. This is precisely the emblematic punishment of Yu and the balanced penal code of Zhou; its provisions correspond, with variations, to the five prohibitions, five admonitions, three grounds for pardon, and three grounds for mitigation. Its general purpose is to make offenses easy to avoid and difficult to commit: with a heart that treats all under Heaven humanely, it carries out the righteous task of setting all under Heaven right.
Knowing that the Five Classics admit neither subtraction nor addition, one knows that the statutory text likewise admits neither addition nor subtraction. Supplementary regulations were nevertheless established, but not to remedy deficiencies in the statutes. Given ordinary human dispositions, people are readily brought within the scope of severe punishments, while offenses carrying light punishments are readily committed. Thus, in the tenth year of Hongzhi [1497], categories of offenses were carefully deliberated; even capital offenses, both those subject to actual execution and those classified as miscellaneous capital offenses, were weighed carefully, out of concern that people might too readily be brought within their scope. In the following year, regulations were first promulgated, with the intention of making offenses difficult to commit. The humane concern for all under Heaven of our Xiaozong reached its utmost expression here. Yet some of these regulations were excessively severe, because the ministers’ deliberations and drafting at the time had lacked precision. By the Zhengde reign, miscellaneous …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
例愈多注疏者輒以旁附律文之下目爲
斷例豈不謬哉
聖天子中興首革雜例仍
勑所司不許深文煩語濫及無辜所以上體
天德下惠元元甚盛渥也邇年
屢俞諸司之請斟酌新例參□條例所不逮
者聞之法官亦旣裒采成編□諸史官行
將增入
會典頒行四方矣四方治獄之吏未見全文
===
往往攙摭雜例轉相比況禁防寖密律意
寖微甚者文致成姦因緣爲市所欲出則
傅生議所欲入則予死比甚非所以仰體
聖天子好生之意也昨者
廷臣建議仍欲會集諸司增定條例務求厥
中俾治獄者有所持循麗法者無至枉抑
此
今日仁義竝用所
天永命之道也愚何幸躬逢其盛
punctuated:
例愈多，注疏者輒以旁附律文之下，目爲斷例，豈不謬哉！聖天子中興，首革雜例，仍勑所司不許深文煩語，濫及無辜，所以上體天德，下惠元元，甚盛渥也。邇年屢俞諸司之請，斟酌新例，參□條例所不逮者，聞之法官亦旣裒采成編，□諸史官，行將增入《會典》，頒行四方矣。四方治獄之吏未見全文，往往攙摭雜例，轉相比況，禁防寖密，律意寖微。甚者文致成姦，因緣爲市，所欲出則傅生議，所欲入則予死比，甚非所以仰體聖天子好生之意也。
昨者廷臣建議，仍欲會集諸司，增定條例，務求厥中，俾治獄者有所持循，麗法者無至枉抑。此今日仁義竝用，所天永命之道也。愚何幸躬逢其盛！
translation_en:
…regulations grew ever more numerous. Those who annotated the Code would append them beside and beneath its text, calling them precedents for deciding cases. Was this not mistaken! In restoring flourishing rule, our sagely Son of Heaven first abolished these miscellaneous regulations. He further commanded the responsible offices not to employ strained interpretations and cumbersome wording that would indiscriminately implicate the innocent. In this way he embodied Heaven’s virtue above and bestowed kindness upon the common people below: truly magnificent and generous beneficence. In recent years he has repeatedly approved requests from the various offices, weighing new precedents to address matters inadequately covered by the existing regulations [?]. I have heard that the judicial officials have already collected these into a compilation and [submitted it?] to the historiographers. They will soon be added to the Collected Statutes and promulgated throughout the realm. Officials adjudicating cases in the provinces have not seen the complete text. They frequently mix in miscellaneous precedents and apply analogies from one case to another, so that prohibitions become ever more intricate while the intent of the Code becomes ever more obscure. In the worst cases, they manipulate legal wording for corrupt ends and exploit opportunities to turn justice into a market. Those whom they wish to exonerate receive an argument contrived to spare their lives; those whom they wish to convict receive an analogy warranting death. This utterly fails to embody our sagely Son of Heaven’s desire to preserve life.
Recently, court officials proposed once again bringing together the various offices to supplement and settle the regulations, striving to achieve the proper balance, so that those adjudicating cases would have rules to follow and those subject to the law would not suffer wrongful treatment. This is the way in our own day to employ benevolence and righteousness together, revere Heaven, and perpetuate the mandate [?]. How fortunate I am, in my humble station, to witness this flourishing age in person!

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
第二問
曾邦彥
同考試官教諭葛　批　考列前代及述我
皇祖功德之隆與
皇上著作之懿發揚殆盡且於古樂三致意焉其眞涵濡而有得者矣
同考試官教諭周　批　是篇學有根據氣昌辭
偉敘論
考試官教諭林　批　鋪敘明盡可以爲式
國家制作之盛本於中和之極可謂識其大者信中州奇士也
考試官教諭敖　批　深得探本之論
===
帝王之治本於道而後治可大帝王之道
本於心而後道可成何謂治教化是也何
謂道禮樂是也治而不本於道則所以治
之者無其具欲教化之行不可得矣道而
不本於心則所以行之者無其實欲禮樂
之興不可得矣治可以易言哉先王之治
天下也以人生有欲不能不爭爭則亂亂
則窮故制禮以序之作樂以和之使欲不
punctuated:
第二問

曾邦彥

同考試官教諭葛批：考列前代，及述我皇祖功德之隆與皇上著作之懿，發揚殆盡，且於古樂三致意焉，其眞涵濡而有得者矣。

同考試官教諭周批：是篇學有根據，氣昌辭偉，敘論。

考試官教諭林批：鋪敘明盡，可以爲式。國家制作之盛，本於中和之極，可謂識其大者，信中州奇士也。

考試官教諭敖批：深得探本之論。

帝王之治本於道，而後治可大；帝王之道本於心，而後道可成。何謂治？教化是也。何謂道？禮樂是也。治而不本於道，則所以治之者無其具，欲教化之行不可得矣；道而不本於心，則所以行之者無其實，欲禮樂之興不可得矣。治可以易言哉？先王之治天下也，以人生有欲，不能不爭，爭則亂，亂則窮，故制禮以序之，作樂以和之，使欲不
translation_en:
Second Policy Question

Zeng Bangyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: He examines and lists the preceding dynasties and recounts the exalted achievements and virtue of our imperial ancestor and the excellence of His Majesty’s writings, bringing these almost fully to light. Moreover, he repeatedly gives particular attention to ancient music. He is truly someone who has steeped himself in learning and gained understanding from it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: This essay’s learning has a firm foundation; its spirit is vigorous and its language magnificent. Its exposition and argument [?].

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The exposition is clear and thorough and can serve as a model. He grounds the magnificence of the dynasty’s institutions in the highest realization of equilibrium and harmony: he may be said to understand what is fundamental. Truly an exceptional scholar of Zhongzhou!

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: He has deeply grasped the argument that seeks out the foundation.

Only when the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way can their government become great; only when their Way is rooted in the heart can that Way be brought to fulfillment. What is government? Moral instruction and transformation. What is the Way? Ritual and music. If government is not rooted in the Way, it lacks the means by which to govern, and the desired implementation of moral instruction and transformation cannot be attained. If the Way is not rooted in the heart, its practice lacks substance, and the desired flourishing of ritual and music cannot be attained. Can government be spoken of lightly? When the former kings governed the world, they recognized that people are born with desires and cannot avoid contention; contention leads to disorder, and disorder to destitution. They therefore established ritual to bring order to them and created music to bring harmony to them, so that desires would not…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
窮於物物不屈於欲然後志氣天人交相
感應而雍熙太和之治可馴致也苟推之
無本行之無道徒區區從事於儀文器數
之間抑末矣故記曰禮也者反其所自生
樂也者樂其所自成又曰先王之制禮也
以節事脩樂以道志觀其禮樂而政治可
知也試爲執事誦所聞夫禮樂何爲者也
天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣流而不
息合同而化而樂興焉明於天地然後能
===
興禮樂也考之周禮大宗伯以天產作陰
