德以中禮防之以地產作陽德以和樂防
之有宮室車輿以爲居衣裳冕弁以爲服
樽爵俎豆以爲器金石絲竹以爲樂以適
郊廟以臨朝廷以事神而治民莫不一出
於禮樂天下安習而行之不知所以遷善
遠罪而成俗也及三代以降遭秦變古漢
唐宋相繼而有天下觀其名號位序國家
制度宮車服器其間雖有改作不能超然
punctuated:
窮於物，物不屈於欲，然後志氣、天人交相感應，而雍熙太和之治可馴致也。苟推之無本，行之無道，徒區區從事於儀文器數之間，抑末矣。故《記》曰：「禮也者，反其所自生；樂也者，樂其所自成。」又曰：「先王之制禮也，以節事；脩樂，以道志。觀其禮樂，而政治可知也。」
試爲執事誦所聞。夫禮樂何爲者也？天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣；流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。明於天地，然後能興禮樂也。考之《周禮》，大宗伯以天產作陰德，以中禮防之；以地產作陽德，以和樂防之。有宮室車輿以爲居，衣裳冕弁以爲服，樽爵俎豆以爲器，金石絲竹以爲樂，以適郊廟，以臨朝廷，以事神而治民，莫不一出於禮樂。天下安習而行之，不知所以遷善遠罪而成俗也。
及三代以降，遭秦變古，漢、唐、宋相繼而有天下。觀其名號位序、國家制度、宮車服器，其間雖有改作，不能超然
translation_en:
…desires would not go unsatisfied for lack of material things, nor material things be exhausted by desires. Only then could intentions and vital energies, Heaven and humanity, respond to one another, and a state of peaceful prosperity and supreme harmony gradually be attained. If these practices are promoted without a foundation and carried out without the Way, and one merely busies oneself with ceremonial forms and the prescribed details of implements, this is surely to attend only to the peripheral. Thus the Record of Rites says: “Ritual returns to that from which it arose; music takes joy in that through which it came to completion.” It also says: “The former kings established ritual to regulate affairs and cultivated music to guide intentions. By observing their ritual and music, one may understand their government.”
Allow me to recount for you, honored officials, what I have learned. What do ritual and music accomplish? Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct: thus the ordering of ritual operates. Things flow without ceasing, unite in concord, and undergo transformation: thus music arises. Only after understanding Heaven and earth can one bring ritual and music to flourishing. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that the Minister of Rites uses the products of Heaven to develop yin virtue, regulating it through balanced ritual, and the products of earth to develop yang virtue, regulating it through harmonious music. There are palaces and chambers, carriages and conveyances for accommodation; upper and lower garments, ceremonial crowns and caps for dress; wine vessels and cups, offering stands and dishes for implements; and metal, stone, silk, and bamboo instruments for music. Whether proceeding to the suburban altars and ancestral temples, presiding at court, serving the spirits, or governing the people, everything derives from ritual and music. All under Heaven comfortably grow accustomed to these practices and observe them, unaware of how they are thereby led toward goodness and away from wrongdoing, until these practices become established customs.
After the Three Dynasties, antiquity’s institutions suffered alteration under Qin. Han, Tang, and Song successively possessed the realm. If we examine their designations and titles, ranks and precedence, institutions of state, palaces, carriages, clothing, and implements, although there were revisions among them, they could not rise above …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
遠復三代之隆大抵率其時俗安於苟簡
而已如漢高祖嘗有意於興禮矣而魯兩
生不肯行叔孫通爲綿蕝之儀多仍秦之
舊習曹襃繼之取法舊典雜以五經讖記
之文特以補綿蕝之遺耳唐太宗嘗有意
於興禮矣而當隋隳滅之餘房玄齡有禮
文之獻名爲貞觀禮無忌繼之增益舊儀
作爲顯慶禮特以輯貞觀之畧耳韋公肅
錄開元禮爲禮閣新儀後王彥威爲曲臺
===
新禮以繼之唐非無禮也劉溫叟取唐開
元禮爲開寶通禮後王皡撰禮閣新編以
繼之宋非無禮也是漢唐宋君臣所議之
禮其間雖有損益之不同謂之合於古禮
可乎漢武帝時王禹受河間樂有二十四
卷之獻劉向則校書二十三篇計其所存
者僅有樂記樂本樂詩等諸篇而已其樂
奏樂品樂始等篇無傳焉及大祝迎神於
廟門奏嘉至入廟門奏永至而見其行步
punctuated: 遠復三代之隆，大抵率其時俗，安於苟簡而已。如漢高祖嘗有意於興禮矣，而魯兩生不肯行。叔孫通爲綿蕝之儀，多仍秦之舊習；曹襃繼之，取法舊典，雜以五經讖記之文，特以補綿蕝之遺耳。唐太宗嘗有意於興禮矣，而當隋隳滅之餘，房玄齡有禮文之獻，名爲《貞觀禮》。無忌繼之，增益舊儀，作爲《顯慶禮》，特以輯貞觀之畧耳。韋公肅錄《開元禮》爲《禮閣新儀》，後王彥威爲《曲臺新禮》以繼之，唐非無禮也。劉溫叟取唐《開元禮》爲《開寶通禮》，後王皡撰《禮閣新編》以繼之，宋非無禮也。是漢唐宋君臣所議之禮，其間雖有損益之不同，謂之合於古禮，可乎？漢武帝時，王禹受河間樂，有二十四卷之獻；劉向則校書二十三篇。計其所存者，僅有《樂記》《樂本》《樂詩》等諸篇而已，其《樂奏》《樂品》《樂始》等篇無傳焉。及大祝迎神於廟門，奏《嘉至》；入廟門，奏《永至》，而見其行步
translation_en:
…to reach back to the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties. For the most part, they merely followed the customs of their own times and rested content with makeshift simplicity. Emperor Gaozu of Han, for example, once intended to revive ritual, but the two scholars of Lu refused to go. Shusun Tong devised ceremonies using cords and bundles of grass to mark positions, largely retaining the old practices of Qin. Cao Bao followed him, taking ancient canons as his models and mixing in passages from prophetic writings associated with the Five Classics; he merely supplied what Shusun Tong’s ceremonies had omitted. Emperor Taizong of Tang likewise intended to revive ritual. In the aftermath of the Sui dynasty’s collapse, Fang Xuanling presented ritual texts entitled the Rituals of the Zhenguan Era. Wuji followed him, expanding the old ceremonies to produce the Rituals of the Xianqing Era; he merely filled out the abbreviated provisions of the Zhenguan compilation. Wei Gongsu drew on the Rituals of the Kaiyuan Era to compile the New Ceremonies of the Ritual Office. Later, Wang Yanwei followed this with the New Rituals of the Qutai. The Tang was certainly not without ritual. Liu Wensou drew on the Tang Rituals of the Kaiyuan Era to compile the Comprehensive Rituals of the Kaibao Era. Later, Wang Hao followed this with the New Compilation of the Ritual Office. The Song was certainly not without ritual. Such were the rituals deliberated upon by the rulers and ministers of Han, Tang, and Song. Although their additions and omissions differed, can these rituals be said to accord with ancient ritual?

During the reign of Emperor Wu of Han, Wang Yu received the musical tradition of Hejian and presented it in twenty-four scrolls; Liu Xiang, for his part, collated twenty-three chapters. Of these, only such chapters as the Record of Music, the Foundations of Music, and the Poetry of Music survive. Chapters such as the Performance of Music, the Categories of Music, and the Origins of Music have not been transmitted. When the Grand Invocator welcomed the spirits at the temple gate, Auspicious Arrival was performed; upon entering the temple gate, Eternal Arrival was performed, revealing the manner of their measured steps…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之節既饗登歌奏休成就酒東廂奏永安
而見其事神之禮此漢樂之可考者也唐
有祭畢而還之樂在貞觀則有十二和在
開元又益之十五和此唐樂之可考者也
是漢唐宋君臣所議之樂雖有詳畧之不
同謂之合於古樂可乎至魏黃初所定之
儀晉天始所更之制與梁武帝五禮之裁
成隋文帝北齊之取法名雖不同而其失
實則一焉劉宋終獻之樂以永爲名蕭梁
===
出入以雅爲名與陳所用之韶隋所用之
夏號雖不同而其弃義則一焉是五季所
議之禮樂又非漢唐宋之可比矣是何也
君子曰甘受和白受采忠信之人可以學
禮苟非其人道不虛行得其人之爲貴也
若漢高祖之規模宏遠唐太宗之萬目畢
舉宋太祖之忠厚立國卓然爲三代以下
令主非不足與於中和也但漢雜霸唐雜
夷宋亦不能無疵雖有安民濟世之功而
punctuated:
之節。既饗，登歌奏休成，就酒東廂奏永安，而見其事神之禮。此漢樂之可考者也。唐有祭畢而還之樂，在貞觀則有十二和，在開元又益之十五和。此唐樂之可考者也。是漢唐宋君臣所議之樂，雖有詳畧之不同，謂之合於古樂可乎？至魏黃初所定之儀、晉天始所更之制，與梁武帝五禮之裁成、隋文帝北齊之取法，名雖不同，而其失實則一焉。劉宋終獻之樂以永爲名，蕭梁出入以雅爲名，與陳所用之韶、隋所用之夏，號雖不同，而其弃義則一焉。是五季所議之禮樂，又非漢唐宋之可比矣。是何也？
君子曰：「甘受和，白受采，忠信之人可以學禮。」苟非其人，道不虛行，得其人之爲貴也。若漢高祖之規模宏遠、唐太宗之萬目畢舉、宋太祖之忠厚立國，卓然爲三代以下令主，非不足與於中和也。但漢雜霸，唐雜夷，宋亦不能無疵，雖有安民濟世之功，而
translation_en:
…the measured rhythm of their steps. Once the offerings had been presented, the singers ascending the hall performed Xiucheng (Perfect Fulfillment); when wine was taken in the eastern wing, they performed Yong’an (Lasting Peace). In these practices one can discern their rites for serving the spirits. These are the ascertainable features of Han music. The Tang had music for returning after the completion of sacrifices. In the Zhenguan era there were the Twelve Harmonies, and in the Kaiyuan era these were increased to Fifteen Harmonies. These are the ascertainable features of Tang music. Thus, although the music deliberated upon by the rulers and ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song differed in its degree of elaboration, can it be said to accord with ancient music? As for the ceremonies established in the Huangchu era of Wei, the institutions revised in the Tianshi [?] era of Jin, Emperor Wu of Liang’s formulation of the Five Rites, and Emperor Wen of Sui’s adoption of Northern Qi as his model, their names differed, but their loss of the true substance was the same. The music for the final offering under the Liu Song used yong (perpetuity) in its titles; that for entrances and exits under the Xiao Liang used ya (elegance). Together with the Shao used by Chen and the Xia used by Sui, these differed in designation, but were alike in abandoning the underlying meaning. The rites and music deliberated upon in these five dynasties [?] cannot even be compared with those of the Han, Tang, and Song. Why is this?
The gentleman says: “Sweetness receives the blending of flavors; white receives colors. A loyal and trustworthy person can learn ritual.” Without the right person, the Way does not put itself into practice: hence the importance of finding the right person. Consider Han Gaozu’s grand and far-reaching designs, Tang Taizong’s attention to every detail of government, and Song Taizu’s founding of his state upon loyalty and generosity. They stood out as excellent rulers since the Three Dynasties; it was not that they lacked the capacity to participate in equilibrium and harmony. Yet the Han mingled hegemonic methods into its rule, the Tang mingled foreign ways into its rule, and the Song, too, could not be free of flaws. Although they achieved the pacification of the people and brought relief to the age, yet …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
無躬行心得之實欲作禮樂以事鬼神諧
萬民致百物吾見其難矣所謂見禮知政
聞樂知德者不其然與洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺
天眷命用夏變夷
恢復文明之統蕩除腥穢之風治定制禮
開國之治何治也功成作樂
奠安宇宙之功何功也萬古之綱常旣立
一代之創始自明觀天下初定即
===
開禮樂二局旣
命儒臣陶凱等撰
郊祀禘祫等禮又招俊乂梁寅等編集
大明集禮等書
觀心有亭
精誠有錄此禮樂之在於心身者也嚴
郊廟之祀肅
宮闈之禁此禮樂之脩於其家者也
君臣同遊即虞廷之都俞學士醉歌即小雅之
punctuated:
無躬行心得之實，欲作禮樂以事鬼神、諧萬民、致百物，吾見其難矣。所謂見禮知政、聞樂知德者，不其然與？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，膺天眷命，用夏變夷，恢復文明之統，蕩除腥穢之風。治定制禮，開國之治何治也！功成作樂，奠安宇宙之功何功也！萬古之綱常旣立，一代之創始自明。觀天下初定，即開禮樂二局；旣命儒臣陶凱等撰郊祀禘祫等禮，又招俊乂梁寅等編集《大明集禮》等書。觀心有亭，精誠有錄，此禮樂之在於心身者也。嚴郊廟之祀，肅宮闈之禁，此禮樂之脩於其家者也。君臣同遊，即虞廷之都俞；學士醉歌，即小雅之
translation_en:
…yet they lacked the substance of personal practice and inward understanding. If they wished to institute rites and music to serve spirits, bring harmony to the myriad people, and bring all things to fulfillment, I see how difficult this would have been. As the saying goes, one knows a government by observing its rites and knows its virtue by hearing its music. Is this not so?
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who received Heaven’s gracious mandate and transformed the barbarians through Chinese civilization, restoring the succession of civilized rule and sweeping away foul and polluted customs. Once order was established, he instituted rites: how magnificent was the governance with which he founded the dynasty! Once his achievements were complete, he created music: how magnificent was his achievement in securing peace throughout the universe! With the guiding relationships and enduring moral norms established for all ages, the founding institutions of the dynasty became manifest. Consider how, as soon as the realm was pacified, he established two bureaus for rites and music. He commissioned the Confucian official Tao Kai and others to draw up rites for the suburban sacrifices and the di and xia collective ancestral sacrifices, and also summoned outstanding men such as Liang Yin to compile the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming and other books. For examining the mind, there was a pavilion; for perfect sincerity, there was a record. These were rites and music embodied in his mind and person. He made the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices solemn and enforced strict prohibitions within the palace’s inner quarters. These were rites and music cultivated within his household. Sovereign and ministers taking their pleasure together recalled the approving exchanges at Shun’s court; Hanlin academicians singing in their cups recalled the Lesser Odes’…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
周行此禮樂之宣於
朝廷者也由是而正神祇之號均父母之服
禁兄弟之婚定上下之式宗周官讀法以
行鄉社遵朱子家禮以行民間而禮達之
天下矣
大祀樂章則
親御宸藻大成樂器則頒習庠校俾泠謙正
舞佾之位及詹同製燕享之辭厭前代鄙
陋容悅之聲禁胡虜諠淫舞隊之戲而樂
===
無不正矣中庸曰君子之道本諸身徵諸
庶民考諸三王而不謬建諸天地而不悖
質諸鬼神而無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑
我
朝禮樂監視前代損益百王其冠古而獨盛
者乎嗣是而後
列聖相承益彰繼述肆惟
皇上懋德格天纘承丕緒
純心守敬一之箴
punctuated:
周行，此禮樂之宣於朝廷者也。由是而正神祇之號，均父母之服，禁兄弟之婚，定上下之式，宗周官讀法以行鄉社，遵朱子家禮以行民間，而禮達之天下矣。大祀樂章，則親御宸藻；大成樂器，則頒習庠校。俾泠謙正舞佾之位，及詹同製燕享之辭，厭前代鄙陋容悅之聲，禁胡虜諠淫舞隊之戲，而樂無不正矣。
中庸曰：「君子之道，本諸身，徵諸庶民，考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑。」我朝禮樂，監視前代，損益百王，其冠古而獨盛者乎！嗣是而後，列聖相承，益彰繼述。肆惟皇上懋德格天，纘承丕緒，純心守敬一之箴。
translation_en:
…the “perfect way” of the Minor Odes: this was ritual and music given expression at court. Thereupon, the titles of the celestial and terrestrial deities were rectified, mourning observances for fathers and mothers were equalized, marriages between brothers and sisters were prohibited, and prescribed forms for superiors and inferiors were established. The reading of laws described in the Offices of Zhou was adopted for local communities, and Master Zhu’s Family Rituals were followed among the common people. Thus ritual reached throughout the realm. For the musical texts of the great sacrifices, the emperor personally wielded his literary brush; instruments for the music of Great Perfection were distributed to schools for practice. He had Ling Qian [?] correct the positions of the ranks of dancers and Zhan Tong compose lyrics for court banquets. He rejected the vulgar, debased music of earlier dynasties that sought to curry favor, and prohibited the clamorous, licentious performances of barbarian dance troupes. Thus all music was rectified.
The Doctrine of the Mean says: “The gentleman’s way is rooted in his own person and verified among the common people. Tested against the Three Kings, it is without error; established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; submitted to the spirits, it leaves no doubt; and it can await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgiving.” The ritual and music of our dynasty take earlier dynasties as their model [?], subtracting from and adding to the practices of the many kings. Do they not surpass antiquity in their unparalleled splendor? Thereafter, the successive sage emperors carried on this inheritance, ever more fully displaying their continuation of their predecessors’ work. Now His Majesty cultivates virtue that reaches Heaven and succeeds to the great imperial undertaking, purifying his mind and observing the Admonition on Reverence and Unity…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
脩身建中和之極由是
天地爲昭人文載啓首以綱常爲重也纂脩
明倫大典則
簡命儒臣焉復以典則當詒也重脩
大明會典則歸之史館焉他如
勑諭輔臣更正典禮定
丘澤之方位配
日月之晨昏嶽瀆從類而
社稷各處其尊
===
祖考攸崇而
帝王則歸本廟
欽天有頌
大報有歌除夕有詠
平臺有作皆裁自
聖心協義而協所謂與
天地合德日月合明四時合序鬼神合吉凶者
也仰覩俯察彬彬焉洋洋焉如
今日之盛誠千古一時矣但樂書不傳古樂
punctuated: 脩身建中和之極，由是天地爲昭，人文載啓。首以綱常爲重也，纂脩《明倫大典》，則簡命儒臣焉；復以典則當詒也，重脩《大明會典》，則歸之史館焉。他如勑諭輔臣，更正典禮，定丘澤之方位，配日月之晨昏，嶽瀆從類，而社稷各處其尊；祖考攸崇，而帝王則歸本廟。《欽天》有頌，《大報》有歌，除夕有詠，平臺有作，皆裁自聖心，協義而協，所謂與天地合德、日月合明、四時合序、鬼神合吉凶者也。仰覩俯察，彬彬焉，洋洋焉！如今日之盛，誠千古一時矣。但樂書不傳，古樂
translation_en:
…cultivating his person and establishing the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. Thus Heaven and Earth shine forth, and civilized culture is renewed. First, regarding the cardinal bonds and constant virtues as paramount, he commissioned the compilation of the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), selecting and appointing Confucian officials for the task. Further, regarding institutional standards as something to be handed down, he entrusted the Historiography Office with revising the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian). Other measures included commanding his chief ministers to correct ceremonial institutions, determining the locations and orientations of the altars to Heaven and Earth, assigning the sacrifices to the sun and moon to morning and evening respectively, grouping the sacred mountains and waterways by category, and giving the gods of soil and grain their respective places of honor. Imperial ancestors received due veneration, while emperors and kings of earlier ages were assigned to their own temples.

There were odes on revering Heaven, songs for the Great Sacrifice of Recompense, verses for New Year’s Eve, and compositions at the Platform. All were fashioned by the imperial mind, according with righteousness and in accord [?]. This is what is meant by matching Heaven and Earth in virtue, the sun and moon in brightness, the four seasons in their order, and the spirits in their auspicious and inauspicious workings. Whether we look upward or examine what is below, how refined and how abundant it all is! Such flourishing as we enjoy today truly occurs but once in a thousand ages. Yet the books on music have not been transmitted, and ancient music…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
莫考非所當脩復以彰
功德之盛而媲典謨之美者乎記曰五帝殊
時不相沿樂三王異世不相襲禮必待后
夔而後作樂師曠而後審音豈理也哉世
無后夔師曠而后夔之心師曠之耳今不
異於古也昔宋季改鑄鍾磬徐復笑之以
爲聖人寓器以聲當先求其聲而不必更
其器正謂此耳故孟子曰今之樂猶古之
樂也試使知樂者由今之器寄古之聲如
===
蔡元定之律呂新書朱子之通解鍾律可
考而知也如呂氏春秋通鑑外紀及隋志
所載黃鍾含少之數與朱蔡異者可按而
校也依俗法之所移換尋古調之所抑揚
然後被之絲竹吹之以竹宣之以金收之
以石作於一堂之上而有應和之美則有
以開萬世之和平與古帝王異世同符而
鳳儀獸舞將特見於
今日矣愚敢以爲
punctuated: 莫考，非所當脩復，以彰功德之盛，而媲典謨之美者乎？記曰：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異世，不相襲禮。」必待后夔而後作樂，師曠而後審音，豈理也哉？世無后夔、師曠，而后夔之心、師曠之耳，今不異於古也。昔宋季改鑄鍾磬，徐復笑之，以爲聖人寓器以聲，當先求其聲，而不必更其器，正謂此耳。故孟子曰：「今之樂，猶古之樂也。」試使知樂者由今之器寄古之聲，如蔡元定之《律呂新書》、朱子之《通解》，鍾律可考而知也。如《呂氏春秋》、《通鑑外紀》及《隋志》所載黃鍾含少之數，與朱、蔡異者，可按而校也。依俗法之所移換，尋古調之所抑揚，然後被之絲竹，吹之以竹，宣之以金，收之以石，作於一堂之上，而有應和之美，則有以開萬世之和平，與古帝王異世同符，而鳳儀獸舞，將特見於今日矣。愚敢以爲
translation_en: …cannot be investigated. Should it not be restored, to manifest the fullness of imperial achievement and virtue and rival the beauty of the Canons and Counsels? The Record of Rites says: “The Five Emperors lived at different times and did not perpetuate one another’s music; the Three Kings lived in different ages and did not inherit one another’s rites.” Must we await a Hou Kui before composing music, or a Shi Kuang before discerning tones? How could that be reasonable? Although the world has no Hou Kui or Shi Kuang, minds like Hou Kui’s and ears like Shi Kuang’s are no different today from those of antiquity. Formerly, in the closing years of the Song, when bells and chime stones were recast [?], Xu Fu laughed at this. He held that the sages embodied sound in instruments: one should first seek the sound, without necessarily replacing the instruments. This was precisely his point. Thus Mengzi said: “The music of today is like the music of antiquity.” Let those who understand music try to convey ancient sounds through present-day instruments. Works such as Cai Yuanding’s New Book on the Pitch Standards and Master Zhu’s Comprehensive Explanations allow the pitch standards for bells to be investigated and understood. Numerical values for the Huangzhong pitch, including the lesser [?], recorded in Master Lü’s Spring and Autumn Annals, the Outer Annals of the Comprehensive Mirror, and the Treatises of the Book of Sui, which differ from those of Zhu and Cai, can be examined and compared. Follow the transpositions of current practice and seek the rise and fall of ancient melodies. Then set them to strings and winds: sound them through bamboo, proclaim them through metal, and bring them to a close with stone. When performed together in a single hall with the beauty of mutual response and harmony, they will usher in peace and concord for ten thousand generations. Though belonging to a different age, the present will accord with the ancient emperors and kings; phoenixes appearing in stately grace and beasts dancing will be witnessed especially in our own day. I humbly venture to offer this as …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖明獻
第三問　　王陽生
同考試官教諭毛　批〔射禮一策正欲究士子觀德之學場中作者不失之昧則失之踈漫不知〕
〔爲何物子能酌古準今以實心實政歸本言之有用之學也取之取之〕
同考試官教諭黄　批〔射藝之格久矣主司發策探其留心否也子能歷舉成周之政而發揚〕
===
聖明之治可謂不專章句者矣然則子非文武之才也邪
考試官教諭林　批〔讀子之策鑿鑿可行非徒事博洽者〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔能條荅詳明足占所蘊〕
聖王之以射教天下也非故漫然而強人以太勞也蓋必有文焉以爲淑世之具有本焉以爲出治之基文者何儀章度數是已本者何恭敬溫和是已是故無本不立無文不行先王導民善俗之政靡不由之
punctuated:
聖明獻。

第三問　王陽生

同考試官教諭毛批〔射禮一策，正欲究士子觀德之學。場中作者，不失之昧，則失之踈漫，不知爲何物。子能酌古準今，以實心實政歸本，言之有用之學也。取之，取之！〕

同考試官教諭黄批〔射藝之格久矣。主司發策，探其留心否也。子能歷舉成周之政，而發揚聖明之治，可謂不專章句者矣。然則子非文武之才也邪？

考試官教諭林批〔讀子之策，鑿鑿可行，非徒事博洽者。〕

考試官教諭敖批〔能條荅詳明，足占所蘊。〕

聖王之以射教天下也，非故漫然而強人以太勞也。蓋必有文焉，以爲淑世之具；有本焉，以爲出治之基。文者何？儀章度數是已。本者何？恭敬溫和是已。是故無本不立，無文不行。先王導民善俗之政，靡不由之。
translation_en:
…to present to Your enlightened Majesty.

Third Policy Question — Wang Yangsheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “This policy question on the archery rites was intended precisely to investigate candidates’ understanding of how virtue is observed through archery. Those writing in the examination hall have fallen either into ignorance or into such careless vagueness that one cannot tell what they mean. You have weighed antiquity against present circumstances and traced the matter to its foundations in sincerity of heart and substantive government. What you say exemplifies learning that can be put to use. Accept him, accept him!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The practice of archery has long been in abeyance [?]. The presiding examiners posed this policy question to discover whether candidates had given it attention. You have enumerated the institutions of the Zhou at its height and extolled the government of our enlightened sovereign. You may indeed be called someone whose learning is not confined to textual exegesis. Are you not, then, a man of both civil and military talent?”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Reading your policy essay, I find its proposals concrete and practicable. You do not merely pursue breadth of erudition.”

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: “Your ability to answer point by point, fully and clearly, gives ample evidence of the learning you possess.”

When the sage kings taught all under Heaven through archery, they were not acting arbitrarily and deliberately forcing people into excessive exertion. There must have been outward forms that served as instruments for improving the world, and a foundation that served as the basis from which good government emerged. What were these outward forms? Ceremonial forms and prescribed measures. What was the foundation? Reverence, respect, gentleness, and harmony. Thus, without a foundation, the practice could not be established; without outward forms, it could not be carried out. All the former kings’ measures for guiding the people and improving their customs proceeded from these principles.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
此其所以卓越萬代而非漢唐宋可追也
且射之義何昉乎伏羲神農開物成務于
天下久矣其時猶未有射也乃若弧矢之
作始於黃帝侯明之典見於虞書夏商無
文周制大備時則有若周公制禮作樂以
相成王之治於是乎射義之所由起焉自
今觀之其在當時一曰大射天子將祭于
羣臣諸侯習禮則然也二曰賓射諸侯來
朝天子入而與射也三曰燕射天子與羣
===
臣燕息之射也四曰鄉射卿大夫貢賢能
之後詢衆庶而射也是故有六弓焉曰王
弓弧弓夾弓庾弓唐弓大弓之異也有八
矢焉曰枉矢絜矢殺矢鍭矢矰矢茀矢常
矢庳矢之殊也以言其射侯也則天子與
其諸大夫之異侯者所以辨其等也賓射
燕射天子與其諸侯大夫之同侯者所以
一其權也以言其射耦也則天子六耦諸
侯四耦孤卿大夫三耦士二耦而耦則不
punctuated:
此其所以卓越萬代，而非漢唐宋可追也。

且射之義何昉乎？伏羲、神農開物成務于天下久矣，其時猶未有射也。乃若弧矢之作，始於黃帝；侯明之典，見於虞書。夏商無文，周制大備。時則有若周公制禮作樂，以相成王之治，於是乎射義之所由起焉。自今觀之，其在當時，一曰大射，天子將祭，于羣臣諸侯習禮則然也；二曰賓射，諸侯來朝，天子入而與射也；三曰燕射，天子與羣臣燕息之射也；四曰鄉射，卿大夫貢賢能之後，詢衆庶而射也。是故有六弓焉，曰王弓、弧弓、夾弓、庾弓、唐弓、大弓之異也；有八矢焉，曰枉矢、絜矢、殺矢、鍭矢、矰矢、茀矢、常矢、庳矢之殊也。以言其射侯也，則天子與其諸大夫之異侯者，所以辨其等也；賓射、燕射，天子與其諸侯大夫之同侯者，所以一其權也。以言其射耦也，則天子六耦，諸侯四耦，孤卿大夫三耦，士二耦，而耦則不
translation_en:
This is why it surpassed all subsequent ages, beyond anything the Han, Tang, or Song could equal.

Now, where did the ritual significance of archery originate? Fuxi and Shennong had long ago opened up the resources of the world and brought human undertakings to completion, yet in their time archery did not exist. The making of bows and arrows began with the Yellow Emperor; the precedent for making virtue manifest through the target appears in the Documents of Yu. No written account survives from the Xia and Shang, but under the Zhou the institutions became fully developed. Then the Duke of Zhou established rites and composed music to assist King Cheng’s government: this was the origin of archery’s ritual significance. Looking back from the present, there were four forms at that time. The first was the Great Archery Ceremony: when the Son of Heaven was about to offer sacrifice, he rehearsed the rites with his officials and the feudal lords. The second was Guest Archery: when the feudal lords came to court, the Son of Heaven entered and shot with them. The third was Festive Archery: the Son of Heaven shot with his officials during their leisure. The fourth was District Archery: after ministers and grand masters had recommended worthy and capable men, they consulted the populace and held an archery ceremony. Thus there were six distinct kinds of bow, called wang, hu, jia, yu, tang, and da; and eight distinct kinds of arrow, called wang, jie, sha, hou, zeng, fu, chang, and bi. As for the archery targets, the Son of Heaven and his grand masters used different targets to distinguish their ranks. In Guest Archery and Festive Archery, the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, and the grand masters used the same targets to place them on an equal footing. As for the pairs of archers, the Son of Heaven had six pairs, the feudal lords four pairs, junior guardians, ministers, and grand masters three pairs, and servicemen two pairs; thus the numbers of pairs were not …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
同也以言其射地也則天子於郊諸侯於
境大夫於鄉士於學而地則不同也天子
百二十步諸侯九十步大夫七十步士五
十步明尊卑所服有遠近也天子合九而
成規諸侯合七而成規大夫合五而成規
士合三而成規明尊卑所統有廣狹也然
猶未也天子以騶虞為節騶虞者樂官備
也諸侯以貍首為節貍首者樂會時也卿
大夫以采蘋為節采蘋者樂循法度也士
以采蘩為節采蘩者樂不失職也是故古
===
之射者則然也此天下師門弟子學士疇
人攷之於古質之於周禮可見矣然其數
可陳也其義難知也執事欲得其義乎蓋
射者男子之事有四方之志而飾之以禮
樂者也天子既以三射擇人而又澤宮以
選士鄉射以教士其容體比於禮節奏
比於樂焉其中多者得與于祭其容體不
比於樂焉其中多者得與于祭其容體不
比于禮節奏不比于樂而中少者不得與
punctuated: 同也。以言其射地也，則天子於郊，諸侯於境，大夫於鄉，士於學，而地則不同也。天子百二十步，諸侯九十步，大夫七十步，士五十步，明尊卑所服有遠近也。天子合九而成規，諸侯合七而成規，大夫合五而成規，士合三而成規，明尊卑所統有廣狹也。然猶未也。天子以騶虞為節，騶虞者，樂官備也；諸侯以貍首為節，貍首者，樂會時也；卿大夫以采蘋為節，采蘋者，樂循法度也；士以采蘩為節，采蘩者，樂不失職也。是故古之射者則然也。此天下師門弟子、學士疇人，攷之於古，質之於周禮，可見矣。然其數可陳也，其義難知也。執事欲得其義乎？蓋射者，男子之事，有四方之志，而飾之以禮樂者也。天子既以三射擇人，而又澤宮以選士，鄉射以教士。其容體比於禮，節奏比於樂焉，其中多者得與于祭；其容體不比於樂焉，其中多者得與于祭；其容體不比于禮，節奏不比于樂，而中少者不得與
translation_en:
…differ. As for the places where archery is performed, the Son of Heaven shoots in the suburbs, the feudal lords within their borders, the great officers in their districts, and the shi in their schools: their shooting grounds thus differ. The distance is 120 paces for the Son of Heaven, ninety for the feudal lords, seventy for the great officers, and fifty for the shi, showing that the distances prescribed vary according to rank. For the Son of Heaven, nine are joined to form a circle; for the feudal lords, seven; for the great officers, five; and for the shi, three [?]. This shows that the scope of their authority varies in breadth according to rank. Nor is this all. The Son of Heaven shoots to the rhythm of “The Z Zou Beast” (Zouyu), which expresses joy that all official posts are filled; the feudal lords shoot to “The Wildcat’s Head” (Lishou), which expresses joy in assembling at the proper time; ministers and great officers shoot to “Gathering Duckweed” (Caiping), which expresses joy in following laws and standards; and the shi shoot to “Gathering White Southernwood” (Caifan), which expresses joy in not neglecting one’s duties. Such was archery in antiquity.

Disciples of teachers throughout the realm, scholars, and specialists can see this by investigating antiquity and checking it against the Rites of Zhou. Yet although its prescribed particulars can be set forth, their meaning is difficult to understand. Do you, honored sir, wish to grasp that meaning? Archery is a man’s undertaking: it embodies aspirations toward the four quarters and is adorned with ritual and music. The Son of Heaven not only chose men through the three forms of archery, but also selected shi at the Archery Palace and instructed them through district archery. Those whose bearing conformed to ritual, whose movements kept time with the music, and who scored many hits were permitted to participate in sacrifices. “Those whose bearing did not conform to the music, and who scored many hits, were permitted to participate in sacrifices” [?—the transcription repeats part of the preceding passage]. Those whose bearing did not conform to ritual, whose movements did not keep time with the music, and who scored few hits were not permitted to participate…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
于祭其敘進於射也又曰射中而多者得
爲諸侯射不中而少者不得爲諸侯故曰
射者射爲諸侯也是以君臣盡志於射以
習禮樂故當其時教化興行人才衆多致
治之盛光映簡冊有由爾哉嬴秦焚籍古
典盡湮後之君臣有志射禮者吾陋焉漢
之明帝習大射於辟雍矣唐之高祖行大
射于殿廷矣太宗貞觀則演於武德殿前
玄宗開元則行于景福樓下此四君者非
===
不銳然于古也然不過侈圜橋之聚觀逞
雄心于一試是乃爭能較勝之意而非尚
德序賢之舉噫亦末矣至晉之庾亮于武
昌作帥也行鄉射之禮倣古周制親執其
事而洋洋有洙泗之風漢之劉昆陳留野
儒也教授弟子春秋饗射備列典儀桑弧
蒿矢以射菟首而縣宰率屬以觀此二臣
者亦可謂有志矣然徒慕其名而不究其
實行於暫而不能持於久要之習於苟簡
punctuated: 于祭，其敘進於射也。又曰：「射中而多者得爲諸侯，射不中而少者不得爲諸侯。」故曰：「射者，射爲諸侯也。」是以君臣盡志於射，以習禮樂。故當其時，教化興行，人才衆多，致治之盛，光映簡冊，有由爾哉！嬴秦焚籍，古典盡湮。後之君臣有志射禮者，吾陋焉。漢之明帝習大射於辟雍矣，唐之高祖行大射于殿廷矣，太宗貞觀則演於武德殿前，玄宗開元則行于景福樓下。此四君者，非不銳然于古也，然不過侈圜橋之聚觀，逞雄心于一試，是乃爭能較勝之意，而非尚德序賢之舉。噫，亦末矣！至晉之庾亮于武昌作帥也，行鄉射之禮，倣古周制，親執其事，而洋洋有洙泗之風。漢之劉昆，陳留野儒也，教授弟子，春秋饗射，備列典儀，桑弧蒿矢以射菟首，而縣宰率屬以觀。此二臣者，亦可謂有志矣，然徒慕其名，而不究其實，行於暫，而不能持於久。要之，習於苟簡
translation_en:
…in the sacrifice; their advancement in rank depended upon archery. It also says: “Those who hit the target many times may become regional lords; those who fail to hit it and score few hits may not become regional lords.” Thus it is said: “In archery, one shoots to become a regional lord.” Hence rulers and ministers devoted themselves fully to archery in order to practice rites and music. Thus, in those days, moral instruction flourished and men of talent abounded. There was indeed a reason why the splendor of their good government shone so brilliantly in the historical records!

When the Qin of the Ying house burned the books, the ancient canons were entirely lost. As for subsequent rulers and ministers who aspired to revive the archery rites, I find them wanting. Emperor Ming of Han practiced the Great Archery Ceremony at the Biyong ceremonial academy. Gaozu of Tang performed it in the palace court. During Taizong’s Zhenguan reign, it was conducted before Wude Hall; during Xuanzong’s Kaiyuan reign, beneath Jingfu Tower. These four rulers certainly showed enthusiasm for antiquity. Yet they did no more than make a lavish spectacle for the crowds gathered at the encircling bridge and display their prowess in a single contest. Their intention was to compete in skill and vie for victory, rather than to honor virtue and rank the worthy. Alas, how superficial!

When Yu Liang of Jin served as military commander at Wuchang, he performed the district archery rite, following the ancient institutions of Zhou and personally directing the proceedings. These amply evoked the spirit of the Zhu and Si rivers, the homeland of Confucius. Liu Kun of Han, a scholar of Chenliu holding no office, taught disciples and held feasts and archery ceremonies in spring and autumn, setting out the full ceremonial arrangements. They shot at a rabbit-head target with mulberry bows and mugwort arrows, while the district magistrate led his subordinates to watch. These two subjects may also be said to have had worthy aspirations. Yet they merely admired the name without investigating the substance, practicing it briefly without being able to sustain it for long. In sum, habituated to makeshift and perfunctory practices…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
格於時勢亦無補於觀德之舉也故曰苟
非其人道不虛行其是之謂乎肆我
國家
太祖創造鴻業
成祖丕隆善治
訏謨度越乎百王
睿見超出乎千古
即位之初常
令羣臣以時合射天下甫定遂
===
詔內成均博士弟子員及郡縣庠序之士皆
建圃習射于學宮今
大明集禮所載至爲明備即成周鄉射之遺意
其於先王之禮教人以立德行習禮樂蓋
先後一揆異世同符所當服行無斁者也
我
皇上神聖御極禮樂作人菁莪棫樸之化恭敬
仁讓之俗彬彬焉洋洋焉與三代同風而
射禮一節則又恪遵
punctuated:
格於時勢，亦無補於觀德之舉也。故曰：「苟非其人，道不虛行。」其是之謂乎？
肆我國家，太祖創造鴻業，成祖丕隆善治，訏謨度越乎百王，睿見超出乎千古。即位之初，常令羣臣以時合射；天下甫定，遂詔內成均博士弟子員及郡縣庠序之士，皆建圃習射于學宮。今《大明集禮》所載，至爲明備，即成周鄉射之遺意。其於先王之禮，教人以立德行、習禮樂，蓋先後一揆，異世同符，所當服行無斁者也。
我皇上神聖御極，禮樂作人，菁莪棫樸之化、恭敬仁讓之俗，彬彬焉，洋洋焉，與三代同風。而射禮一節，則又恪遵
translation_en:
…constrained by the circumstances of their times, they likewise contributed nothing to the practice of observing virtue through archery. Thus it is said: “Without the right person, the Way does not put itself into practice.” Is this not precisely what those words mean?
Now, in our dynasty, Taizu founded the great imperial enterprise, and Chengzu greatly advanced good government. Their grand designs surpassed those of a hundred kings; their sagacious insight exceeded that of a thousand ages. At the beginning of his reign, the emperor regularly ordered his assembled ministers to hold archery gatherings at the appropriate seasons. As soon as the realm was pacified, he commanded the enrolled students of the Imperial University at the capital and the scholars of prefectural and county schools all to establish archery grounds and practise archery at their schools. The provisions now recorded in the Collected Rites of the Great Ming are exceptionally clear and comprehensive, preserving the intent of the district archery ceremonies of Zhou. In using the rites of the former kings to teach people to establish virtuous conduct and to practise ritual and music, these provisions follow the same standard as their ancient predecessors and accord across the ages. They should be put into practice without weariness.
Our august emperor, divinely sage, occupies the imperial throne and cultivates men through ritual and music. His transforming influence resembles that celebrated in “Luxuriant Wormwood” (Jing e) and “Oak Clumps” (Yu pu), fostering worthy talent; the customs of reverence, respect, benevolence, and deference are refined and flourishing, sharing the spirit of the Three Dynasties. As for the particular matter of the archery rites, he also scrupulously observes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
成憲敦崇古制尚行而不尚文師意而不泥
迹使天下章縫之士頌讀之餘詣圃而習
射亦既敦行愆讓矣然臣下遵行日久未
免有偏而不舉之處學舍鞠爲蔬圃士風
流於鹵莽觀德之意寖失其初宜釐執事
之問也豈任事者執古以好奇通變之或
缺業舉者隨時以遷就苟簡之是襲乎記
曰作者之謂聖述者之謂明明聖者述作
之謂也則夫振厲作新之機化民成俗之
===
洽宜我
聖心之惓惓而不能以自已焉者邇者
皇上因撫臣之建白禮官之覆請
慨然嘉納遍行兩京國子及天下諸學一倣
大明集禮督令生徒朔望習行甚盛意也一時
人士得於耳目觀感之餘有不丕應傒志
向風承德乎然善俗者法也行法者道也
故純心乃善治之原而至誠爲參贊之本
然則脩明之政惟以實心行之焉耳何也
punctuated:
成憲，敦崇古制，尚行而不尚文，師意而不泥迹，使天下章縫之士頌讀之餘，詣圃而習射，亦既敦行愆讓矣。然臣下遵行日久，未免有偏而不舉之處，學舍鞠爲蔬圃，士風流於鹵莽，觀德之意寖失其初，宜釐執事之問也。豈任事者執古以好奇，通變之或缺；業舉者隨時以遷就，苟簡之是襲乎？記曰：「作者之謂聖，述者之謂明。明聖者，述作之謂也。」則夫振厲作新之機、化民成俗之洽，宜我聖心之惓惓而不能以自已焉者。
邇者，皇上因撫臣之建白、禮官之覆請，慨然嘉納，遍行兩京國子及天下諸學，一倣大明集禮，督令生徒朔望習行，甚盛意也。一時人士得於耳目觀感之餘，有不丕應傒志、向風承德乎？然善俗者法也，行法者道也。故純心乃善治之原，而至誠爲參贊之本。然則脩明之政，惟以實心行之焉耳。何也？
translation_en:
…the established statutes, honoring and upholding ancient institutions, valuing practice rather than outward forms, and taking their intent as a guide without clinging to their precedents. Thus scholars throughout the realm, wearing the caps of the learned, go to the grounds to practice archery after their recitation and reading, and have already earnestly practiced humility and deference [?]. Yet as your servants have followed these provisions over time, some aspects have inevitably been pursued unevenly or left unimplemented. School premises have been reduced to vegetable gardens, and scholarly conduct has lapsed into coarseness. The original intent of observing virtue through archery has gradually been lost. These matters ought to be put in order through the inquiries of the officials responsible [?]. Could it be that those charged with administering them cling to antiquity out of a taste for the unusual, failing to adapt to changing circumstances, while those preparing for the examinations accommodate themselves to current habits and merely perpetuate careless shortcuts? The Record of Rites says: “One who originates is called a sage; one who transmits is called discerning. Discernment and sageliness refer to transmitting and originating.” Thus the opportunity to rouse and renew the people, and the thorough transformation of the people and their customs, rightly occupy our sovereign’s sacred mind with a concern that cannot cease.
Recently, in response to a provincial governor’s proposal and the ritual officials’ petition following their review, Your Majesty graciously and readily accepted it. You ordered its implementation at the Directorates of Education in both capitals and at schools throughout the realm, all following the Collected Rites of the Great Ming, and directed that students be supervised in practicing these rites on the first and fifteenth days of each month. This is a most generous intention. Among the scholars of the day, moved by what they hear and see, could any fail to respond wholeheartedly, unite their aspirations [?], turn toward your influence, and receive your virtue? Yet it is regulations that improve customs, and the Way that puts regulations into practice. Hence purity of heart is the source of good government, and utmost sincerity is the foundation for assisting the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. Policies that restore and clarify these rites must therefore simply be carried out with a sincere heart. Why is this so?

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
射者六藝之術三物之教也然變通神化
古諸射禮雖難盡卒行也而鄉射則達之
士人詢于衆庶選其賢能定于澤宫者非
取其有貫革穿札之勇也舍拔覆䈁之捷
也習於容止揖讓而賢不肖以判焉等於
行同能偶而好惡趨舍以分焉本之以和
順從容之心形之而爲發揚蹈厲之節無
事於矜驕誇詡之習而自消乎鄒陋陵躐
之氣仁愛可以推之庭懃焉忠敬可以推
===
之君長焉恂篤可以推之州閭焉慈惠可
以推之民庶焉故曰射者鵠也爲人君者
以爲君鵠爲人臣者以爲臣鵠爲人父者
以爲父鵠爲人子者以爲子鵠鵠者正也
各欲正己而已矣是不可行乎雖然猶有
說焉三代之時上無異教下無異習仁義
並用文武同方比閭族鄙民也亦兵也陳
師鞠旅者將也亦相也周公篤棐而有東
山之征太公鷹揚而有丹書之授伐儉狁
punctuated:
射者，六藝之術、三物之教也。然變通神化，古諸射禮雖難盡卒行也，而鄉射則達之士人。詢于衆庶，選其賢能，定于澤宫者，非取其有貫革穿札之勇也、舍拔覆䈁之捷也。習於容止揖讓，而賢不肖以判焉；等於行同能偶，而好惡趨舍以分焉。本之以和順從容之心，形之而爲發揚蹈厲之節，無事於矜驕誇詡之習，而自消乎鄒陋陵躐之氣。仁愛可以推之庭懃焉，忠敬可以推之君長焉，恂篤可以推之州閭焉，慈惠可以推之民庶焉。故曰：「射者，鵠也。爲人君者，以爲君鵠；爲人臣者，以爲臣鵠；爲人父者，以爲父鵠；爲人子者，以爲子鵠。鵠者，正也，各欲正己而已矣。」是不可行乎？
雖然，猶有說焉。三代之時，上無異教，下無異習，仁義並用，文武同方。比閭族鄙，民也，亦兵也；陳師鞠旅者，將也，亦相也。周公篤棐，而有東山之征；太公鷹揚，而有丹書之授。伐儉狁
translation_en:
Archery is a skill among the Six Arts and part of instruction in the Three Categories. Yet, through adaptation and wondrous transformation, although the various ancient archery rites may be difficult to carry out in their entirety, community archery can be extended to the scholars. Consulting the populace, selecting the worthy and capable, and assessing them at the archery hall are not intended to choose men for their valor in piercing leather and armor plates, or for their dexterity in releasing arrows and overturning bow cases [?]. Through practice in bearing, bowing, and yielding precedence, the worthy are distinguished from the unworthy; through ranking and matching those of equal conduct and ability, their likes and dislikes, inclinations and rejections become distinct. This takes as its foundation a harmonious, compliant, and composed disposition, expressed outwardly in vigorous and spirited movements. Without recourse to pride or boastfulness, the temper of narrow-mindedness [?] and presumptuous overstepping naturally dissipates. Benevolent affection can then be extended to the family [?], loyalty and reverence to rulers and superiors, sincerity and steadfastness to the neighborhood, and kindness and generosity to the common people. Thus it is said: “Archery means taking aim at a target. A ruler takes being a ruler as his target; a minister takes being a minister as his target; a father takes being a father as his target; a son takes being a son as his target. A target means rectitude: each seeks only to set himself right.” Can this not be put into practice?
Even so, there is more to say. In the time of the Three Dynasties, there were no divergent teachings above and no divergent practices below. Benevolence and righteousness were employed together, and civil and military pursuits followed the same course. Those organized into neighborhood and district units were civilians, but also soldiers; those who arrayed armies and mustered troops were generals, but also chief ministers. The Duke of Zhou was devoted in his assistance, yet undertook the eastern campaign celebrated in “Eastern Hills.” The Grand Duke soared like a hawk, yet received the teachings of the “Cinnabar Writing.” Those who attacked the Xianyun [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
者元老之方叔同燕喜者孝友之張仲今
之爲士者呻其佔畢之功沒於帖括之習
視觀德之學爲長物細故漫不加意是以
文之鄙武不識一丁武之誚文徒事文墨
今欲使操觚染翰者一折衝禦侮之能爲
干城腹心者悉兎罝中林之士則澤宮之
制顧不可斟之酌之而一舉乎雖然愚又
有說焉君者民之表上者下之倡也故君
好之民必從之上爲之下必安之風行草
===
偃之勢也然則欲舉先王之實政以成天
下之人才夫豈有他術哉無亦曰加之意
而已我
皇上稽謀自天多聞縱
聖穆清之上春秋之暇倣大閱之制振曠古之
典於大射賔射燕射間一舉之俾中外臣
民有所觀法天下士庶得以率作而又行
鄉射遵
大明集禮以歲考責之督學之憲臣以時練揩
punctuated:
者，元老之方叔；同燕喜者，孝友之張仲。今之爲士者，呻其佔畢之功，沒於帖括之習，視觀德之學爲長物細故，漫不加意。是以文之鄙武，不識一丁；武之誚文，徒事文墨。今欲使操觚染翰者一折衝禦侮之能，爲干城腹心者悉兎罝中林之士，則澤宮之制，顧不可斟之酌之而一舉乎？

雖然，愚又有說焉。君者，民之表；上者，下之倡也。故君好之，民必從之；上爲之，下必安之，風行草偃之勢也。然則欲舉先王之實政，以成天下之人才，夫豈有他術哉？無亦曰加之意而已。我皇上稽謀自天，多聞縱聖，穆清之上，春秋之暇，倣大閱之制，振曠古之典，於大射、賔射、燕射間一舉之，俾中外臣民有所觀法，天下士庶得以率作，而又行鄉射，遵《大明集禮》，以歲考責之督學之憲臣，以時練揩
translation_en:
…was the venerable minister Fang Shu; sharing in the joyous feast was Zhang Zhong, renowned for filial devotion and brotherly affection. Scholars today labor at chanting texts and immerse themselves in examination exercises. They regard the study through which virtue is observed in archery as a superfluity and a trivial matter, giving it no attention. Thus men of letters disparage military men as unable to recognize even a single character, while military men ridicule men of letters for occupying themselves solely with writing. If we now wish those who wield writing tablets and brushes also to possess the ability to repel attacks and resist aggression, and those who serve as the state's shields, walls, and trusted confidants all to be men like the hare-net setters in the forest celebrated in the Odes, could we not deliberate upon the institution of the archery hall and put it into practice?

Nevertheless, I have something further to say. The ruler is the people's model; those above set the example for those below. Hence, whatever the ruler favors, the people will surely follow; whatever those above practice, those below will surely accept. It is as inevitable as grass bending before the wind. If, then, we wish to implement the substantive policies of the former kings and thereby cultivate talented men throughout the realm, could any other method be needed? It is simply a matter of giving this our attention. Our Emperor takes counsel from Heaven; his extensive learning enhances his Heaven-endowed sagacity [?]. From the serene heights of his court, in the leisure afforded by spring and autumn, let him emulate the institution of the grand military review and revive ceremonies long neglected, holding on some occasion a grand archery ceremony, a guest archery ceremony, or a banquet archery ceremony. Officials and people at court and throughout the provinces would thereby have an example to observe and emulate, and scholars and commoners throughout the realm could follow it in practice. Let community archery also be conducted in accordance with the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming, charging the education censor with annual assessments, and, at regular intervals, with practice and correction [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之提調之有司帥之以儒官本之於儀注
俾天下人士身安而體習日劘而月練陶
成于禮樂羅網于科目則士人兼文武之
才
朝廷獲得人之效閭里興遜讓之風觀德之
治尚何有不舉哉夫然後道德一而風俗
同雍熙太和萬物咸若之化遠追唐虞三
代而獨盛於
今日矣愚也何幸親見之
===
第四問
李邦器
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔均田一策作者每無根著獨是篇區晝周悉敷荅明暢其識時務者與宜〕
錄以式
考試官教諭林　批〔策內區處明當而歸于守令之得人知本之論也足占子經濟之畧〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔措詞典則通達治體眞有本之學也佳士佳士〕
punctuated:
之，提調之有司，帥之以儒官，本之於儀注，俾天下人士身安而體習，日劘而月練，陶成于禮樂，羅網于科目。則士人兼文武之才，朝廷獲得人之效，閭里興遜讓之風，觀德之治尚何有不舉哉？夫然後道德一而風俗同，雍熙太和、萬物咸若之化，遠追唐虞三代，而獨盛於今日矣。愚也何幸親見之！

第四問
李邦器
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔均田一策，作者每無根著，獨是篇區晝周悉，敷荅明暢，其識時務者與！宜〕錄以式。
考試官教諭林　批〔策內區處明當，而歸于守令之得人，知本之論也，足占子經濟之畧。〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔措詞典則，通達治體，眞有本之學也。佳士！佳士！〕
translation_en:
…them; place them under the supervision of the responsible officials [?], lead them through the Confucian school officials, and ground their practice in the prescribed ceremonies. Let scholars throughout the realm become physically at ease and practiced in these observances, honing their skills daily and training month by month, molded by rites and music and gathered into the examination system. Then scholars will possess both civil and military talents, the court will succeed in obtaining worthy men, and a spirit of modesty and deference will flourish in the villages. What aspect of government that discerns virtue through archery would then remain unfulfilled? Only then will moral principles be unified and customs made alike. A transforming influence of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony, in which all things find their proper order, will reach back to rival the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, flourishing uniquely in our own day. How fortunate I, in my ignorance, am to witness it myself!

Fourth Question
Li Bangqi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔In policy essays on equalizing landholdings, writers commonly lack a firm foundation. This essay alone is comprehensive and meticulous in its planning [?], and its exposition is clear and fluent. Surely its author understands the affairs of the age! It should be〕 recorded to serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔The arrangements proposed in this policy essay are clear and appropriate, and its conclusion rests on obtaining suitable men as prefects and magistrates. This is an argument that understands the fundamentals, and it sufficiently reveals your capacity for statecraft.〕

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: 〔Its wording is classical and well regulated, and it shows a thorough understanding of the essentials of government. This is truly learning with a firm foundation. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
阜天下之利者厚民之紀也通天下之變
者因時之治也夫天下之民非政以治之
則闓克胥匡以生王人導利于上下如其
狃于故常安于積習而不因時以達天下
之治其何以厚民之生而善其治于不窮
哉知此則可以論均田之法而復執事之
問矣粤自井田之制肇於黄虞歷千百年
至成周乃備養民之政莫善於此矣然猶
有貢助徹之不同者豈夏商周之聖人事
===
不師古而好爲是更張耶蓋亦因時以立
政通變以宜民而其什一之賦愛民之心
則一而已矣及周之衰稅畝之法行而井
田之意遂微阡陌之利開而井田之法盡
廢至漢以來咸踵其弊富者連阡陌之田
貧者無立錐之地古人良法蕩然無存迨
唐長慶間元稹有志於均天下之田上圖
策而未果於行後周世宗見其圖嘆曰此
致治之本也詔諸路議均定民租何行之
punctuated: 阜天下之利者，厚民之紀也；通天下之變者，因時之治也。夫天下之民，非政以治之，則闓克胥匡以生。王人導利于上下，如其狃于故常，安于積習，而不因時以達天下之治，其何以厚民之生，而善其治于不窮哉？知此，則可以論均田之法，而復執事之問矣。粤自井田之制肇於黄虞，歷千百年，至成周乃備，養民之政莫善於此矣。然猶有貢、助、徹之不同者，豈夏商周之聖人事不師古，而好爲是更張耶？蓋亦因時以立政，通變以宜民，而其什一之賦、愛民之心，則一而已矣。及周之衰，稅畝之法行，而井田之意遂微；阡陌之利開，而井田之法盡廢。至漢以來，咸踵其弊，富者連阡陌之田，貧者無立錐之地，古人良法蕩然無存。迨唐長慶間，元稹有志於均天下之田，上圖策而未果於行。後周世宗見其圖，嘆曰：「此致治之本也！」詔諸路議均定民租。何行之
translation_en:
To increase the benefits available throughout the realm is the foundation for enriching the people’s livelihood; to respond to changes throughout the realm is to govern according to the times. Unless the people of the realm are regulated through government, they will exploit and deceive one another to make a living [?]. Royal officials direct benefits among those above and below. If they cling to established practices and remain complacent in accumulated habits, without adapting to the times to bring good government to the realm, how can they enrich the people’s livelihood and perpetually maintain good government? Understanding this, we may discuss the method of equalizing landholdings and answer your question.

The well-field system originated under Huangdi and Shun. After hundreds and thousands of years, it reached completion under the Zhou. No policy for nourishing the people was better than this. Yet there were still differences among the gong, zhu, and che systems of taxation. Could it be that the sages of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou failed to model their actions on antiquity and simply delighted in making these alterations? They too established policies according to the times and adapted to change for the people’s benefit. Their levy of one tenth and their concern for the people, however, were the same.

When the Zhou declined, taxation by the mu was introduced, and the purpose of the well-field system gradually faded. Once opportunities for profit through private fields were opened, the well-field system was entirely abolished. From the Han onward, successive regimes perpetuated these abuses: the rich held fields extending across boundary after boundary, while the poor lacked even enough ground to stand an awl upon. The sound institutions of antiquity vanished without a trace. During the Changqing reign period of the Tang, Yuan Zhen aspired to equalize landholdings throughout the realm. He submitted a diagram and policy proposal, but they were never put into effect. Emperor Shizong of the Later Zhou saw his diagram and exclaimed, “This is the foundation of good government!” He ordered the various circuits to deliberate on equitably fixing the people’s land taxes. But when this was put into practice [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
求久世族蜂起而廢之司牧者亦不能為
之禁也要之積成以漸而于宜民之道有
歉焉耳亦何恠其政之不終也他如漢之
十五稅一三十稅一五十稅一雖有愛民
厚生之意要之皆非中正之法唐之租庸
調以取民雖為一代征賦之典要之亦非
近古之制嗣是而後益無足言矣洪惟我
太祖聖神啓運驅逐胡元寧一海宇復自古帝
王之土地定天下省會之疆域
===
創制立法分田成賦人有常業糧有定額卽
三代什一而賦之制而陋漢唐於不侔矣
列聖相承益隆德化春初有勸農之諭水旱有
蠲免之恵
仁澤汪濊浹於民心迨我
皇上視民如傷孳孳圖治每以及時耕耘勸諭
百姓海宇黎庶莫不忻戴
天地飽沐
仁化凡中外臣工亦皆仰體
punctuated:
求久，世族蜂起而廢之，司牧者亦不能為之禁也。要之，積成以漸，而于宜民之道有歉焉耳，亦何恠其政之不終也？他如漢之十五稅一、三十稅一、五十稅一，雖有愛民厚生之意，要之皆非中正之法。唐之租庸調以取民，雖為一代征賦之典，要之亦非近古之制。嗣是而後，益無足言矣。
洪惟我太祖聖神啓運，驅逐胡元，寧一海宇，復自古帝王之土地，定天下省會之疆域，創制立法，分田成賦，人有常業，糧有定額，卽三代什一而賦之制，而陋漢唐於不侔矣。列聖相承，益隆德化，春初有勸農之諭，水旱有蠲免之恵，仁澤汪濊，浹於民心。迨我皇上視民如傷，孳孳圖治，每以及時耕耘勸諭百姓，海宇黎庶莫不忻戴天地，飽沐仁化。凡中外臣工，亦皆仰體
translation_en:
…before long [?], powerful hereditary clans rose in a swarm and brought it to an end; those charged with governing the people could not restrain them either. In sum, these conditions had accumulated gradually, leaving shortcomings in the work of benefiting the people. Why, then, be surprised that the policy was not carried through? Other examples include the Han levies of one-fifteenth, one-thirtieth, and one-fiftieth. Although these expressed an intention to cherish the people and enrich their livelihoods, none was, in essence, a properly balanced method. The Tang system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and household levies in textiles, though the established fiscal code of that dynasty, was likewise no system approaching that of antiquity. What followed merits still less discussion.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, in his sagely and divine wisdom, inaugurated the dynasty’s destined rule, expelled the barbarian Yuan, pacified and unified the realm, recovered the lands held by emperors and kings since antiquity, and fixed the territorial boundaries of the provinces throughout the empire. He established institutions and laws, apportioned land and assessed taxes: everyone had a settled occupation, and grain-tax quotas were fixed. This was precisely the tithe system of the Three Dynasties; the Han and Tang arrangements appeared inferior, unable to match it. Successive sage sovereigns further strengthened transformation through virtue. At the beginning of spring they issued instructions encouraging agriculture, and in times of flood or drought they graciously remitted taxes. Their abundant benevolence penetrated the people’s hearts. Now our reigning Emperor cares for the people as though they were injured and works diligently for good government, repeatedly exhorting the common people to plow and weed at the proper times. Throughout the realm, all joyfully revere him as Heaven and Earth and partake fully of his benevolent transforming influence. All officials serving at court and in the provinces likewise reverently embody…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
洪慈不遑寧處固宜户口增繁田畝墾闢乃
今有未盡然者即以河南考之蓋古豫冀
之地也厥田中上厥賦上中墳壚白壤未
可謂不美矣洪武初當草創之際得地二
十九萬永樂初得地三十六萬至成化以
後乃復損而爲二十八萬户口版籍莫可
爲憑稅糧逋負殆又甚焉且以河南一省
若是他省亦可類推豈非臣下奉行日久
政弛民惰之故耶考之
===
國初分田之制有四曰魚鱗有圖曰刑嚴詭
寄曰律禁欺隱曰籍沒有稽夫魚鱗有圖
則疆界明矣刑嚴詭寄則法令行矣律嚴
欺隱則賦役均矣籍沒有稽則官民辨矣
而且賦有定期役有常額此師古而迹不
泥政善而民宜焉者也今則豪右之兼併
也而賦獨輕問之曰何不舉初年之法乎
則皆曰南陽弘農不可問姦猾之詭射也
而役不供問之曰何不舉初年之法乎則
punctuated: 洪慈，不遑寧處，固宜户口增繁，田畝墾闢。乃今有未盡然者，即以河南考之，蓋古豫冀之地也。厥田中上，厥賦上中，墳壚白壤，未可謂不美矣。洪武初，當草創之際，得地二十九萬；永樂初，得地三十六萬；至成化以後，乃復損而爲二十八萬。户口版籍莫可爲憑，稅糧逋負殆又甚焉。且以河南一省若是，他省亦可類推，豈非臣下奉行日久，政弛民惰之故耶？考之國初，分田之制有四：曰魚鱗有圖，曰刑嚴詭寄，曰律禁欺隱，曰籍沒有稽。夫魚鱗有圖，則疆界明矣；刑嚴詭寄，則法令行矣；律嚴欺隱，則賦役均矣；籍沒有稽，則官民辨矣。而且賦有定期，役有常額，此師古而迹不泥，政善而民宜焉者也。今則豪右之兼併也，而賦獨輕。問之曰：「何不舉初年之法乎？」則皆曰：「南陽弘農不可問。」姦猾之詭射也，而役不供。問之曰：「何不舉初年之法乎？」則
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s vast benevolence, allowing themselves no repose. Surely households and population should have multiplied, and fields should have been reclaimed and opened to cultivation. Yet this has not been fully realized. Consider Henan: it occupies the lands of ancient Yu and Ji. Its fields were ranked upper-middle, its tribute middle-upper; its rich earth, dark soil, and white loam could hardly be called poor. At the beginning of the Hongwu reign, when the dynasty was first being established, the land recorded amounted to 290,000; at the beginning of the Yongle reign, it amounted to 360,000; but from the Chenghua reign onward, it declined again to 280,000 [units unspecified]. The household and population registers cannot be relied upon, and arrears in tax grain are probably an even graver problem. If this is the situation in Henan alone, conditions in other provinces can be inferred by analogy. Is this not because, after officials have administered these policies for so long, government has grown lax and the people idle?
Examining the arrangements for allocating land at the dynasty’s founding, we find four provisions: fish-scale cadastral maps were maintained; fraudulent registration under another’s name was severely punished; statutes prohibited deception and concealment; and confiscations were subject to verification. With fish-scale maps, boundaries were clear; with severe punishment for fraudulent registration, laws and orders were enforced; with strict statutes against deception and concealment, taxes and labor services were equitably apportioned; with verification of confiscations, government and private holdings were distinguished. Moreover, taxes had fixed deadlines and labor services had regular quotas. These arrangements took antiquity as their model without adhering rigidly to its forms: the policies were sound and suited the people.
Now powerful families engross land, yet enjoy especially light taxation. Asked, “Why not enforce the laws of the dynasty’s early years?” they all reply, “Nanyang and Hongnong cannot be called to account.” Cunning rogues use fraudulent devices to evade their obligations and fail to provide labor service. Asked, “Why not enforce the laws of the dynasty’s early years?” then …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
又曰投鼠忌器城狐莫究夫兼併不抑則
無土之民必逃詭射不問則守法之民必
貧夫兼併何以能驅民於逃也得其地而
遺其糧賦奚以供而可獨存乎詭射何以
能致民於貧也差重而供之者寡役奚以
辦而能獨供乎故地去而糧存兼併者使
之也人逃而賦存詭射者為之也况兼併
必勢豪其財智足以迷吏書而賦獨減詭
射必貴顯其位望足以懾官守而役獨蠲
===
由是鬻產者逃而責陪於里甲里甲復逃
而均之槩縣包陪不勝而告者紛紛矣守
令無如之何而均田之說起矣蓋古之所
謂均田者因人而授之田而無不耕之夫
顧賦有定籍法不可以盡壞人有定業勢
有難以遽奪是未可行也今之均田云者
無亦欲因田以平其賦使無不稅之田乎
然行之未得其道弊且緣是以興其故何
也蓋
punctuated:
又曰：「投鼠忌器，城狐莫究。」夫兼併不抑，則無土之民必逃；詭射不問，則守法之民必貧。夫兼併何以能驅民於逃也？得其地而遺其糧，賦奚以供，而可獨存乎？詭射何以能致民於貧也？差重而供之者寡，役奚以辦，而能獨供乎？故地去而糧存，兼併者使之也；人逃而賦存，詭射者為之也。况兼併必勢豪，其財智足以迷吏書而賦獨減；詭射必貴顯，其位望足以懾官守而役獨蠲。

由是鬻產者逃，而責陪於里甲；里甲復逃，而均之槩縣。包陪不勝，而告者紛紛矣。守令無如之何，而均田之說起矣。蓋古之所謂均田者，因人而授之田，而無不耕之夫。顧賦有定籍，法不可以盡壞；人有定業，勢有難以遽奪，是未可行也。今之均田云者，無亦欲因田以平其賦，使無不稅之田乎？然行之未得其道，弊且緣是以興。其故何也？蓋……
translation_en:
…they again say: “To throw at the rat risks breaking the vessel; the fox sheltered in the city wall cannot be investigated.” If land engrossment is not checked, people left landless will inevitably flee; if fraudulent evasion is not investigated, law-abiding people will inevitably become impoverished. How does land engrossment drive people to flee? The engrossers acquire their land but leave them liable for its grain tax. How can they pay the tax, and how can they alone remain? How does fraudulent evasion impoverish people? Service obligations are heavy, but few remain to meet them. How can the labor services be performed, and how can those few bear them alone? Thus, when land is gone but grain-tax liability remains, the land engrossers have caused it; when people flee but tax liabilities remain, the fraudulent evaders have brought it about. Moreover, land engrossers are invariably powerful magnates: their wealth and cunning suffice to hoodwink the clerks, so that their own taxes alone are reduced. Fraudulent evaders are invariably men of rank and prominence: their position and prestige suffice to intimidate the officials, so that their own service obligations alone are remitted.

Consequently, those who have sold their property flee, and the village-and-tithing units are required to make up the shortfall. When members of those units also flee, the burden is apportioned across the entire county. Unable to bear these collective liabilities, people submit complaints in growing numbers. Prefects and magistrates can do nothing about it, and proposals for equalizing land arise. What was called equalizing land in antiquity meant allocating land according to the people, so that no man lacked land to cultivate. Yet taxes have fixed registers, and the established system cannot be wholly dismantled; people have established holdings, which circumstances make difficult to seize abruptly. This therefore cannot yet be put into practice. What is now called equalizing land presumably means adjusting tax burdens according to the land, so that no land goes untaxed. But unless the proper method of implementation is found, abuses will arise from this very measure. Why is that? Because…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
國初以監生供丈量之差履畝畫圖有差錯
則罪之以故法行而難犯今則民僞滋甚
法有難以盡行者且田有等則賦有上下
不論其等則欲盡取而均之則官民莫辨
肥瘠無等吾恐法雖行而弊之踵于昔者
愈滋矣何也蓋兼併詭射者威旣足以制
人賄又有以通神向也賦雖匿而名猶存
今則併其名而亡之矣向也役雖隱而籍
猶存今則併其籍而去之矣矧夫投獻過
===
寄流弊日深有長民之責者寧恝然而不
爲之所哉玆欲除其弊以復其舊使不去
其所以爲法之蠹者可乎夫田不可均固
也而兼併獨不可抑乎糧不可均固也而
詭射獨不可革乎然抑兼併之法有三曰
稽田地曰重差役曰先徵科產去稅存則
稽鬻產者誰也由是計畝而責之催收田
多糧少也由是則稽其脫漏而責之收籍
此稽田地之法也富者必重其差役必先
punctuated:
國初，以監生供丈量之差，履畝畫圖，有差錯則罪之，以故法行而難犯。今則民僞滋甚，法有難以盡行者。且田有等，則賦有上下；不論其等，則欲盡取而均之，則官民莫辨，肥瘠無等。吾恐法雖行，而弊之踵于昔者愈滋矣。何也？蓋兼併詭射者，威旣足以制人，賄又有以通神。向也，賦雖匿而名猶存；今則併其名而亡之矣。向也，役雖隱而籍猶存；今則併其籍而去之矣。矧夫投獻過寄，流弊日深，有長民之責者，寧恝然而不爲之所哉？玆欲除其弊以復其舊，使不去其所以爲法之蠹者，可乎？

夫田不可均，固也；而兼併獨不可抑乎？糧不可均，固也；而詭射獨不可革乎？然抑兼併之法有三：曰稽田地，曰重差役，曰先徵科。產去稅存，則稽鬻產者誰也，由是計畝而責之催收。田多糧少也，由是則稽其脫漏而責之收籍。此稽田地之法也。富者必重其差役，必先
translation_en:
…at the beginning of the dynasty, students of the Imperial University were assigned to land-surveying duties. They walked the fields and drew maps, and were punished for errors. Thus the law was enforced and was difficult to violate. Now fraud among the people has grown so prevalent that some provisions of the law are difficult to enforce fully. Moreover, land has different grades, and consequently tax assessments are higher or lower. If these grades are disregarded and all land is subjected to uniform assessment, no distinction will be made between government and private land, nor between fertile and barren soil. I fear that even if this measure is implemented, abuses continuing from the past will proliferate still further. Why? Those who engross land and fraudulently evade taxation possess enough power to dominate others, while their bribes can sway even the spirits. Formerly, although taxes were concealed, the names remained on record; now even those names will be erased. Formerly, although service obligations were concealed, the registers remained; now even those registrations will be removed. Furthermore, the abuses arising from placing land under powerful patrons’ protection and transferring its registration to others grow deeper by the day. Can those charged with governing the people remain indifferent and make no provision against them? If we now wish to eliminate these abuses and restore the former order, can we do so without removing what undermines the law?

That landholdings cannot be equalized is granted; but can land engrossment alone not be restrained? That grain-tax assessments cannot be equalized is granted; but can fraudulent evasion alone not be abolished? There are three methods of restraining land engrossment: investigating landed property, increasing service obligations, and collecting taxes first. Where property has been transferred but the tax liability remains, investigate who sold the property; then calculate its acreage and hold that person responsible for pressing for collection [?]. Where landholdings are extensive but grain-tax assessments small, investigate the omissions and evasions and require their entry in the registers. This is the method of investigating landed property. The wealthy must have their service obligations increased, and must be first…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
其科徵役重則不勝其差之繁彼或且無
樂其業之廣徵先則不勝其督之嚴而亦
將苦其糧之多此重差役先徵科之法也
稽詭射之術有二曰愼優免曰考寄莊夫
優免免其本業耳今則廣收富人之田以
射利欲愼之則近日之例可尋也寄莊者
寄其廣布者耳今則借豪貴之名以隱差
欲革之亦近日之禁可尋也至於投獻有
例强占有禁其法具存也其他荒蕪汙下
===
之地糧不可減也召民耕種之使之止供
輕糧而差不與焉獨曰不可乎河水衝決
之地糧不減也則以淤漲者補給之計畝
而不使羸焉獨曰不可乎是皆救振之急
務而通變宜民之至術也舉而行之則利
不必興也去其害利者則利自興矣法不
必改也去其蠹法者則法無不善矣夫然
則積弊已革賦役已均流亡漸復荒蕪漸
墾如是而其民有不富盛而其法有不行
punctuated:
其科徵。役重，則不勝其差之繁，彼或且無樂其業之廣；徵先，則不勝其督之嚴，而亦將苦其糧之多。此重差役、先徵科之法也。
稽詭射之術有二：曰愼優免，曰考寄莊。夫優免，免其本業耳，今則廣收富人之田以射利。欲愼之，則近日之例可尋也。寄莊者，寄其廣布者耳，今則借豪貴之名以隱差。欲革之，亦近日之禁可尋也。至於投獻有例，强占有禁，其法具存也。
其他荒蕪汙下之地，糧不可減也，召民耕種之，使之止供輕糧，而差不與焉，獨曰不可乎？河水衝決之地，糧不減也，則以淤漲者補給之，計畝而不使羸焉，獨曰不可乎？是皆救振之急務，而通變宜民之至術也。舉而行之，則利不必興也，去其害利者，則利自興矣；法不必改也，去其蠹法者，則法無不善矣。夫然，則積弊已革，賦役已均，流亡漸復，荒蕪漸墾。如是而其民有不富盛，而其法有不行
translation_en:
…their tax collection. When service obligations are heavy, they will find the numerous assignments unbearable and may cease to take pleasure in the extent of their estates. When taxes are collected from them first, they will find the strict enforcement unbearable and will likewise resent the size of their grain-tax liabilities. These are the methods of imposing heavier service obligations and giving priority to tax collection.
There are two ways to investigate fraudulent evasion: exercise care in granting privileged exemptions, and scrutinize outlying estates. Privileged exemptions exempt only the beneficiary’s own property. Now, however, beneficiaries take extensive holdings from wealthy landowners under their names to seek profit. To exercise care in this matter, one may consult recent precedents. Outlying estates merely accommodate widely dispersed holdings [?]; now, however, people borrow the names of the powerful and eminent to conceal their service liabilities. To eliminate this practice, one may likewise consult recent prohibitions. As for presenting land to powerful patrons and forcibly occupying land, there are precedents governing the former and prohibitions against the latter: the relevant laws are all in place.
As for other land that is waste or low-lying and waterlogged, if its grain-tax assessment cannot be reduced, could one not recruit people to cultivate it, require them to pay only a light grain tax, and exempt them from service obligations? For land devastated by rivers breaching their banks, if its grain-tax assessment is not reduced, could one not compensate the holders with land formed by alluvial deposits, calculating the acreage so that they suffer no shortfall [?]? These are all urgent measures for relief and the best means of adapting to circumstances for the people’s benefit. Put them into practice, and there will be no need to institute benefits deliberately: remove what impairs those benefits, and they will arise of themselves. There will be no need to change the laws: remove what undermines them, and all the laws will work well. Then accumulated abuses will have been eliminated, taxes and service obligations equalized, displaced people will gradually return, and waste land will gradually be reclaimed. Under such circumstances, that the people might fail to prosper and the laws fail to be implemented…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
者吾未之信也若曰必欲行均田之法則
將奪富人之所有給貧者之所無情牴勢
格必羣起而爭之況司府會計之煩郡邑
踏勘之擾又有不勝其弊者乎故朱子謂
均田爲東坡之戲論良有以也雖然善天
下之治存乎法行天下之法存乎人先正
亦曰有治人無治法夫守令之任最爲親
民不得其人而任之欲其更化善治亦難
矣果得忠實才識之士布列州縣守令之
===
官而又復久任以固其志精考課以稽其
政嚴舉刺以甄其類明黜陟以示其典則
感激奮勵之餘必有守己愛民之實使之
敦行節儉輕徭薄賦使民安其政而有常
從其好而不貳則田雖不均而阜成之政
舉矣何必專事于法古爲哉方今
聖明在上百辟承式宏謀淵筭固不假於芻蕘
之言者然葑菲之采或亦集思廣益之道
也惟進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 者，吾未之信也。若曰必欲行均田之法，則將奪富人之所有，給貧者之所無，情牴勢格，必羣起而爭之。況司府會計之煩，郡邑踏勘之擾，又有不勝其弊者乎？故朱子謂均田爲東坡之戲論，良有以也。雖然，善天下之治存乎法，行天下之法存乎人。先正亦曰：「有治人，無治法。」夫守令之任最爲親民，不得其人而任之，欲其更化善治亦難矣。果得忠實才識之士，布列州縣守令之官，而又復久任以固其志，精考課以稽其政，嚴舉刺以甄其類，明黜陟以示其典，則感激奮勵之餘，必有守己愛民之實。使之敦行節儉，輕徭薄賦，使民安其政而有常，從其好而不貳，則田雖不均，而阜成之政舉矣。何必專事于法古爲哉？方今聖明在上，百辟承式，宏謀淵筭，固不假於芻蕘之言者。然葑菲之采，或亦集思廣益之道也。惟進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…that this could be so, I cannot believe. If one insists that a system of equalizing landholdings must be implemented, this would mean taking what the rich possess and giving it to the poor who lack it. People’s feelings would resist and circumstances would obstruct it; they would surely rise together to contest it. Moreover, would not the burdensome accounting in the provincial administrations and prefectures, and the disruptive field inspections in prefectures and counties, produce further intolerable abuses? Master Zhu therefore had good reason to call land equalization a playful argument of Dongpo’s.

Nevertheless, good government throughout the realm depends upon laws, while implementing the realm’s laws depends upon people. A worthy predecessor likewise said: “There are men who bring about order, but no laws that bring about order.” Prefects and magistrates hold offices that bring them closest to the people. If suitable men are not appointed, it will be difficult to expect a transformation toward good government. If loyal, honest men of ability and discernment are indeed found and appointed throughout the prefectures and counties as prefects and magistrates, and if they are then retained long enough to steady their resolve, their performance carefully assessed to scrutinize their administration, recommendations and denunciations rigorously conducted to distinguish their respective qualities, and demotions and promotions clearly administered to manifest the governing standards, they will be moved to gratitude and strenuous effort, and will assuredly display genuine integrity in their own conduct and care for the people. Have them earnestly practice frugality, lighten labor service, and reduce taxes, so that the people may live securely under their administration and enjoy constancy, following what they favor without wavering. Then, even though landholdings are not equalized, measures to enrich and secure the people will be put into effect. Why must one devote oneself exclusively to imitating antiquity?

At present, our sagacious sovereign reigns above, and all officials follow his example. His grand plans and profound calculations certainly have no need of a woodcutter’s humble words. Yet gathering even humble turnips and radishes—that is, accepting modest counsel—may also be a way to draw upon many minds for broader benefit. I would be most fortunate if you would receive these words and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
第五問
徐養相
同考試官教諭劉　批〔考據精詳處分明當通篇以時勢立意而一言一意皆數巳見爲文予其〕
抱先憂之志而不徙事于章句者乎傑士傑士
考試官教諭林　批〔治河之議紛紛靡定予援古證今據事論勢卓有定見其通達治體者與〕
考試官教諭敖　批〔治河一策條析明盡可行取冠多士〕
===
議治河者相古今之時則不泥常理以倖
一時之功權輕重之勢則不執巳見以妨
天下之計何者天下時與勢而巳矣計天
下之事相時與權勢而巳矣究而言之則
時者勢之趨也勢者時之會也故時有古
今固不得執時以論勢勢有輕重亦不得
拂勢以徇時變而通之則天下之勢會同
于一心而至順在我矣其于河之治也夫
何難哉然則有經
punctuated:
第五問

徐養相

同考試官教諭劉批〔考據精詳，處分明當。通篇以時勢立意，而一言一意皆數巳見，爲文予其〕抱先憂之志而不徙事于章句者乎？傑士！傑士！

考試官教諭林批〔治河之議紛紛靡定，予援古證今，據事論勢，卓有定見，其通達治體者與？〕

考試官教諭敖批〔治河一策，條析明盡，可行，取冠多士。〕

議治河者，相古今之時，則不泥常理以倖一時之功；權輕重之勢，則不執巳見以妨天下之計。何者？天下時與勢而巳矣。計天下之事，相時與權勢而巳矣。究而言之，則時者勢之趨也，勢者時之會也。故時有古今，固不得執時以論勢；勢有輕重，亦不得拂勢以徇時。變而通之，則天下之勢會同于一心，而至順在我矣。其于河之治也，夫何難哉？然則有經
translation_en:
Fifth Policy Question

Xu Yangxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔“The evidential research is meticulous and thorough; the proposed measures are clear and appropriate. The entire essay takes present circumstances and prevailing conditions as its guiding idea, and every word and thought sets forth his own views [?]. In composing this essay, does he〕 cherish the aspiration to worry before others do, rather than merely occupy himself with textual explication [?]? An outstanding scholar! An outstanding scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔“Proposals for managing the Yellow River proliferate without reaching a settled conclusion. You [?] invoke antiquity to illuminate the present and assess prevailing conditions on the basis of facts, displaying exceptionally firm judgment. Surely you understand the essentials of governance!”〕

Comment by Examiner Ao, Instructor: 〔“This policy essay on managing the Yellow River analyzes its subject clearly and exhaustively, and its proposals are practicable. Selected to rank first among the candidates.”〕

Those who deliberate on managing the Yellow River should examine the circumstances of antiquity and the present; then they will not cling to fixed principles in the hope of securing a fleeting success. They should weigh the relative importance of prevailing conditions; then they will not insist on their own views to the detriment of plans for the realm. Why is this so? The affairs of the realm come down to circumstances and prevailing conditions alone. Planning for those affairs consists simply in examining circumstances and weighing conditions. To investigate this more deeply: circumstances are the direction in which conditions tend, while conditions are the convergence of circumstances. Thus, although circumstances differ between antiquity and the present, one must not hold rigidly to those of a particular period when assessing conditions. And although conditions differ in relative importance, one must not disregard them in order to conform to the circumstances of a particular time. If one adapts to change and makes the necessary adjustments, the conditions of the realm will converge within a single mind, and the capacity to act in perfect accordance with them will lie within oneself. What difficulty, then, could there be in managing the Yellow River? Thus, those concerned with ordering …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
國之慮者可以深長思矣執事以河務下詢
承學然識在俊傑顧章句之儒何足以知
之雖然亦嘗聞之矣請以時勢復明問可
乎按河之源出崑崙之隅凡九折而入中
國禹鑿龍門納而東焉自大伾而下則析
爲三渠大陸而下則播爲九河同爲逆河
入于海故歷三代無河患禹之功也及周
定王時河始南徙訖于漢而禹之故道失
矣是非禹蹟之替也亦時勢之變爲之也
===
厥後倡議疏治代不乏人如許商索故道
之跡延年壯胡中之謀張仲義弛灌溉之
防王横度就下之勢皆徒托空言罔裨實
效夫何暇論也耶就中舉其已試者賈讓
當哀平之世河徙汲郡乃應詔陳三策其
畧有曰内徙民居以爲曠地北放大河以
入渤海不與水爭咫尺之地上策也多穿
漕渠分殺水勢中策也至于繕完故隄增
卑倍薄則謂之下策是三策者皆可行然
punctuated:
國之慮者，可以深長思矣。執事以河務下詢承學，然識在俊傑，顧章句之儒何足以知之？雖然，亦嘗聞之矣。請以時勢復明問，可乎？按河之源出崑崙之隅，凡九折而入中國。禹鑿龍門，納而東焉。自大伾而下，則析爲三渠；大陸而下，則播爲九河，同爲逆河，入于海。故歷三代無河患，禹之功也。及周定王時，河始南徙，訖于漢而禹之故道失矣。是非禹蹟之替也，亦時勢之變爲之也。

厥後倡議疏治，代不乏人。如許商索故道之跡，延年壯胡中之謀，張仲義弛灌溉之防，王横度就下之勢，皆徒托空言，罔裨實效，夫何暇論也耶？就中舉其已試者，賈讓當哀平之世，河徙汲郡，乃應詔陳三策。其畧有曰：「内徙民居，以爲曠地，北放大河，以入渤海，不與水爭咫尺之地，上策也。多穿漕渠，分殺水勢，中策也。至于繕完故隄，增卑倍薄，則謂之下策。」是三策者皆可行，然
translation_en:
…those concerned with governing the state may reflect deeply and at length. You, sir, have graciously questioned a student such as myself about river management. Yet understanding belongs to men of outstanding ability: how could a scholar devoted to textual explication know enough about it? Nevertheless, I have heard something of the matter. May I answer your enlightened question in terms of circumstances and prevailing conditions? The Yellow River rises in a corner of the Kunlun Mountains and, after nine bends, enters the central lands. Yu cut through Longmen, channeling it eastward. Below Dapi it divided into three channels; below Dalu it spread into nine rivers, which joined as the Ni River and entered the sea. Thus throughout the Three Dynasties there were no river calamities: this was Yu's achievement. In the time of King Ding of Zhou, the river first shifted southward, and by the Han dynasty Yu's former course had been lost. This was not a failure of Yu's works; changing circumstances and conditions brought it about.

Thereafter, every age had men who proposed dredging and regulating the river. Xu Shang sought traces of its former course; Yannian advanced a bold plan concerning Hu Zhong [?]; Zhang Zhongyi proposed relaxing the embankments used for irrigation [?]; and Wang Heng assessed the tendency of water to flow toward lower ground. All merely relied on empty words, contributing nothing of practical effect. Why spend time discussing them? To select from among them a proposal that had already been tried: during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, when the river shifted into Ji Commandery, Jia Rang responded to an imperial edict by presenting three policies. In outline, he said: “Move the inhabitants inland to create open ground, and release the great river northward to enter the Bohai Sea, without contesting even a foot or an inch of ground with the water: this is the best policy. Excavate numerous transport canals to divide and diminish the force of the water: this is the middle policy. As for repairing the old embankments, raising the low sections and doubling the thin ones, this is called the lowest policy.” All three policies could be implemented, yet…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
決黎陽遮害亭以全冀州爲金隄水門以
漲洪口蓋就夫漢之時勢論云爾而今果
可以盡行乎賈魯當勝國爲總治河防使
言治河之法有三曰疏曰濬曰塞故釃河
之流因而導之之謂疏去河之淤因而深
之之謂濬至于塞者抑河之暴因而扼之
之謂也是三法若皆可行然防龍口之潰
而勞憊無時收北岸之功而靡費無紀徒
以倡亂焉耳其于時勢何如也故丘文莊
===
有曰後世言治河者莫備于賈讓之三策
又曰所以治之之法莫出于賈魯之三法
焉得非取其言之善與然歷代所用皆不
出其下策者亦以河之徙決無常有不能
執故道以施疏濬之力而因潰致防于拯
溺之功易效也耶洪惟我
國家漕會通之河輸東南之賦邇者二洪梗
澁取濟黃流適天啓之會也但丹沁同歸
流必旁溢河淮並入勢爲兩大而横潰之
punctuated:
決黎陽、遮害亭以全冀州，爲金隄水門以漲洪口，蓋就夫漢之時勢論云爾，而今果可以盡行乎？賈魯當勝國爲總治河防使，言治河之法有三，曰疏，曰濬，曰塞。故釃河之流，因而導之，之謂疏；去河之淤，因而深之，之謂濬；至于塞者，抑河之暴，因而扼之，之謂也。是三法若皆可行，然防龍口之潰而勞憊無時，收北岸之功而靡費無紀，徒以倡亂焉耳，其于時勢何如也？故丘文莊有曰：「後世言治河者，莫備于賈讓之三策。」又曰：「所以治之之法，莫出于賈魯之三法焉。」得非取其言之善與？然歷代所用皆不出其下策者，亦以河之徙決無常，有不能執故道以施疏濬之力，而因潰致防，于拯溺之功易效也耶？
洪惟我國家，漕會通之河，輸東南之賦。邇者二洪梗澁，取濟黃流，適天啓之會也。但丹沁同歸，流必旁溢；河淮並入，勢爲兩大，而横潰之
translation_en:
…breaching the river at Liyang and blocking it at Haiting to preserve Jizhou, and constructing sluice gates at the Jin Embankment to raise the water at Hongkou [?]—these proposals were made in light of the circumstances of the Han period. Can they really all be implemented today? Under the former dynasty, Jia Lu served as Director-general of River Defense. He stated that there were three methods of controlling the river: opening channels, dredging, and blocking breaches. Dividing the river’s flow and thereby guiding it is called opening channels; removing its silt and thereby deepening it is called dredging; restraining its violence and thereby checking it is called blocking breaches. These three methods might all seem practicable. Yet guarding against a breach at Longkou brought unending toil and exhaustion, while achieving results on the northern bank entailed expenditure beyond reckoning. This merely fomented rebellion. How well did it suit the circumstances of the time? Thus Qiu Wenzhuang said: “Among later discussions of river control, none is more comprehensive than Jia Rang’s three proposals.” He also said: “The methods for controlling it do not go beyond Jia Lu’s three methods.” Was he not appreciating the merits of their arguments? Yet the measures employed by successive dynasties have never gone beyond the least desirable proposal. Might this also be because the river shifts course and breaches its banks unpredictably, making it impossible always to adhere to its old course and devote effort to opening channels and dredging, whereas building defenses in response to breaches more readily produces results in rescuing people from drowning?
We reverently consider that our state uses the Huitong River for grain transport, conveying the tax revenues of the southeast. Recently, the two rapids became obstructed and difficult to navigate; drawing upon the Yellow River’s flow to assist transport was an opportunity opened by Heaven. But when the Dan and Qin rivers converge, their waters will inevitably overflow to the sides; when the Yellow River and the Huai both enter, they constitute two mighty forces, and the…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
禍將所不免者若往歲河決曹單民用蕩
析其理河諸臣議開趙皮寨孫家渡以殺
河勢體
國恤民意亦周至然詢之民情察之地宜二
河之開似有未易言者以趙皮寨言之在
蘭陽之北僅數里由畢莊接舊河至懷遠
荆山口入淮昔以曹沛之溢議開此河其
故道可考也今沈莊至丁家集開淤計三
百餘里其事勢誠爲艱大蓋夫役之勞必
動數十萬衆工費之煩必捐數十萬金矧
===
夫復渦河之流則
壽春之陵可虞分南注之勢則徐呂之洪罔
濟而蘭儀寧柘又將不爲水鄉耶是趙皮
寨之不可開也明矣以孫家渡言之在滎
澤之東數十里接白露河入淮昔以張秋
之決議開此河其故道可考也今姚家村
一帶開淤止四十里其功力若可爲者然
河當汴藩之北今析之而南則兩流夾衝
punctuated: 禍將所不免者。若往歲河決曹單，民用蕩析，其理河諸臣議開趙皮寨、孫家渡以殺河勢，體國恤民，意亦周至。然詢之民情，察之地宜，二河之開似有未易言者。以趙皮寨言之，在蘭陽之北僅數里，由畢莊接舊河，至懷遠荆山口入淮。昔以曹沛之溢議開此河，其故道可考也。今沈莊至丁家集開淤，計三百餘里，其事勢誠爲艱大。蓋夫役之勞，必動數十萬衆；工費之煩，必捐數十萬金。矧夫復渦河之流，則壽春之陵可虞；分南注之勢，則徐呂之洪罔濟，而蘭儀寧柘又將不爲水鄉耶？是趙皮寨之不可開也明矣。以孫家渡言之，在滎澤之東數十里，接白露河入淮。昔以張秋之決議開此河，其故道可考也。今姚家村一帶開淤止四十里，其功力若可爲者。然河當汴藩之北，今析之而南，則兩流夾衝
translation_en:
…the calamity of flooding from breaches will be unavoidable. In past years, for example, the Yellow River breached its banks at Caozhou and Shanxian, leaving the people displaced and scattered. The ministers responsible for river management proposed opening channels at Zhaopizhai and Sunjiadu to reduce the river’s force. Their intention to serve the state and care for the people was indeed thorough and considerate. Yet, upon consulting local opinion and examining the terrain, opening these two channels appears less straightforward than one might suppose.

Zhaopizhai lies only a few li north of Lanyang. From Bizhuang, the proposed channel joins the old river course and enters the Huai at Jingshankou in Huaiyuan. In the past, flooding in Caozhou and Peixian prompted proposals to open this channel, and its former course can be traced. Now, clearing the silt from Shenzhuang to Dingjiaji would extend over more than three hundred li: the undertaking would indeed be difficult and immense. The labor required would necessarily mobilize hundreds of thousands of people, and the expense would require hundreds of thousands in funds. Moreover, restoring the flow of the Guo River would endanger the imperial mausoleum at Shouchun; diverting the current southward would leave the rapids at Xuzhou and Lüliang without sufficient water. Would Lanyang, Yifeng, Ningling, and Zhecheng not also become a watery expanse? It is thus clear that the channel at Zhaopizhai must not be opened.

Sunjiadu lies several tens of li east of Xingze; its channel joins the Bailu River and enters the Huai. In the past, a breach at Zhangqiu prompted proposals to open this channel, and its former course can be traced. Now, clearing the silt around Yaojiacun would cover only forty li, so the work appears feasible. Yet the river lies north of the princely seat at Bian. If it is now divided and directed southward, the two currents will assail it from either side…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
勢恐危殆其滎項通扶諸邑經流渙漫禍
必騰播矧夫
皇陵值淮泗之衝運漕梗徐沛之道是所關繫
蓋不止一郡一邑之利害則孫家渡之不
可開也亦明矣用是觀之趙皮寨之開非
苦其難也時勢妨之也孫家渡之開非
其易也而時勢亦有同于趙皮寨者故近
功有不爲也夫二河既不可開而或者之
議是徒有見于曹單之可憂而無見于潁
河之民之可憂有見于疏治之爲功而無
===
見于
皇陵運道之大有可慮者矣是其輕重大小之
勢又何庸于煩較也耶乃若執事欲求爲
畫一之策使節省而不妨開濬之議輕減
而不失保障之宜然事關大計非愚生之
所敢與也嘗考之宋儒朱熹氏有曰禹之
治水只是從低處下手下面之水盡殺則
上面之水漸淺呂祖謙又曰禹不惜數百
punctuated: 勢恐危殆。其滎、項、通、扶諸邑，經流渙漫，禍必騰播。矧夫皇陵值淮泗之衝，運漕梗徐沛之道，是所關繫，蓋不止一郡一邑之利害，則孫家渡之不可開也亦明矣。用是觀之，趙皮寨之開，非苦其難也，時勢妨之也；孫家渡之開，非其易也，而時勢亦有同于趙皮寨者，故近功有不爲也。夫二河既不可開，而或者之議，是徒有見于曹單之可憂，而無見于潁河之民之可憂；有見于疏治之爲功，而無見于皇陵運道之大有可慮者矣。是其輕重大小之勢，又何庸于煩較也耶？乃若執事欲求爲畫一之策，使節省而不妨開濬之議，輕減而不失保障之宜，然事關大計，非愚生之所敢與也。嘗考之，宋儒朱熹氏有曰：「禹之治水，只是從低處下手，下面之水盡殺，則上面之水漸淺。」呂祖謙又曰：「禹不惜數百
translation_en:
…the situation would, I fear, become perilous. In the counties of Rong, Xiang, Tong, and Fu, the waters passing through would spread unchecked, and disaster would surely extend far and wide. Moreover, the imperial mausoleums lie where the Huai and Si rivers converge, and grain transport would be obstructed along the route through Xu and Pei. What is at stake thus extends beyond the interests of a single prefecture or county. It is therefore also clear that the channel at Sunjiadu must not be opened.

Viewed in this light, the objection to opening Zhaopizhai is not the difficulty of the undertaking: present circumstances prevent it. As for opening Sunjiadu, it is not its ease [?]; present circumstances pose obstacles similar to those at Zhaopizhai. Thus there are immediate gains that one must forgo. Since neither channel can be opened, the proposals of some men merely recognize the grounds for concern at Cao and Shan, without recognizing the grounds for concern for the people along the Ying River. They recognize the achievement represented by dredging, without recognizing the grave dangers to the imperial mausoleums and the grain-transport route. What need, then, is there for a laborious comparison of the relative weight and magnitude of these considerations?

As for your wish to obtain a unified policy that would economize without impeding proposals for opening and dredging channels, and lighten burdens without sacrificing proper protection, this concerns a major undertaking in which I, an unworthy student, dare not presume to intervene. I have, however, consulted the words of the Song scholar Zhu Xi, who said: “In controlling the waters, Yu simply began at the lowest places. Once the water below had fully subsided, the water above gradually became shallower.” Lü Zuqian also said: “Yu did not begrudge several hundred…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
里地疏爲九河以分其勢善治水者不與
水爭地也斯二說者其知治水之要乎蓋
天下之事就其所利者易爲力而圖其所
不敢必者難爲功夫曹單之決適然之變
也未幾而旋復故道固河之利也今惟用
古之法而不失今之宜師禹之意而不泥
禹之迹濬其下流以順其利達之勢寬其
東隘以緩其湍急之性使其上無所激而
接河濟洪之道如舊也下有所納而由清
===
河達淮會淮入海之道如舊也故曰勢者
時之會也萬一河流衝齧洪水肆溢則相
其便宜以爲分殺之計然困敝之民不堪
重役淤徙之性難責成功此又不可不爲
之慮也故必節役以恤其力計費以惜其
財時挑濬以保垂成之功治遥隄以備不
虞之患失業之民可憫也則清退灘之田
以償之積侵之弊可革也則平稍芻之價
以抑之丁夫派及于通省非計也則申飭
punctuated: 里地，疏爲九河，以分其勢。善治水者，不與水爭地也。」斯二說者，其知治水之要乎！蓋天下之事，就其所利者易爲力，而圖其所不敢必者難爲功。夫曹單之決，適然之變也；未幾而旋復故道，固河之利也。今惟用古之法而不失今之宜，師禹之意而不泥禹之迹，濬其下流以順其利達之勢，寬其東隘以緩其湍急之性，使其上無所激，而接河濟洪之道如舊也；下有所納，而由清河達淮、會淮入海之道如舊也。故曰：「勢者，時之會也。」萬一河流衝齧，洪水肆溢，則相其便宜，以爲分殺之計。然困敝之民不堪重役，淤徙之性難責成功，此又不可不爲之慮也。故必節役以恤其力，計費以惜其財，時挑濬以保垂成之功，治遥隄以備不虞之患。失業之民可憫也，則清退灘之田以償之；積侵之弊可革也，則平稍芻之價以抑之；丁夫派及于通省，非計也，則申飭
translation_en:
…li of land, opening nine channels to divide the force of the water. Those skilled in managing water do not contend with it for land.” Surely these two statements grasp the essentials of water management! In the affairs of the world, it is easy to make headway by following favorable conditions, but difficult to achieve results by pursuing what cannot confidently be assured. The breach at Cao and Shan was an unforeseen event; the river’s return to its former course shortly afterward was certainly a favorable development.
