Now we need only employ ancient methods without losing sight of what suits present circumstances, and emulate Yu’s intentions without adhering rigidly to his actions. Dredge the lower reaches to facilitate the water’s free passage, and widen the constriction to the east to moderate its turbulent flow. Thus upstream the water will encounter nothing that provokes its violence, and the route connecting with the river and supplying the rapids [?] will remain as before; downstream there will be room to receive the water, and its route through the Qing River to the Huai, joining the Huai and entering the sea, will remain as before. Hence the saying: “The configuration of circumstances is the convergence of the moment.” Should the river batter and erode its banks and floodwaters overflow unchecked, assess the local conditions and devise measures to divide and diminish the flow.

Yet the exhausted people cannot endure heavy labor service, and success is difficult to ensure when the river is prone to silting and changing course. These considerations, too, must inform our planning. We must therefore limit labor service to spare the people’s strength, calculate expenditures to conserve their resources, dredge periodically to preserve work nearing completion, and maintain the setback embankments against unforeseen calamities. Those who have lost their livelihoods deserve compassion: investigate and restore lands on the river flats to compensate them. Longstanding abuses of encroachment and exaction can be reformed: regulate the prices of brushwood and straw [?] to restrain them. Extending labor levies throughout the entire province is no sound policy: therefore reiterate the injunctions…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
舊例以爲可守之規貯積近輸于户曹非
例也則力懲往事勿蹈取盈之戒凡其有
裨于河防關于民瘼者罔不周慮而詳慮
之如此則不惟遠
陵寢之害濟漕洪之利而瀕河之民俱免困敝
其曹單之憂亦可以少紓矣此之謂行所
無事之智而乘時達治之良猷也故曰時
者勢之趨也至于以爲水性就下必欲倡
南濬之謀然今河行之勢獨非下乎又以
===
爲水惟安其故道假使水性無常全河南
徙則今日之道又將不爲他日之故道乎
是皆未之思耳若夫棄魚臺之地而引沁
以濟洪濬武陽之道而由北以入海此又
計一時之利害而不可與語今之時勢者
也故曰變而通之則天下之至順在我矣
愚生管見如此惟執事因其言而裁試之
幸甚
punctuated: 舊例，以爲可守之規。貯積近輸于户曹，非例也，則力懲往事，勿蹈取盈之戒。凡其有裨于河防、關于民瘼者，罔不周慮而詳慮之。如此，則不惟遠陵寢之害，濟漕洪之利，而瀕河之民俱免困敝，其曹單之憂亦可以少紓矣。此之謂行所無事之智，而乘時達治之良猷也。故曰：「時者，勢之趨也。」至于以爲水性就下，必欲倡南濬之謀，然今河行之勢，獨非下乎？又以爲水惟安其故道，假使水性無常，全河南徙，則今日之道，又將不爲他日之故道乎？是皆未之思耳。若夫棄魚臺之地而引沁以濟洪，濬武陽之道而由北以入海，此又計一時之利害，而不可與語今之時勢者也。故曰：「變而通之，則天下之至順在我矣。」愚生管見如此，惟執事因其言而裁試之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…the established precedents, making them rules to be observed. The recent remittance of accumulated reserves to the Ministry of Revenue [?] accords with no established precedent; one must therefore take past events firmly to heart and avoid repeating the mistake of exacting the full quota. Everything that benefits river defenses or bears upon the people’s suffering must receive comprehensive and detailed consideration. In this way, not only would harm to the imperial mausoleums be averted and the benefits of the rapids used for grain transport secured, but all the people along the river would escape exhaustion and impoverishment. The anxieties concerning Cao and Shan could also be somewhat relieved. This is what is meant by the wisdom of proceeding without needless interference, and a sound strategy for achieving good government by acting as circumstances permit. Thus it is said: “Timeliness lies in the direction circumstances are taking.”

As for those who maintain that water naturally flows downward and therefore insist on advocating dredging to the south: does the river’s present course alone not run downward? Others maintain that water settles only in its former channel. But suppose that water’s disposition is inconstant and the entire river shifts southward: would today’s channel not become a former channel in the future? These views simply have not been thought through. As for abandoning the land at Yutai and diverting the Qin River to supply the rapids, or dredging the channel at Wuyang and taking a northern route to the sea, these proposals likewise calculate the advantages and disadvantages of a particular moment; those who advance them cannot be engaged in a discussion of present circumstances. Thus it is said: “By adapting to change and opening a way through, the utmost accord with all under Heaven will lie within my grasp.” Such are this humble student’s limited views. I would be most fortunate if you, honored officials, would weigh these words and put them to the test as you judge appropriate.

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖己酉秋河南省校士自
御史曁諸執事業有成勞矣
行且進多士歌鹿鳴而賓興
之也〔烋〕不佞猥佐校文之役
乃申言曰爾多士進矣
主上歛才圖治之意其在茲乎臣
===
子以人事
君之忠其有藉於是乎然才賢之
生也不偶其出而名世也亦
不易是故匪地弗毓靈異之
所鍾也匪天弗啓氣機之所
導也匪時弗顯道化之所隆
也中州之域太行磅礴黃河
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖己酉秋，河南省校士，自御史曁諸執事，業有成勞矣。行且進多士，歌《鹿鳴》而賓興之也。〔烋〕不佞，猥佐校文之役，乃申言曰：「爾多士進矣！主上歛才圖治之意，其在茲乎？臣子以人事君之忠，其有藉於是乎？然才賢之生也不偶，其出而名世也亦不易。是故匪地弗毓，靈異之所鍾也；匪天弗啓，氣機之所導也；匪時弗顯，道化之所隆也。中州之域，太行磅礴，黃河
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination
In the autumn of the jiyou year of Jiajing (1549), Henan Province examined its scholars. From the Censor to all the officials engaged in the examination, their labors had already borne fruit. Soon they would advance the assembled scholars, sing “The Deer Call,” and honor them as guests as they recommended them for advancement. I, 〔Xiu〕, unworthy though I am, had the undeserved privilege of assisting in the evaluation of their writings. I therefore offered these further words:
“You scholars have now advanced! Is this not where our sovereign’s intention to gather talent and seek good government finds expression? Is this not what enables us, his servants, to fulfill our loyal duty of serving our lord by providing him with worthy men? Yet the birth of talented and worthy men is no accident, nor is it easy for them to emerge and win renown in their age. Thus, without the earth they cannot be nurtured: they are where its numinous and extraordinary powers converge. Without Heaven they cannot be awakened: they are guided by the dynamic workings of vital energy. Without the proper age they cannot become manifest: they arise where the Way and its transforming influence flourish. In the region of the Central Plain, the Taihang Mountains spread in imposing grandeur, and the Yellow River …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
盪潏而又風雨之所交焉陰
陽之所合焉其山川幽淑之
鬱積不在于物則在于人謂
不稟于地之靈乎故曰維嶽
降神生甫及申有由爾也夫
天人相爲流通景光由于感
召時值洪濛則人物爲之榛
===
狉運當熙洽則太和爲之流
行然虎嘯而風冽龍興而雲
升又氣類相從也故曰天降
時雨山川出雲耆欲將至有
開必先謂不啓之以天運乎
皇祖宅夏當天一時佐命之士風
猋景附乘時樹勛中州儁乂
punctuated:
盪潏，而又風雨之所交焉，陰陽之所合焉。其山川幽淑之鬱積，不在于物，則在于人，謂不稟于地之靈乎？故曰：「維嶽降神，生甫及申。」有由爾也。夫天人相爲流通，景光由于感召。時值洪濛，則人物爲之榛狉；運當熙洽，則太和爲之流行。然虎嘯而風冽，龍興而雲升，又氣類相從也。故曰：「天降時雨，山川出雲。耆欲將至，有開必先。」謂不啓之以天運乎？
皇祖宅夏，當天一時，佐命之士風猋景附，乘時樹勛，中州儁乂
translation_en:
…surges and churns; here, too, winds and rains converge, and yin and yang unite. The accumulated, hidden excellence of its mountains and rivers manifests itself, if not in things, then in people. Can one say that they do not receive their endowment from the spiritual potency of the land? Thus it is said: “The sacred peaks sent down their spirits, giving birth to Fu and Shen.” There is a reason for this. Heaven and humanity communicate with one another, and splendid radiance arises through mutual influence and response. When the age is one of primordial obscurity, people and things remain wild and uncultivated; when the course of time brings flourishing concord, supreme harmony flows throughout. Yet when the tiger roars, the wind blows fiercely; when the dragon rises, clouds ascend. This, too, is the mutual attraction of kindred vital forces. Thus it is said: “Heaven sends down timely rain; mountains and rivers send forth clouds. When what is desired is about to arrive, an opening must first appear.” Can one say that Heaven’s workings do not open the way?
When our imperial ancestor established himself in the Chinese realm, at a uniquely Heaven-appointed moment [?], men who assisted in fulfilling the dynastic mandate rushed to him like the wind and followed him like shadows, seizing the occasion to establish their achievements. The outstanding men of the Central Region…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
輩出竝爲
明輔治
聖天子應運中興統一聖眞振厲
儒術
文命誕敷卽遐陬罔不融浹乃
中州密邇
畿輔諸士衣被
===
聖化最深且久日漸月劘無不丕
應徯志以承
休德是以文質彬彬稱君子焉
易曰聖人久于其道而天下
化成是之謂矣雖然孕靈者
地也必當有以煥其靈啓運
者天也必當有以昌其運應
punctuated:
輩出，竝爲明輔治。聖天子應運中興，統一聖眞，振厲儒術，文命誕敷，卽遐陬罔不融浹。乃中州密邇畿輔，諸士衣被聖化最深且久，日漸月劘，無不丕應徯志，以承休德，是以文質彬彬，稱君子焉。《易》曰：「聖人久于其道，而天下化成。」是之謂矣。
雖然，孕靈者地也，必當有以煥其靈；啓運者天也，必當有以昌其運；應
translation_en:
…emerged in succession, all serving as illustrious aids to governance [?]. The sagely Son of Heaven, responding to the course of destiny, has brought about a restoration, unified sagely truth [?], and invigorated Confucian learning. His civilizing commands have spread far and wide; even the remotest corners have been thoroughly imbued with them. Now Zhongzhou lies close to the capital region, and its scholars have received the sagely transforming influence most deeply and for the longest time. Steeped in it day by day and polished month by month, all have responded wholeheartedly, looking expectantly toward his intentions so as to receive his glorious virtue. Thus, balanced in refinement and substance, they merit the name of gentlemen. The Book of Changes says: “The sage abides long in his Way, and the transformation of all under Heaven is accomplished.” This is precisely what it means.
Nevertheless, it is the earth that nurtures spiritual potency, and there must be means to make that potency shine forth; it is Heaven that inaugurates the course of destiny, and there must be means to bring that course to flourishing fulfillment; those who respond …

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
時者人也必當有以濟于時
爾多士以言進矣行將擢秀
南宮而觀光
上國矣盍亦思所以言行相顧之
義乎是故古之人有曰伊傅
曰周召固中州之産聖人之
儔而前脩之可法焉者伊尹
===
以天下爲已任矣傅說相高
宗致中興矣周公之篤棐王
室召公之保釐西土其功業
光映簡冊歷萬年如一日非
爾多士所當致力者耶繼自
今列于有位服在大僚其必
矢乃志毋流于卑一乃心毋
punctuated:
時者，人也，必當有以濟于時。爾多士以言進矣，行將擢秀南宮，而觀光上國矣。盍亦思所以言行相顧之義乎？是故古之人，有曰伊、傅，曰周、召，固中州之産、聖人之儔，而前脩之可法焉者。伊尹以天下爲已任矣，傅說相高宗致中興矣，周公之篤棐王室，召公之保釐西土，其功業光映簡冊，歷萬年如一日，非爾多士所當致力者耶？
繼自今，列于有位，服在大僚，其必矢乃志，毋流于卑；一乃心，毋
translation_en:
…Those who respond to the times are human beings, and they must have the means to serve the needs of their age. You assembled scholars have advanced through your words; soon you will distinguish yourselves at the Ministry of Rites and behold the splendor of the imperial capital. Should you not also ponder the principle that words and deeds must accord with one another? Among the ancients were Yi Yin and Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao: natives of the Central Region, peers of the sages, and worthy predecessors to be emulated. Yi Yin took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. Fu Yue served as chief minister to Gaozong and brought about a restoration. The Duke of Zhou gave steadfast assistance to the royal house, and the Duke of Shao protected and governed the western lands. Their achievements shine in the historical records, remaining as bright through ten thousand years as on the first day. Are these not the accomplishments toward which you assembled scholars should direct your efforts?
From now on, when you take your places in office and serve in high posts, you must firmly set your resolve and not descend into baseness; make your hearts single in purpose, and do not…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
溢於貳澡浴其德而愼脩其
言與行俟有令圖用匹美於
前聞人庶無忝於秀靈無戾
於氣運無負於
聖人之神化是誠河洛之英而亦
殷周之才也已豈惟多士之
休主司亦有得人之慶焉否
===
則言於靜而庸或違昧自獻
之誠奭成身之信亦何貴于
科目爲哉書有云舉能其官
惟爾之能稱匪其人惟爾不
任則今日主司與爾多士交
相賛以有成者也〔怵〕不佞重
惟一日之雅故於終篇惓惓
punctuated: 溢於貳，澡浴其德，而愼脩其言與行，俟有令圖，用匹美於前聞人，庶無忝於秀靈，無戾於氣運，無負於聖人之神化。是誠河洛之英，而亦殷周之才也已。豈惟多士之休，主司亦有得人之慶焉。否則，言於靜而庸或違，昧自獻之誠，奭成身之信，亦何貴于科目爲哉？《書》有云：「舉能其官，惟爾之能；稱匪其人，惟爾不任。」則今日主司與爾多士交相賛以有成者也。〔怵〕不佞重惟一日之雅，故於終篇惓惓
translation_en:
…stray into divided purposes. Cleanse your virtue, and carefully cultivate your speech and conduct. Await the opportunity to put worthy plans into effect, thereby matching the excellence of the illustrious men of the past. Thus may you neither disgrace the spiritual gifts bestowed upon you, nor run counter to the course of the age, nor fail the sage emperor’s wondrous transforming influence. You will then truly be the outstanding men of the He and Luo region, and talents worthy of the Yin and Zhou dynasties. This would bring honor not only to you scholars: those presiding over the examination would also have cause to rejoice in having found worthy men.

Otherwise, if what you say in repose should conflict with what you do in practice, obscuring the sincerity of your dedication and compromising the good faith through which you perfect yourselves [?], what value would there be in examination distinctions? The Book of Documents says: “If those you recommend are capable of fulfilling their offices, that is your ability; if those you commend are not the right men, then you are unequal to your responsibility.” Thus those presiding over today’s examination and you scholars must assist one another in bringing this endeavor to fruition. 〔Apprehensive [?]〕 I, unworthy as I am, deeply cherish even this brief acquaintance; therefore, at the close of this piece, I earnestly…

title: 嘉靖二十八年河南鄉試錄
text:
焉無亦曰忠告善道之意也
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教
諭林〔烋〕謹序
punctuated:
焉，無亦曰忠告善道之意也。
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭林〔烋〕謹序。
translation_en:
…with earnest concern. Is this not simply an expression of the intent to offer loyal counsel and guide toward the good?
This preface is respectfully written by Lin Xiu 林烋, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuyi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang.
